beats.say: For area we need the side. The 4 equal sides add up to 132. How do we find one side?
132 divided by 4. Half of 132 is 66, and half of 66 is 33. So each side is 33 centimetres.
Area is side times side: 33 times 33. Split one 33 into 30 and 3.
33 times 30 is 990. And 33 times 3 is 99.
Add the two parts. 990 plus 99 makes 1089.

ask.ifNot: Look back at the question: the perimeter is in centimetres. So the little squares we count are square centimetres.

beats.say: Now be careful, because two of the choices say 1089! The side was in centimetres. So which unit does the area have?
So the area is 1089 square centimetres. Always read the unit as well as the number.
Check the side: 4 times 33 is 132. That is our perimeter.
For a square: divide the perimeter by 4 to get the side. Then side times side gives the area.
This one has three small jobs hidden inside. Find the greatest 2-digit prime. Find two even numbers after it. Then add them.

board.text: 7th + 11th even numbers after the greatest 2-digit prime

beats.say: A prime number has no factors except 1 and itself. Which is the greatest 2-digit prime?

ask.ifNot: 99 is 9 times 11, and 98 is even. So neither is prime. 97 has no factors like that.

beats.say: 99 is 9 times 11. 98 is even, so 2 goes into it. That makes 97 the greatest 2-digit prime.
The 1st even number after 97 is 98. The 2nd is 100. Each jump is 2.
From the 1st even number to the 7th, how many jumps of 2 do we make?

ask.ifNot: The 1st one needs no jump at all. So to reach the 7th we make 6 jumps.

beats.say: 6 jumps of 2 make 12, and 98 plus 12 is 110. So the 7th even number is 110.
For the 11th we make 10 jumps. 10 twos are 20, and 98 plus 20 is 118.
Now add the two numbers. 110 plus 118 is 228.
Look at the choices. 228 is not there! Don't bend your working to fit a choice. When your careful answer is not listed, pick none of these.

board.text: 228 is not listed: None of these

beats.say: Break a long question into small jobs and do them one at a time. And trust your careful working.
First we need the one-digit prime numbers. A prime number has exactly 2 factors: 1 and itself.

board.text: Greatest − smallest, using the one-digit primes once

beats.say: Which of these is the full list of one-digit primes?

ask.ifNot: 1 is not a prime, because it has only one factor. And 9 is 3 times 3. The one-digit primes are 2, 3, 5 and 7.

beats.say: So our digits are 2, 3, 5 and 7. Each is used once.
For the greatest number, put the biggest digit first and go down. That gives 7532.
For the smallest number, put the smallest digit first and go up. That gives 2357.
Now subtract 2357 from 7532. We have to borrow twice, in the ones and in the tens, so go slowly.
The difference is 5175.
Check by adding back: 5175 plus 2357 is 7532. It works.
Careful: 2357 is one of the choices, but that is only the smallest number. The question wants the difference.
Our series is 122, 117, 107, 92, 72, and then a letter A. A stands for the next number, and we must find it.
The numbers are getting smaller. Let's see how much they drop each time. The drops are 5, then 10, then 15, then 20.
The drops are not the same. So what is the next drop?

ask.ifNot: Look at the drops: 5, 10, 15, 20. Each drop is 5 bigger than the last. So after 20 comes 25.

beats.say: The drops grow by 5 each time, so the next drop is 25. This is the trap: don't just take away 20 again.
72 take away 25. First take away 20 to get 52. Then take away 5 more to get 47.
So A is 47.
Check the whole chain of drops: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. It grows steadily, so 47 fits.
When the jumps are not all the same, look at the jumps themselves. They often have a little pattern of their own.

board.text: Right triangle: base 19 cm, height 16 cm. Area = ?

spec.note: Area = ?

beats.say: A right triangle has a base of 19 centimetres and a height of 16 centimetres. We want its area.

spec.note: Two of the triangles make a rectangle

beats.say: In a right triangle the base and the height meet at the square corner. Put 2 of these triangles together and they make a rectangle, 19 by 16.

ask.ifNot: 19 times 16 is the whole rectangle. Our triangle is one of its 2 equal halves, so we take half.

beats.say: So what is the area of one triangle?
First 19 times 16. Here is a quick way: 20 times 16 is 320. That is one 16 too many, so take 16 away. 304.
Now half of 304. Half of 300 is 150, and half of 4 is 2. So half of 304 is 152.

ask.ifNot: Look back at the question. The sides are measured in centimetres, so the little squares that fill the triangle are square centimetres.

beats.say: Now the unit, and here is the trap. The sides are in centimetres. So the area is in...
152 square centimetres. One of the choices has the right number but says square metres. Always read the unit as well as the number.
So: half of base times height, and match the unit to the question.

board.text: Which pair can be 2 angles of an isosceles triangle?

beats.say: Here are 4 pairs of angles. One pair can belong to an isosceles triangle. Which one?

ask.ifNot: Each pair shows only 2 of the triangle's 3 angles. The third angle is not shown, and it might match one of the pair.

beats.say: An isosceles triangle has 2 equal angles. But no pair here shows 2 equal angles. So where could the twin be hiding?
So for each pair we find the third angle. The 3 angles of a triangle always add up to 180 degrees.
Pair A. 63 plus 54 is 117. And 180 minus 117 is 63.
The third angle is 63, and the pair already has a 63. 2 equal angles! This triangle is isosceles.
Let's make sure about the others. Pair B: 75 and 45 make 120, so the third angle is 60. It matches nothing.
Pair C: the third angle is 51. That is close to 49, but close is not equal. Pair D: the third angle is 68. No match.
So the pair is 63 degrees and 54 degrees.
Whenever you see 2 angles of a triangle, find the third one. It often holds the surprise.

board.text: Circumference and area of a circle: same number

spec.note: Circumference and area are the same number

beats.say: The circumference and the area of a circle are the same number. We want the diameter.
Write the two rules. Circumference is 2 times pi times r. Area is pi times r times r.
They are equal. Pi times r times 2 on one side, pi times r times r on the other. Both sides have pi times r.

ask.ifNot: On the left, after covering pi times r, the 2 is left. On the right, one r is left.

beats.say: Cover up the pi times r on both sides. What is left on each side?
A 2 is left on one side and an r on the other. So r must be 2. The radius is 2 centimetres.
Careful! Is 2 our answer? Read the question again. It asks for the diameter, not the radius.
The diameter is twice the radius. 2 times 2 is 4.
The diameter is 4 centimetres.
Check: with radius 2, the circumference is 2 times 2 lots of pi, and the area is 2 times 2 lots of pi. Both are 4 lots of pi.
Here is a sum with three decimals. We add the first two, then take away the third.
Two of these numbers have four digits after the point. Which one does not?

ask.ifNot: Count the digits after each point. 17.005 has only three, so it is one short.

beats.say: So we give 17.005 one more zero. Careful: the zero goes at the very end, so the 5 stays in the thousandths place.
Now add the first two. From the right: 2 and 0 is 2. 1 and 5 is 6. 2 and 0 is 2. 1 and 0 is 1.
And the wholes: 12 and 17 make 29. So far we have 29.1262.
What do we do with the 9.1102?

ask.ifNot: Look at the sign in front of 9.1102. It is a minus, so we take it away from the total we have so far.

beats.say: From the right: 2 take away 2 is 0. 6 take away 0 is 6. 2 take away 1 is 1. 1 take away 1 is 0.
And the wholes: 29 take away 9 is 20. That gives 20.0160.
So the answer is 20.0160. Notice where the 6 sits: in the thousandths place, just where the columns put it.
A quick check with the wholes only: 12 plus 17 take away 9 is 20, and our answer is just over 20. Line up the points, fill gaps with zeros, and go one column at a time.
We must multiply 588 by the least number that makes a perfect square. The secret is in its prime factors.

spec.note: Break 588 into prime factors

beats.say: Break 588 down. 588 is 2 times 294, and 294 is 2 times 147.
147 is 3 times 49, and 49 is 7 times 7. So 588 is 2 times 2 times 3 times 7 times 7.
In a perfect square every factor has a partner. The 2s make a pair and the 7s make a pair. Which factor is alone?

ask.ifNot: There are two 2s and two 7s, so they pair up. There is only one 3, so it is alone.

beats.say: The 3 is alone. So we multiply by 3 to give it a partner.
Check: 1764 is 42 times 42. A perfect square.
So the least number is 3. Now look at the choices: 2, 6 and 4. There is no 3!
Here is the trap. When your answer is not in the list, do not bend it to fit. The answer is None of these.
A quick check of the others: multiplying by 2, 4 or 6 still leaves a factor without a partner.
We have two facts. 8 P, plus 7, equals 39. And Q equals P plus 3. We must find 2 P, plus 3 Q.
That is three small jobs. Find P. Then find Q. Then work out the last sum. Which fact lets us find P straight away?

ask.ifNot: Q equals P plus 3 has two letters we do not know yet. But the other fact has only P in it, so we start there.

beats.say: Take 7 from both sides. 39 minus 7 is 32. So 8 P equals 32.
Divide both sides by 8. 8 times 4 is 32, so P equals 4.
Now Q. Q is 3 more than P, so Q is 4 plus 3, which is 7.
Now the last job: 2 P, plus 3 Q. Which sum is that?

ask.ifNot: The 2 goes with P, and P is 4. The 3 goes with Q, and Q is 7. So it is 2 times 4, plus 3 times 7.

beats.say: 2 times 4 is 8. And 3 times 7 is 21.
8 plus 21 is 29. So 2 P, plus 3 Q, equals 29.
Careful not to swap the 2 and the 3, and not to stop at 21. Do each job in order, and the last sum is easy.
There are two jobs here. First we put five decimals in descending order. Then we add the 1st and the 4th.
The numbers have different lengths, and that can fool us. So we give every one four digits after the point.
Descending means biggest first. Which number is the biggest?

ask.ifNot: 0.219 is the only one with a digit in the tenths place: it has 2 tenths. All the others have 0 tenths. So it is the biggest, even though 0.0075 has more digits.

beats.say: Now read the parts after the point as whole numbers. 2190 is first. Then come 820, then 700, then 80, and last of all 75.
Count along our ordered line. Which number is 4th?

ask.ifNot: Count them off: 0.219 is 1st, 0.082 is 2nd, 0.07 is 3rd, and 0.008 is 4th. 0.0075 is the smallest, so it comes last.

beats.say: That is the trap. 0.0075 has the most digits, but 80 beats 75, so 0.008 is bigger. The 1st is 0.219 and the 4th is 0.008.
Now add them with the points in line. 219 thousandths and 8 thousandths make 227 thousandths.
So the sum of the 1st and the 4th is 0.227.
When decimals have different lengths, write them all with the same number of places before you compare. Then nothing can hide.
Half a dozen bananas cost 30 rupees. We want to know how many bananas 85 rupees will buy.

board.text: Half a dozen bananas cost 30 rupees

beats.say: First, how many bananas is half a dozen?

ask.ifNot: A dozen is 12, and half of 12 is 6. So half a dozen is 6 bananas.

beats.say: A dozen is 12, so half a dozen is 6. That means 6 bananas cost 30 rupees.
Now find the price of one banana. Share 30 rupees among 6 bananas. 30 divided by 6 is 5.
So one banana costs 5 rupees. How do we find how many bananas 85 rupees buys?

ask.ifNot: Each banana uses up 5 rupees. So we count how many fives there are in 85. That is 85 divided by 5.

beats.say: 85 divided by 5. Split 85 into 50 and 35. 50 is 10 fives, and 35 is 7 fives.
10 fives and 7 fives make 17 fives. So 85 rupees buys 17 bananas.
Check by multiplying back. 17 bananas at 5 rupees each cost 85 rupees. It fits.
So: find the price of one first. Then divide the money by that price.
It is 4:30 p.m. on the 15th of April. Then the minute hand turns 30 times. What are the date and time now?

board.text: 4:30 pm, 15th April. Minute hand turns 30 times.

spec.note: 4:30 pm on 15th April. The minute hand then turns 30 times

beats.say: How long does the minute hand take to go once round the clock?

ask.ifNot: The long minute hand goes all the way round once every hour. The hand that takes 12 hours is the short hour hand.

beats.say: One turn is 1 hour. So 30 turns is 30 hours.
30 hours is more than a day. A day has 24 hours, and 30 minus 24 leaves 6. So it is 1 day and 6 hours.
Add the full day first. 24 hours after 4:30 p.m. on the 15th is 4:30 p.m. on the 16th. Same time, next day.
Now add the 6 hours. What is 6 hours after 4:30 p.m.?

ask.ifNot: Count on 6 hours from 4:30: 5:30, 6:30, 7:30, 8:30, 9:30, 10:30. It is still evening, so it is 10:30 p.m.

beats.say: 6 hours after 4:30 p.m. is 10:30 p.m., and it is still the 16th of April.
Notice the minutes never changed. After whole turns, the minute hand is back where it started.
So: turns of the minute hand are hours. Take out the full days, then add the hours that are left.
A five-digit number: 3, A, A, 4, 8. Both A's are the same digit. We want the greatest digit for A that lets 12 divide the number.
12 is 3 times 4. So the number must pass two tests: the test for 3, and the test for 4.
Test for 4: look only at the last two digits, 48. 48 divided by 4 is 12, with nothing left over. So this test is passed, whatever A is.
Test for 3: the digits must add up to a number in the 3 times table. The digits we know are 3, 4 and 8. They add up to 15.
A is there twice. We want the greatest digit, so try 9 first. 15 plus 9 plus 9 is 33. Is 33 in the 3 times table?

ask.ifNot: 3 times 11 is 33. So 33 is in the 3 times table.

beats.say: 33 is 3 times 11, so A equals 9 works. No digit is bigger than 9, so we are done. The number is 39,948.
Here is the trap. 3 works as well, because 15 plus 3 plus 3 is 21. But the question asks for the greatest digit, so always start from the top.
So for 12, use two tests: the last two digits for 4, and the digit sum for 3.
A square of numbers. Each column follows the same rule, going down. We must find Z, in the middle of the third column.

board.text: Each column follows the same rule.  Z = ?

spec.note: Each column follows the same rule. Z = ?

beats.say: The first column is 7, 3 and 16. The second is 13, 6 and 49. Which rule works for both columns?

ask.ifNot: 7 take away 3 is 4, and 4 times 4 is 16. 13 take away 6 is 7, and 7 times 7 is 49. That rule fits both columns.

beats.say: 7 take away 3 is 4, and 4 times 4 is 16. 13 take away 6 is 7, and 7 times 7 is 49. The rule fits both.
The third column is 24, then Z, then 169. This time we know the bottom number and not the middle. So we work backwards.
Which number, multiplied by itself, makes 169?

ask.ifNot: Try 13. 13 times 13 is 169.

beats.say: 13 times 13 is 169. So 24 take away Z must be 13.
Careful: 13 is not Z. Z is what we take from 24 to leave 13. 24 take away 13 is 11.
Check the whole column. 24 take away 11 is 13, and 13 times 13 is 169. So Z is 11.
When the gap is in the middle of a rule, find the rule from the full columns, then run it backwards.
Two years, written in Roman numerals. To find how long the company ran, we turn both into our numbers, subtract, and turn the answer back.

board.text: Began MCDXLIX, closed MDCLXV. How long?

beats.say: The starting year, part by part: M is 1000, C D is 400, X L is 40 and I X is 9. That makes 1449.

spec.note: The starting year, part by part

beats.say: The closing year starts M, then D C. D is 500 and C is 100. What is D C worth?

ask.ifNot: Here the bigger letter D comes first, so we add: 500 and 100 make 600. Only C D, the other way round, is 400.

beats.say: This is the trap in this question. C D is 400, but D C is 600. The order of the letters changes everything.
So the closing year is 1000, 600, 60 and 5. That makes 1665.
Now subtract. 1665 minus 1449 is 216 years.
Back to Roman. 216 is 200, 10 and 6. That is C C, then X, then V I.
So the plan: read each numeral in parts, do the sum in our own numbers, then write the answer in Roman letters.
Our series starts 13, 15, 18, 23, 30, 41. We want the 12th term. First, the rule.
Look at the jumps between neighbours. They are 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11.
Those jumps belong to a famous family of numbers. Which one?

ask.ifNot: They are not the odd numbers, because 2 is there and 9 is missing. 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 are the prime numbers in order.

beats.say: So each jump is the next prime. Now the trap: to go from the 1st term to the 12th we make 11 jumps, not 12.
So we need the first 11 primes. After 11 come 13, 17, 19, 23, 29 and 31.
Let's add them in friendly groups. The first five make 28. Then 13 and 17 make 30.
19 and 23 make 42. 29 and 31 make 60. All together, 28 plus 30 plus 42 plus 60 is 160.
The 11 jumps add up to 160. Where do we add them on?

ask.ifNot: All 11 jumps were counted from the very start. So they are added to the 1st term, 13.

beats.say: 13 plus 160 is 173. So the 12th term is 173.
When jumps look strange, ask which family they belong to. And remember: reaching the 12th term takes only 11 jumps.
We have 11 kilograms and 11 grams. We want to write it as one decimal number of kilograms.
The 11 kilograms stay as they are. It is the 11 grams we must change. A gram is what part of a kilogram?

ask.ifNot: Kilo means a thousand. So 1 gram is one thousandth of a kilogram.

beats.say: 1000 grams make 1 kilogram. So we divide the grams by 1000.
11 divided by 1000 is 0.011. Thousandths take 3 places after the point, so a 0 stands in front of the 11.
Here is the trap. 0.11 kilograms would be 110 grams, far more than our 11 grams.
Now join it to the 11 whole kilograms. 11 plus 0.011 is 11.011.
So the weight is 11.011 kilograms.
Remember: grams to kilograms means 3 decimal places. Fill the empty place with a 0.
We must find the one statement that is completely true. So we test each one in turn. No guessing.
First: is 240 divided by 16 more than 16? Think in times. 16 times 10 is 160, and 16 times 5 is 80. Together, 240.
So 240 divided by 16 is 15. And 15 is less than 16, not more. This one is not true.
Second: is 18 plus 18 divided by 2 equal to 18? Which bit goes first here?

ask.ifNot: Divide goes before plus. So 18 divided by 2 comes first.

beats.say: 18 divided by 2 is 9, and 18 plus 9 is 27, not 18. So this one is not true either.
Now the long one. Left side first. 17 times 10 is 170, and 17 times 7 is 119. So 17 times 17 is 289.
Add the 18. 289 plus 18 is 307. So the left side is 307.
Right side. 16 times 16 is 256, and 17 times 3 is 51.
256 plus 51 is 307. The right side is 307 too!
Both sides are 307, so this statement is the true one.
The trap: a statement can look right at a glance. Work out both sides fully before you believe it.

board.text: 8 circles in a rectangle: 2 rows of 4

spec.note: One circle fits in each square. Radius = 7 cm. Area = ?

beats.say: Eight equal circles sit inside a rectangle in 2 rows of 4, touching each other and the sides. Each radius is 7 centimetres. What is the area of the rectangle?

ask.ifNot: 7 centimetres only reaches from the centre to the edge. From edge to edge is the diameter, which is two radii.

beats.say: The circles fill the rectangle from side to side. So how much room does one whole circle take up, from edge to edge?

spec.note: The diameter is twice the radius

beats.say: That's the trap: use the diameter, not the radius. 2 times 7 is 14 centimetres.

spec.note: The length holds 4 circles side by side

beats.say: 4 circles fit along the length. 4 times 14 is 56 centimetres.

spec.note: The breadth holds 2 circles

beats.say: 2 circles fit up the side. 2 times 14 is 28 centimetres.
Area is length times breadth: 56 times 28. Split 28 into 20 and 8.
56 times 20 is 1120. 56 times 8 is 448.
Add the parts: 1120 plus 448 makes 1568.
The area of the rectangle is 1568 square centimetres.
So: radius to diameter, count the circles each way to get the sides, then multiply.
We need the difference between the L C M and the H C F of 16 and 36. That is three jobs: find the H C F, find the L C M, then subtract.
Start by breaking each number into prime factors, the building blocks it is made of.
Take 16. It is made only of 2s: 2 times 2 times 2 times 2.
Take 36. Keep pulling out the smallest prime that fits: 2 twice, then 3, and 3 is left. So 36 is 2 times 2 times 3 times 3.
First the H C F. It is built only from the primes that both numbers have. Which of these is exactly what 16 and 36 share?

ask.ifNot: Look for the primes that sit on both lines. A prime that only one number has cannot divide the other one, so it stays out.

beats.say: Both lines have two 2s. 2 times 2 is 4, so the H C F is 4.
Next the L C M. Both 16 and 36 must fit inside it. So each prime goes in the most times it appears in one number: four 2s and two 3s. Multiplied together, that is 144.
A quick check on the L C M. 144 divided by 16 is 9, and 144 divided by 36 is 4. Both are exact.
We have the H C F, 4, and the L C M, 144. Now the last job. What do we work out to finish?

ask.ifNot: Difference means subtract. And it is the L C M and the H C F that we subtract, not the two numbers we started with.

beats.say: 144 minus 4 is 140. That is our answer.
Read the last word of the question with care: difference means subtract. And do finish the last step. The L C M on its own is not the answer.
3 years ago, the ages of Nirav and Vipul added up to 38. Vipul is 2 years younger than Nirav. We want Vipul's age after 2 years.

board.text: Vipul is 2 years younger than Nirav

beats.say: First bring the sum to today. 3 years ago they added up to 38. What do their ages add up to now?

ask.ifNot: Nirav is 3 years older now, and Vipul is 3 years older too. So add 3 twice.

beats.say: 38 plus 3 plus 3 is 44. Two people, so the 3 is added twice.
Now we split the 44 between them. Look at the bars. Nirav's bar is the same as Vipul's bar, plus 2 extra years.
Take away Nirav's 2 extra years. 44 minus 2 is 42. Now we have two equal bars.
Half of 42 is 21. So Vipul is 21 years old now.
The question asks for Vipul's age after 2 years. So what do we do?

ask.ifNot: After means going forward in time. Vipul will be 2 years older than he is now.

beats.say: 21 plus 2 is 23. So after 2 years Vipul will be 23 years old.
Check today's ages. Vipul is 21, so Nirav is 2 more, which is 23. And 21 plus 23 is 44. It fits.
So: bring the sum to today, take away the extra years, halve, and then move to the time the question asks about.
A four-digit number: 9, star, 3, star. Both stars are the same digit, and 11 divides the number exactly. Which digit is the star?

spec.note: Both stars are the same digit.

beats.say: Here is the test for 11. Add the 1st and 3rd digits. Then add the 2nd and 4th digits. The two sums must be equal, or differ by 11.

board.text: Test for 11: two sums equal, or differ by 11

beats.say: The 1st and 3rd digits are 9 and 3. They add up to 12.
The two stars are the 2nd and 4th digits. For the two sums to be equal, what must the two stars add up to?

ask.ifNot: The two sums must match. The first sum is 12, so the two stars must add up to 12 as well.

beats.say: Two equal digits that add up to 12: each one is 6. So the star is 6.
Let's check. The number is 9636, and 11 times 876 is 9636. It works.
Now look at the choices: 4, 5, 7, or none of these. Which one do we pick?

ask.ifNot: Our digit is 6. It is not 4, 5 or 7, so the right choice is none of these.

beats.say: 6 is not in the list, so the answer is none of these. Do not let that shake you. When your working checks out, trust it.
The letter Q stands for the greatest two-digit number. We must write the smallest two-digit prime using Q.
First, what is the greatest two-digit number?

ask.ifNot: 100 has three digits. The biggest number with just two digits is 99.

beats.say: So Q is 99.
Now the smallest two-digit prime. The smallest two-digit number is 10, but 10 is 2 times 5, so it is not prime. Next comes 11. Its only factors are 1 and 11, so 11 is prime.
What must we take away from 99 to leave 11?

ask.ifNot: 99 take away 11 is 88. So taking 88 away from 99 leaves 11.

beats.say: 99 minus 88 is 11. So the smallest two-digit prime is Q minus 88.
The trap is Q minus 89. That gives 10, the smallest two-digit number. But 10 is not prime.
a is 3 and b is 6. We have four expressions, and we want the one with the least value. Least means smallest. So we find the value of every one.
First, 4 a minus b. 4 times 3 is 12, and 12 minus 6 is 6.
Next, 5 b minus 7 a. 5 times 6 is 30. 7 times 3 is 21. And 30 minus 21 is 9.
Your turn. What is 3 b minus 5 a?

ask.ifNot: 3 b means 3 times 6. 5 a means 5 times 3. Work out each one, then take the second from the first.

beats.say: 3 times 6 is 18. 5 times 3 is 15. And 18 minus 15 is 3.
Last one, 7 a minus 2 b. 7 times 3 is 21. 2 times 6 is 12. And 21 minus 12 is 9.
Now compare the four values: 6, 9, 3 and 9. The smallest is 3.
That 3 came from 3 b minus 5 a. So that one has the least value.
When you are asked for the least or the greatest, do not guess from the look. Work out every one, then compare. Here the least is 3 b minus 5 a.
4 mangoes give 250 millilitres of juice. We want enough juice to make 1 decalitre. How many mangoes is that?
First, that unusual word. What do you think deca means?

ask.ifNot: Deca means ten, as in a decade, which is ten years. Deci, with an i, is the one that means a tenth.

beats.say: So 1 decalitre is 10 litres. Each litre is 1000 millilitres, so that is 10000 millilitres.
Now, how many lots of 250 fit in 10000? Start small: 4 lots of 250 make 1000, which is 1 litre.
We have 10 litres, so that is 10 times 4 lots. 40 lots of 250 millilitres.
Careful now. 40 is the number of lots, and it is one of the choices. But how many mangoes does each lot need?

ask.ifNot: Go back to the start of the question. It takes 4 mangoes to make each 250 millilitres.

beats.say: Each lot needs 4 mangoes. 40 times 4 is 160. So we need 160 mangoes.
The plan: change to the same unit, count the lots, then multiply by the mangoes in each lot.
A mystery number, divided by 8, gives 12 with nothing left over. Then the same number is divided by 3. What do we get?
First we must find the mystery number. How?

ask.ifNot: Dividing by 8 gave 12. To go back, we do the opposite of dividing, which is multiplying. 8 times 12.

beats.say: Times undoes divide. So the number is 8 times 12. 8 times 10 is 80, and 8 times 2 is 16. Together, 96.
The mystery number is 96. Now we divide 96 by 3.
Split 96 into 90 and 6. 90 divided by 3 is 30, and 6 divided by 3 is 2.
30 and 2 make 32. So the new quotient, the answer to the division, is 32.
Check by multiplying back. 3 times 32 is 96. It fits.
Careful with the trap. Do not just mix up the 8, the 12 and the 3. Find the mystery number first, and then divide it.

board.text: Two sides: 20 cm and 15 cm. Which CANNOT be the perimeter?

spec.note: The third side is not given

beats.say: 2 sides of a triangle are 20 centimetres and 15 centimetres. One of these 4 perimeters is impossible. Which?
Imagine 2 sticks, 20 and 15 centimetres long, joined at one end like a hinge. The third side has to close the gap between their free ends.

ask.ifNot: When the 2 sticks lie end to end in a straight line, the distance is both lengths together: 20 plus 15.

beats.say: Open the hinge wider and wider, until the 2 sticks lie in one straight line. How far apart are the free ends then?

board.text: Third side is shorter than 35 cm

beats.say: 35 centimetres. But a straight line is not a triangle! So the third side must be shorter than 35. That is the key idea.
The perimeter is all 3 sides: 35, plus the third side. The third side is less than 35, so the perimeter is less than 35 plus 35, which is 70.

ask.ifNot: The perimeter must be less than 70. Only one of the 4 is bigger than 70.

beats.say: So which of the 4 perimeters is impossible?
72. Check it: 72 minus 35 leaves 37 for the third side. But 37 is longer than both sticks put together, so they could never reach across.
The others are fine. Take 67: 67 minus 35 is 32, and 32 is shorter than 35.
So the perimeter cannot be 72 centimetres.
Remember the hinge. In any triangle, 2 sides together are always longer than the third. If not, they cannot meet.
We start at 12:00 a.m., midnight, on the 2nd of March 2023. What are the date and time 2023 minutes later?
First change the minutes into hours. 60 minutes make an hour, so we ask how many 60s fit into 2023.
30 times 60 is 1800. 3 more 60s are 180. So 33 times 60 is 1980, and that is as close as we can get.
2023 minus 1980 leaves 43. So 2023 minutes is 33 hours and 43 minutes.
33 hours is more than one day. How do we split it?

ask.ifNot: A day has 24 hours. 33 minus 24 is 9. So 33 hours is 1 day and 9 hours.

beats.say: 33 minus 24 is 9. One full day after midnight on the 2nd of March is midnight on the 3rd of March.
Now add the 9 hours and 43 minutes to midnight. That takes us to 9:43 in the morning.
9 hours after midnight is still morning, so it is a.m., and the date has moved on by just one day.
So: minutes to hours, take out the full day, then add what is left.
W is a mystery number. We are told that W plus 9 is odd, and we want the 48th even number after it.
If W plus 9 is odd, what kind of number is the very next one, W plus 10?

ask.ifNot: Odd and even numbers take turns. Straight after an odd number comes an even one.

beats.say: So W plus 10 is the 1st even number after it. The 2nd is W plus 12. Each jump is 2.
From the 1st even number to the 48th, how many jumps of 2 do we make?

ask.ifNot: The 1st one needs no jump. From the 1st to the 2nd is 1 jump, to the 3rd is 2 jumps. So to the 48th it is 47.

beats.say: This is the trap. W plus 10 is already the 1st, so we make only 47 jumps. 47 twos are 94.
We started at W plus 10 and moved 94 further on. 10 plus 94 is 104.
So the 48th even number is W plus 104.
Quick check. W plus 10 is even, and we added 94, which is even. Even plus even stays even. Good.
Even with a letter in it, the idea is the same. Find the 1st one, count 1 fewer jump than the place number, and step on.
We need to write 2349 the Roman way. Romans had no place seats like ours, so first we break the number into parts.
Split it by place: 2000, 300, 40 and 9.
Here are the 7 Roman letters and what each one is worth. Keep them in view.

spec.note: and V = 5, I = 1

beats.say: 2000 is 2 lots of 1000, so we write M M. 300 is 3 lots of 100, so we write C C C.
Now the 40. How do the Romans write 40?

ask.ifNot: X before L means 10 less than 50, which is 40. And a letter is never written 4 times in a row.

beats.say: 40 is 10 less than 50, so the smaller letter goes in front: X L.
9 is 1 less than 10, so the smaller letter goes in front: I X.
Now join the parts in order, biggest first: M M, C C C, X L, I X.
And notice the 300. It is simply three Cs. The take away trick is only for the 4s and the 9s.
So the plan for any number: split it by place, write each part in Roman letters, then join them from left to right.
We need the sum of the L C M and the H C F of 65 and 91. That is three jobs: find the H C F, find the L C M, then add them.
Start by breaking each number into prime factors, the building blocks it is made of.
65 is odd, and 3 will not go in. But it ends in 5, so 5 does. That leaves 13, so 65 is 5 times 13.
2, 3 and 5 will not go into 91. Try 7 next, and 7 does go in. That leaves 13, so 91 is 7 times 13.
First the H C F. It is built only from the primes that both numbers have. Which of these is exactly what 65 and 91 share?

ask.ifNot: Look for the primes that sit on both lines. A prime that only one number has cannot divide the other one, so it stays out.

beats.say: Both lines have a 13, and nothing else in common. So the H C F is 13.
Next the L C M. Both 65 and 91 must fit inside it. So each prime goes in the most times it appears in one number: one 5, one 7 and one 13. Multiplied together, that is 455.
A quick check on the L C M. 455 divided by 65 is 7, and 455 divided by 91 is 5. Both are exact.
We have the H C F, 13, and the L C M, 455. Now the last job. What do we work out to finish?

ask.ifNot: Sum means add. And it is the L C M and the H C F that we add, not the two numbers we started with.

beats.say: 455 plus 13 is 468. That is our answer.
Read the question with care: sum means add, difference means subtract. And do finish the last step. The L C M on its own is not the answer.
Mishti has 97 pens and Manav has 11. Mishti gives some pens to Manav. After that, she has twice as many as he has.
When Mishti gives pens to Manav, what happens to the total number of pens?

ask.ifNot: No pens are lost, and no new pens appear. They only move from one child to the other. So the total stays the same.

beats.say: So let's find the total. 97 plus 11 is 108.
At the end Mishti has twice as many as Manav. So Manav has 1 share and Mishti has 2 shares. That is 3 equal shares.
3 equal shares make 108 pens. How do we find one share?

ask.ifNot: Mishti's 2 shares and Manav's 1 share make 3 shares in all. So we divide 108 by 3, not by 2.

beats.say: 108 divided by 3. 3 times 30 is 90, and 3 times 6 is 18. So one share is 36.
So Manav ends with 36 pens. He started with 11. The pens he gained are the pens Mishti gave.
36 minus 11 is 25. So Mishti gave 25 pens.
Let's check. Mishti is left with 97 minus 25, which is 72. And 72 is twice 36. It works!
So when things only move from one person to another, the total stays the same. Use the total to find the shares.
A 3-digit number ending in 6 is multiplied by a 2-digit number ending in 9. The stars hide the other digits. Which choice can be the product?
We can't see the hidden digits. But we can still work out the last digit of the product. What is it?

ask.ifNot: The last digit of a product comes only from the last digits of the two numbers. 6 times 9 is 54, so the product ends in 4.

beats.say: 6 times 9 is 54, so the product must end in 4. But look: all four choices end in 4! So we need another test.
So let's test the size. What are the smallest numbers that fit: a 3-digit number ending in 6 and a 2-digit number ending in 9?

ask.ifNot: The first digit must be at least 1, and a middle digit can be 0. So the smallest are 106 and 19.

beats.say: The smallest numbers that fit are 106 and 19. Their product is 2014. So 1854 is too small.
The largest numbers that fit are 996 and 99. Their product is 98604. So 986004 is too big.
Two choices are still standing: 51684 and 40548. This is the hard part. The product must divide exactly by a 2-digit number ending in 9.
Here is 40548 divided by each of them. Every time something is left over. So 40548 cannot be made.

spec.note: 40548 never divides exactly

beats.say: Only one choice is left: 51684. It ends in 4, and it is the right size.
And this one really can be made: 876 times 59 is exactly 51684.
Most hidden-digit puzzles fall to the last digit and the size. When two choices are still standing, test whether each one can really be made.
Start with 48 degrees. We need its complementary angle and its supplementary angle, and then the sum of those two.

ask.ifNot: A square corner is a right angle, a quarter turn. That is 90 degrees. 180 is for a straight line.

beats.say: First the complement. Complementary angles fit together into a square corner. How much do they make together?
So the complement is 90 take away 48. 90 take away 40 is 50, and 8 more away leaves 42.

ask.ifNot: The two angles on the line make 180 together. So take 48 away from 180.

beats.say: Now the supplement. Supplementary angles sit together on a straight line, and a straight line is 180 degrees. Which sum gives the supplement?
180 take away 48. Here is a quick way: 180 is 90 more than 90, so the supplement is 90 more than the complement. 42 and 90 make 132.
Careful now. The question wants the sum of the two partners. Not the angle itself. Just the complement and the supplement.
42 plus 132. The tens first: 40 and 130 make 170. Then the ones: 2 and 2 make 4. Altogether, 174.
So the sum is 174 degrees.
So the plan is: take the angle from 90, take the angle from 180, and add the two answers.
One gross of notebooks costs 2592 rupees. We need the cost of 68 notebooks.
A gross is 12 dozen. How many notebooks is that?

ask.ifNot: 12 dozen is 12 lots of 12. And 12 times 12 is 144.

beats.say: 12 dozen is 12 times 12, which is 144. So 144 notebooks cost 2592 rupees.
Next we want the cost of one notebook. That is 2592 divided by 144. Think in times: 144 times what makes 2592?
Try 20, because it is easy. 144 times 2 is 288, so 144 times 20 is 2880. That is too big.
How much too big? 2880 take away 2592 is 288. And 288 is exactly 2 lots of 144. So we need 2 lots fewer than 20.
20 take away 2 is 18. So one notebook costs 18 rupees.
Now, 68 notebooks at 18 rupees each. Which sum do we need?

ask.ifNot: Each of the 68 notebooks costs 18 rupees. So we need 68 lots of 18.

beats.say: Use the same trick. 18 is 20 take away 2. 68 times 2 is 136, so 68 times 20 is 1360.
That is 2 lots of 68 too many, so take away 136. 1360 take away 136 is 1224.
So 68 notebooks cost 1224 rupees.
The key idea: do not jump straight from a gross to 68. Find the cost of one notebook first, then multiply.
We know that 3 x, plus 7, equals 38. We must find 6 x, plus 7.
Here is a secret: we do not need x itself. Look at 6 x and 3 x. How are they related?

ask.ifNot: 6 is 2 times 3. So 6 x is 2 lots of 3 x. It is double.

beats.say: So first let's find 3 x. Take 7 from both sides. 38 minus 7 is 31. So 3 x equals 31.
Now double it. 6 x is 2 times 31, which is 62.
We want 6 x, plus 7. What do we add to 62?

ask.ifNot: Only the 3 x part was doubled. The plus 7 in 6 x plus 7 is a plain 7, so we add 7 just once.

beats.say: 62 plus 7 is 69. So 6 x, plus 7, equals 69.
Here is the trap. Doubling the whole of 38 gives 76. But that doubles the 7 as well, and we only want one 7.
Now look at the choices. 69 is not there! So the answer is: none of these.

board.text: 69 is not listed: none of these

beats.say: So look for a shortcut before solving. And if your checked answer is not listed, choose none of these.

board.text: Square and equilateral triangle: same perimeter
Triangle side = 12 cm. Area of square = ?

spec.note: A square has the same perimeter. Area of the square = ?

beats.say: A square and an equilateral triangle have the same perimeter. Each side of the triangle is 12 centimetres. We want the area of the square.

spec.note: Perimeter = 3 × 12 cm

beats.say: Start with the shape we know. An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides. So its perimeter is 3 times 12, which is 36.

ask.ifNot: 12 centimetres is the triangle's side. The square shares the same 36 centimetres among 4 sides, so its sides are shorter.

beats.say: The square has the same perimeter, 36 centimetres. How long is each side of the square?

spec.note: Same perimeter, shared among 4 equal sides

beats.say: 36 shared among 4 equal sides is 9. So the square's side is 9 centimetres, not 12.
Now the area. Side times side: 9 times 9 is 81.
So the area of the square is 81 square centimetres.
Check: 4 sides of 9 make 36, the same as the triangle. Good.
The trap was using 12 for the square. Same perimeter does not mean same side!
Something is added to 3 over 8, and the total is 8 over 3. What is that something?
We know the total and one part. How do we find the other part?

ask.ifNot: The total is 8 over 3 and one part is 3 over 8. To find the other part, we take the part away from the total.

beats.say: So we need 8 over 3, take away 3 over 8. Thirds and eighths are different pieces. Both 3 and 8 go into 24, so we use twenty-fourths.
For 8 over 3, the bottom is multiplied by 8, so the top is too. 8 times 8 is 64.
For 3 over 8, the bottom is multiplied by 3, so the top is too. 3 times 3 is 9.
Now both are twenty-fourths, so we work with the tops. What is 64 take away 9?

ask.ifNot: Count back 9 from 64 carefully. Then check by adding: 55 plus 9 should give 64 again.

beats.say: 64 take away 9 is 55. So the number to add is 55 over 24.
Check it. 9 over 24, plus 55 over 24, is 64 over 24. And that is 8 over 3. It works.
So to find what must be added: take the part away from the total. And match the bottoms first.
The same number, M, sits on top of three fractions. Together they make 162 over 126. What is M?
Here is the tricky part. The left side is in fourteenths, but the right side has 126 below. So first: 126 is 14 times what?

ask.ifNot: Check by multiplying. 14 times 9 is 126. The other choices do not reach 126.

beats.say: 14 times 9 is 126. So we divide the top and bottom of 162 over 126 by 9. That gives 18 over 14.
Now both sides are in fourteenths. So the three tops on the left must add up to 18.
Three equal numbers add up to 18. What is each one?

ask.ifNot: Share 18 equally among the 3 fractions. 18 divided by 3 is 6.

beats.say: 18 divided by 3 is 6. So M is 6.
Check it. 6 over 14, three times, is 18 over 14. And 18 over 14 is the same as 162 over 126.
So when the two sides have different bottoms, change one side first. Then compare the tops.
Our series starts 24, 41, 58, 75, 92, and keeps going. We want the 28th term. That is a long way along!
First find the jump. 41 minus 24 is 17, and 58 minus 41 is 17 too. So each term is 17 more than the one before.
We could keep going one step at a time, but that is slow. From the 1st term to the 28th, how many jumps do we make?

ask.ifNot: From the 1st to the 2nd is 1 jump. From the 1st to the 3rd is 2 jumps. The jumps are always 1 fewer than the place number.

beats.say: Careful, this is the trap. The 1st term is there before any jump. So we make 1 fewer jump than 28. That is 27 jumps.
27 jumps of 17 is a big sum, so split it. 20 times 17 is 340, and 7 times 17 is 119.
340 plus 119 makes 459. So 27 jumps of 17 cover 459.
The jumps cover 459. What do we do with the 459?

ask.ifNot: The jumps start at the 1st term, which is 24. So the 459 is added on to 24.

beats.say: 24 plus 459 is 483. So the 28th term is 483.
Test the idea on the 5th term, which we can see. 4 jumps of 17 make 68, and 24 plus 68 is 92. It matches.
For a term far along: find the jump, make 1 fewer jump than the term number, multiply, then add the 1st term.
Three decimals in a chain. All of them have four digits after the point, so they already line up. We work from left to right: subtract first, then add.
Start the subtraction from the right. 3 take away 1 is 2. The next column is 2 take away 4. Can we do that straight away?

ask.ifNot: 2 is smaller than 4, so we cannot take 4 away yet. And we must never swap the digits. We borrow 1 from the next place.

beats.say: We borrow 1 from the next place, so the 2 becomes 12. And 12 take away 4 is 8. The place we borrowed from had 3, so now it has 2. And 2 take away 1 is 1.
The tenths are 2 take away 4 again. Borrow from the ones: 12 take away 4 is 8. Now the ones have only 2 left, so 2 take away 4 needs one more borrow. Again 12 take away 4 is 8.
The tens had 2 and lent 1, so 1 is left, and 1 take away 1 is 0. So the subtraction gives 8.8182. Check by adding back: 8.8182 plus 14.4141 is 23.2323. Good.
Now, what do we do with the 13.0423?

ask.ifNot: Look at the sign in front of 13.0423. It is a plus, so we add it to what we have so far.

beats.say: From the right: 2 and 3 is 5. 8 and 2 is 10, so write 0 and carry 1. 1 and 4 and the carried 1 make 6. 8 and 0 is 8.
And the wholes: 8 and 13 make 21. So the answer is 21.8605.
A quick check with the wholes only: 23 take away 14, plus 13, is 22. Our 21.8605 is close to that. Go left to right, and borrow with care.
This looks scary, but it is only brackets inside brackets. The rule: start at the innermost bracket and work outwards.
Which bracket is the innermost one?

ask.ifNot: The round bracket sits inside the square one. So the round bracket, 35 minus 2 times 12, goes first.

beats.say: Inside the round bracket there is a minus and a times. Careful: times goes first. 2 times 12 is 24.
Then 35 take away 24 is 11. So the round bracket is worth 11.
Now we see 6 of 11. What does the little word of mean in maths?

ask.ifNot: In maths, of means lots of. So 6 of 11 is 6 times 11.

beats.say: Of means times. 6 times 11 is 66.
Now finish the square bracket. 15 plus 66 is 81.
Last job. 178 take away 81. Take away 80 first to get 98, then 1 more to get 97.
We went from the inside out: the round bracket, then the of, then the square bracket, then the take away.
A five-digit number: 1, A, 9, A, 5. Both A's are the same digit, and 7 divides the number exactly. Which digit is A?

spec.note: Both A's are the same digit.

beats.say: There is no easy digit test for 7. So here is the smart move: try each choice, and divide by 7.
Start with 4. The number becomes 14945.
Divide in easy chunks. 7 times 2000 is 14000. Take that away from 14945, and 945 is left.
Now 945. 7 times 100 is 700, and that leaves 245. Is 245 in the 7 times table?

ask.ifNot: 7 times 35 is 245. So it is in the 7 times table, with nothing left over.

beats.say: So 14945 is made of 2000 sevens, 100 sevens and 35 sevens. That is 7 times 2135, with nothing left over. A is 4.
Let's test another choice, to be sure. With 5 the number is 15955. But 7 times 2279 is 15953, so 2 is left over.
The other two choices give 17975 and 12925. Each of those leaves a remainder too. Only 4 works.
So when there is no quick test, try the choices one by one. And split a big division into easy chunks.
Here are 4 numbers, and each has a 6 in it. We want the number where the 6 is worth the most.

board.text: In which number is the 6 worth the most?

beats.say: What decides how much a 6 is worth?

ask.ifNot: A long number does not help the 6. Only its own seat matters, so count the places from the right until you reach the 6.

beats.say: Start with 34562. From the right: 2 ones, then 6 tens. This 6 is worth 60.

spec.note: The 6 is in the tens place

beats.say: Next, 3342654. From the right: 4 ones, 5 tens, 6 hundreds. This 6 is worth 600.
Now 4256402. From the right: 2 ones, 0 tens, 4 hundreds, 6 thousands. This 6 is worth 6000.

spec.note: The 6 is in the thousands place

beats.say: Last, 75621. From the right: 1 one, 2 tens, 6 hundreds. Worth 600 again.
6000 is the greatest of the four. So the number is 4256402.
Did you spot the trap? 3342654 is just as long, but its 6 hides near the end. Check the seat, not the size of the number.
We are told that N is 8. We must find which equation is true. So we test each one, by putting 8 in place of N.
An equation is true when the left side and the right side come to the same number.
First: 3 N minus 14, and N plus 3. Left: 3 times 8 is 24, and 24 minus 14 is 10. Right: 8 plus 3 is 11.
10 and 11 are close, but they are not equal. So the first equation is not true.
Second: 44 minus 4 N, and 3 N minus 12. Start with the left side. What is 44, minus 4 times 8?

ask.ifNot: Multiply first: 4 times 8 is 32. Then take 32 away from 44. That leaves 12.

beats.say: So the left side is 12. Now the right: 3 times 8 is 24, and 24 minus 12 is 12. Both sides are 12!
This one is true. But a careful mathematician tests the third one too: 62 plus 3 N, and 11 N plus 2.
Left: 62 plus 24 is 86. Right: 11 times 8 is 88, and 2 more is 90. Not equal.
So the true equation is 44 minus 4 N, equals 3 N minus 12.
To test an equation, put the number in for the letter. Do the times first, then the adding or taking away.
Here is our equation. 7 times a bracket, equals 4 times a bracket, plus 6. It looks big, so we take it one step at a time.
First we open the brackets. The 7 multiplies everything inside its bracket: the 3 P, and the 4 as well.
7 times 3 P is 21 P. And what is 7 times the minus 4?

ask.ifNot: The 7 multiplies the 4 as well, not only the 3 P. 7 times 4 is 28, so we get minus 28.

beats.say: So the left side becomes 21 P, minus 28.
Now the right side. The 4 multiplies the 5 and the 3 P. 4 times 5 is 20, and 4 times 3 P is 12 P. The plus 6 just waits.
20 and 6 make 26. So our equation is now 21 P minus 28, equals 12 P plus 26. No more brackets!
The letter P is on both sides. What shall we take from both sides?

ask.ifNot: We take away the smaller lot of P, which is 12 P. Then the right side has no P left.

beats.say: 21 P take away 12 P is 9 P. So 9 P, minus 28, equals 26.
Add 28 to both sides. 26 plus 28 is 54. So 9 P equals 54.
Divide both sides by 9. 9 times 6 is 54. So P equals 6.
Let's check. Left: the bracket is 14, and 7 times 14 is 98. Right: the bracket is 23, and 4 times 23, plus 6, is also 98.
So open the brackets first, multiplying everything inside. Then gather the letters, and solve.
We add something to 1234 to reach a square number. So we need the first square above 1234.

spec.note: How far is the next square?

beats.say: Where to start? 30 times 30 is 900, too small. 40 times 40 is 1600, too big. So try in between, at 35.
35 times 35 is 1225. That is just under 1234.
1225 is below 1234. So which square should we aim for?

ask.ifNot: We are adding, so we must go up. The next square after 35 times 35 is 36 times 36.

beats.say: 36 times 36: 36 times 30 is 1080, and 36 times 6 is 216. Together, 1296.
Now find the gap from 1234 up to 1296. It is 62.
So we must add 62.
Check: 1234 plus 62 is 1296, and that is 36 times 36.
Two sums with a gap between them. We work out each side, then choose the sign that fits.
Left side. Times first. 17 times 10 is 170, and 17 times 7 is 119. So 17 times 17 is 289.
Now add the 45. 289 plus 45 is 334. That is the left side.
Right side: 16 times 14 plus 89. Which bit goes first?

ask.ifNot: Times goes before plus. So 16 times 14 comes first, and the 89 is added after.

beats.say: 16 times 10 is 160, and 16 times 4 is 64. So 16 times 14 is 224.
Add the 89. 224 plus 89 is 313. That is the right side.
Now compare 334 with 313. Which is bigger?

ask.ifNot: Both have 3 hundreds, so look at the tens. 334 has 3 tens and 313 has only 1 ten. So 334 is bigger.

beats.say: 334 is more than 313. So the left side is greater, and the sign is the greater than sign.
So: work out each side fully, times before plus, and only then compare.
We must add 100 decigrams and 300 decagrams, and give the answer in grams. Look closely: the two words are nearly the same.
Deci, with an i. Is a decigram bigger or smaller than a gram?

choices: smaller: a tenth of a gram
ask.ifNot: Deci means a tenth, like a decimal. So a decigram is a small piece: one tenth of a gram.

beats.say: 10 decigrams make 1 gram. So 100 decigrams is 100 divided by 10, which is 10 grams.
Deca, with an a, means ten. So 1 decagram is 10 grams, and 300 decagrams is 300 times 10. That is 3000 grams.
Now both are in grams, so we can add. 10 plus 3000 is 3010 grams.
Look at the choices: 310, 3100, 3000, or none of these. Is 3010 there?

ask.ifNot: Read each choice digit by digit. 3010 has its 1 in the tens place. None of the numbers matches it.

beats.say: 3010 is not one of the numbers. So the answer is: none of these. Our working is sound, so we can trust it.
Remember: deci is a tenth, deca is ten. One little letter changes everything.
Four fractions, and we want the smallest. The bottoms are 3, 29, 15 and 7. A common bottom would be huge!
So here is a clever trick. Compare each fraction with one half. If double the top is bigger than the bottom, the fraction is more than half.
Two thirds first. Double 2 is 4, and 4 is more than 3. So two thirds is more than half.
11 over 15: double 11 is 22, more than 15. And 5 over 7: double 5 is 10, more than 7. Both are more than half.
Now 13 over 29. Double 13 is 26. Is 13 over 29 more than half, or less than half?

ask.ifNot: Double the top is 26, and that is smaller than the bottom, 29. So 13 over 29 is less than half.

beats.say: 26 is less than 29, so 13 over 29 is less than half. It is the only one below half!
Three fractions are above half and only one is below. So the smallest is 13 over 29.
When the bottoms are awkward, compare with one half first. It can save a lot of work.
Two jobs in one. Add up the first ten two-digit prime numbers. Then write the total in Roman numerals.

board.text: Sum of the first 10 two-digit primes, in Roman numerals

beats.say: First list them. The two-digit primes start at 11. Here are the first ten, ending at 43.
Careful with the ones we skipped. 21, 27, 33 and 39 look prime, but each one is in the 3 times table.
Now add, in friendly pairs. 11 plus 19 is 30. 13 plus 17 is 30. 23 plus 37 is 60. 29 plus 31 is 60. And 41 plus 43 is 84.
Add the pair totals: 30, 30, 60, 60 and 84. What do they make?

ask.ifNot: Add the four round numbers first, then the 84. One at a time, and you reach 264.

beats.say: The total is 264.
Now Roman numerals. Split 264 into 200, 60 and 4. 200 is C C. 60 is L X. And 4 is I V, one before five.
Put the three parts together: C C, L X, I V. That is 264 in Roman numerals.
Watch the order of the letters. L X is 60, but X L is 40, because a smaller letter in front is taken away.
Two mystery numbers. Their L C M is 2040 and their H C F is 8. One of the numbers is 120. We must find the other.

board.text: LCM = 2040, HCF = 8. One number is 120. Other = ?

beats.say: Here is a handy fact. For any two numbers, the H C F times the L C M equals the two numbers multiplied together.

board.text: HCF × LCM = one number × other number

beats.say: So 2040 times 8 is the same as 120 times the other number. And 2040 times 8 is 16320.
So 16320 is 120 times the other number. How do we find the other number?

ask.ifNot: Times and divide are partners. To undo times 120, we divide by 120.

beats.say: 16320 divided by 120. Take one zero off each, and it is 1632 divided by 12, which is 136.
Let's check. 120 times 136 is 16320 as well. And 8 goes into 136 exactly 17 times, just as an H C F should.
So remember: H C F times L C M gives the product of the two numbers. Divide by the number you know, and the other one appears.
Three sums, and three hidden numbers: m, n and p. Each sum uses two of the letters. We must find p.
Here is a clever trick. We add all three sums together. 18 plus 24 is 42, and 42 plus 36 is 78.
In those three sums, how many times does each letter appear?

ask.ifNot: Look at m. It is in the first sum and in the third sum. That is twice. It is the same for n and for p.

beats.say: So 78 is two lots of m plus n plus p.
Half of 78 is 39. So m plus n plus p equals 39.
All three together make 39. And the first sum says m plus n is 18. So how do we find p?

ask.ifNot: Take away the m and the n together, and only p is left. m plus n is 18, so p is 39 minus 18.

beats.say: 39 minus 18 is 21. So p equals 21.
Let's check. n is 24 minus 21, which is 3. m is 36 minus 21, which is 15. And 15 plus 3 is 18. All three sums work!
Now look at the choices. 21 is not there. 18 is only m plus n, and 15 is m. So the answer is: none of these.
So when each letter appears twice, add all the sums and halve. Then take away the pair you do not want.
Each column of this square follows the same rule, going down. We must find Q at the bottom of the third column.

board.text: Each column follows the same rule.  Q = ?

spec.note: Each column follows the same rule. Q = ?

beats.say: Look at the first two columns. 3 goes to 9, and 7 goes to 21. How do we get from the top number to the middle one?

ask.ifNot: 3 times 3 is 9, and 7 times 3 is 21. Multiplying by 3 works in both columns.

beats.say: 3 times 3 is 9. 7 times 3 is 21. And in the third column, 8 times 3 is 24. Good, the rule holds.
Now from the middle to the bottom. 9 becomes 81, and 21 becomes 441. What is the rule?

ask.ifNot: 9 times 9 is 81. And 21 times 21 is 441. Each middle number is multiplied by itself.

beats.say: 9 times 9 is 81, and 21 times 21 is 441. So each bottom number is the middle number times itself.
So Q is 24 times 24. Split it: 24 twenties are 480, and 24 fours are 96.
480 plus 96 is 576. So Q is 576.
A rule can have two steps. Find each step from the complete columns, then follow both steps down the last column.
We have the digits 4, 7, 6 and 9. Using each one only once, how many 4-digit odd numbers can we make?
What makes a number odd?

ask.ifNot: Only the ones digit decides whether a number is odd or even. The other digits do not matter.

beats.say: So the last digit must be odd. Of our digits, 7 and 9 are odd. That is 2 choices for the ones place.
Say we put 7 last. Then 4, 6 and 9 are left for the other 3 places: 3 choices, then 2, then 1. 3 times 2 times 1 is 6 numbers.
It is the same story if 9 goes last: 6 more numbers. Careful not to stop at 6!
6 numbers end in 7 and 6 numbers end in 9. 2 times 6 is 12.
So 12 odd numbers can be made.
The plan: fill the place that has a rule first. Then count the choices for the other places and multiply.
3 pairs of numbers. We add each pair, and look for a total that is a square number.

board.text: Which two numbers add up to a square?

beats.say: First pair: 159 plus 165 is 324.
Is 324 a square? Try 18. 18 times 10 is 180, and 18 times 8 is 144. So what is 18 times 18?

ask.ifNot: 18 times 18 is 18 times 10 and 18 times 8 together. 180 plus 144 makes 324.

beats.say: 180 plus 144 is 324. So 324 is 18 times 18, a square!
Check the others. 198 plus 145 is 343. That is past 324, but short of 19 times 19, which is 361. Not a square.
189 plus 330 is 519. 22 times 22 is 484 and 23 times 23 is 529. In between, so not a square.
So the pair is 159 and 165.
Careful: do not jump to none of these because the sums look hard. Add each pair properly first.

spec.note: Circumference = 132 cm. Area = ?

beats.say: The circumference of a circle is 132 centimetres. We want its area.

ask.ifNot: The area rule is pi times radius times radius. So we need the radius, and the circumference can give it to us.

beats.say: We can't get the area straight from the circumference. What must we find first?
Circumference is 2 times 22 over 7 times r. 2 times 22 is 44. So it is 44 times r, divided by 7.
44 times something makes 132. Try it: 44 and 44 and 44 make 132. That is 3 lots.
So r divided by 7 is 3. That means r is 3 times 7, which is 21 centimetres.
Now the area: 22 over 7, times 21, times 21. Let the 7 divide first: 21 divided by 7 is 3.
That leaves 22 times 3 times 21. 22 times 3 is 66.
66 times 21: 66 times 20 is 1320, and one more 66 makes 1386.
The area is 1386 square centimetres.
Two stages: circumference gives the radius, then the radius gives the area. Don't rush the last multiplying.
What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand at 8:30 in the morning?

board.text: Angle between the hands at 8:30 am = ?

spec.note: Angle between the hands = ?

beats.say: Each gap between two numbers on the clock is 30 degrees, because 360 divided by 12 is 30.
At 8:30 the minute hand points at the 6. And where is the hour hand?

ask.ifNot: Half an hour has passed since 8 o'clock. So the hour hand has moved halfway from the 8 towards the 9.

beats.say: From the 6 up to the 8 is 2 full gaps. 2 times 30 is 60 degrees.
Then the hour hand is half a gap past the 8. Half of 30 is 15 degrees.
Add them. 60 plus 15 is 75 degrees.
Now look at the choices: 85 degrees, 90 degrees, 65 degrees. Our 75 is not there! So the answer is none of these.

board.text: 75° is not listed: none of these

beats.say: Trust your working. Forget the half gap and you get 60. Put the hour hand on the 9 and you get 90. The true angle is 75 degrees.
15 people are at a meeting. Each person shakes hands once with every other person. How many handshakes?

board.text: 15 people. Everyone shakes hands once. Total?

beats.say: Think about one person. They shake hands with everyone except themselves. That is 14 handshakes.
15 people, 14 handshakes each. 15 times 10 is 150, and 15 times 4 is 60. Together, 210.
Is 210 the number of handshakes?

ask.ifNot: When two people shake hands, that is one handshake. But we counted it once for each of them.

beats.say: Every handshake was counted twice, once for each person. So we halve 210. Half of 210 is 105.
So there are 105 handshakes.
Try it with 3 people: 3 times 2 is 6, and half of that is 3 handshakes. Each person with all the others, then halve.
Which of these four numbers can be divided exactly by 18? We will not divide. We will use two quick tests.
18 is 2 times 9. So the number must pass the test for 2 and the test for 9. Both, not just one.
Test for 2: the number must be even. 9567 ends in 7, so it is odd. It is out.
Test for 9: the digits must add up to a number in the 9 times table. 9672 gives 24, and 9876 gives 30. Neither is in the 9 times table.
Now 9486. What do its digits add up to?

ask.ifNot: Add them one at a time: 9, then 4, then 8, then 6. You reach 27.

beats.say: The digits add up to 27, and 27 is 9 times 3. And 9486 ends in 6, so it is even. Both tests are passed!
Here is the trap. The digits of 9567 add up to 27 as well, so 9 divides it. But it is odd, so 2 does not, and 18 cannot.
So for 18, use two tests together: an even last digit for 2, and the digit sum for 9.
We are told that 0.42 times 645 is 270.9. Now we want 4.2 times 6.45. Good news: we do not need to multiply at all.
Look at the digits. 4 and 2 in both. 6, 4 and 5 in both. Only the decimal points have moved. So the answer has the same digits too, and we just have to find where its point goes.
Compare 4.2 with 0.42. How many times as big is 4.2?

ask.ifNot: From 0.42 to 4.2, each digit has moved one place to the left. One place to the left makes a number 10 times as big.

beats.say: So the answer becomes 10 times as big. 270.9 times 10 is 2709.
Now compare 6.45 with 645. What has happened?

ask.ifNot: From 645 to 6.45, each digit has moved two places to the right. Two places to the right makes a number 100 times smaller.

beats.say: So the answer becomes 100 times smaller. 2709 divided by 100 is 27.09.
So 4.2 times 6.45 is 27.09.
Check with an estimate: 4 times 6 is 24, and 27.09 is near 24. So the point is in the right place. Same digits, so just track how the points moved.
Republic Day in 2023 was a Thursday. In which year does it fall on a Tuesday?

spec.note: Republic Day, year by year

beats.say: Republic Day is the 26th of January. In an ordinary year the same date moves on by 1 day, because 365 days is 52 weeks and 1 day.
From January 2023 to January 2024 there is no leap day in between. So 2024 gives Friday.
Careful now. Between January 2024 and the next January we pass the 29th of February 2024. How far does the day move this time?

ask.ifNot: That stretch has 366 days, one more than usual. So the day moves on by 2, not 1.

beats.say: Friday plus 2 days is Sunday. So Republic Day 2025 is a Sunday. Saturday got skipped!
Now ordinary years again. 2026 gives Monday, and 2027 gives Tuesday.
There is our Tuesday. Republic Day falls on a Tuesday in 2027.
Go one year at a time. Move 1 day, but move 2 days whenever a 29th of February sits in between.
We are asked which bracket makes this sum equal 40. The only way to know is to test each bracket in turn.
First, a bracket round 16 plus 24. That bracket is worth 40. Then 40 divided by 4 is 10, and 6 times 2 is 12.
10 plus 12 is 22. That is not 40, so cross this bracket off.
Second, a bracket round 4 plus 6 times 2. Inside it, times goes first. 6 times 2 is 12, and 4 plus 12 is 16.
So we would need 24 divided by 16. That does not share out evenly, so it cannot give 40. Cross it off.
Third, a bracket round 16 plus 24 divided by 4. Inside the bracket, what goes first?

ask.ifNot: Even inside a bracket, divide goes before plus. So 24 divided by 4 comes first.

beats.say: 24 divided by 4 is 6, and 16 plus 6 is 22. Then add the 12 from 6 times 2. 22 plus 12 is 34. Not 40.
We tested all three brackets. None of them makes 40. So the answer is none of these.
That is the trap here. Do not pick a bracket just because it looks neat. Test every choice, and be brave enough to say none of these.
Four statements, and only one of them is true. So we test every one, like a detective.
First: 18 plus 18 divided by 2 equals 18. But we divide before we add. 18 divided by 2 is 9, and 18 plus 9 is 27, not 18.
Second: a leap year has 8760 hours. A leap year has 366 days, and 366 times 24 is 8784. It is the ordinary year, with 365 days, that has 8760 hours.
Next: 586 is a square number. 24 times 24 is 576, and 25 times 25 is 625. 586 sits between them, so it is not a square.
That leaves: 2816 is divisible by 11. Use the test for 11. The 1st and 3rd digits add up to 3. The 2nd and 4th add up to 14. How far apart are 3 and 14?

ask.ifNot: Take the smaller sum from the bigger one. 14 take away 3 is 11.

beats.say: The two sums differ by 11, and that is just what the test for 11 needs. So 11 divides 2816. In fact 11 times 256 is 2816.
When a question asks which one is true, test every statement. Do not stop at the first one that looks right.
m is 2, n is 3 and p is 5. Four expressions, and we want the one with the least value. So we work out each one.
First, m times n, plus p. Times first: 2 times 3 is 6. Then 6 plus 5 is 11.
Next, p minus m in a bracket, times n. Bracket first: 5 minus 2 is 3. Then 3 times 3 is 9.
Now p minus n in a bracket, times m. With the numbers in, that is 5 minus 3 in a bracket, times 2. What do we do first?

ask.ifNot: A bracket always goes first. So work out 5 minus 3, and then multiply by 2.

beats.say: 5 minus 3 is 2. And 2 times 2 is 4.
Last, p plus n minus m. 5 plus 3 is 8, and 8 minus 2 is 6.
Compare the four values: 11, 9, 4 and 6. The smallest is 4.
That 4 came from p minus n, in a bracket, times m. So that one has the least value.
To find the least, work out every expression, brackets first. Then compare the numbers, not the letters.
Here x is a mystery number, and x plus 9 is a 2-digit prime. We want the 12th even number after it.
We don't know which prime it is. But we can still say something. Is a 2-digit prime odd or even?

ask.ifNot: An even number has 2 as a factor. The only even prime is 2 itself, and that has just 1 digit.

beats.say: So x plus 9 is odd. That makes x plus 10 the 1st even number after it, and x plus 12 the 2nd. Each jump is 2.
From the 1st even number to the 12th, how many jumps of 2 do we make?

ask.ifNot: The 1st one needs no jump. So the jumps are 1 fewer than 12, which is 11.

beats.say: Careful, that is the trap. x plus 10 is already the 1st, so we make 11 jumps. 11 twos are 22.
We started at x plus 10 and moved 22 further on. 10 plus 22 is 32.
So the 12th even number is x plus 32.
Quick check. x plus 10 is even, and 22 is even. Even plus even stays even, so x plus 32 is an even number. Good.
So the plan is: find the 1st even number, count 1 fewer jump than the place number, and step on in 2s.
Here is 48 degrees. The question wants two other angles, the complement and the supplement, added together.

ask.ifNot: A square corner is a right angle, a quarter turn. That is 90 degrees. 180 is for a straight line.

beats.say: First the complement. Complementary angles fit together into a square corner. How much do they make together?
So the complement is 90 take away 48. 90 take away 40 is 50, and 8 more away leaves 42.

ask.ifNot: The two angles on the line make 180 together. So take 48 away from 180.

beats.say: Now the supplement. Supplementary angles sit together on a straight line, and a straight line is 180 degrees. Which sum gives the supplement?
180 take away 48. Here is a quick way: 180 is 90 more than 90, so the supplement is 90 more than the complement. 42 and 90 make 132.
Careful now. The question wants the sum of the two partners. Not the angle itself. Just the complement and the supplement.
42 plus 132. The tens first: 40 and 130 make 170. Then the ones: 2 and 2 make 4. Altogether, 174.
So the sum is 174 degrees.
Remember the two totals. 90 for complementary, 180 for supplementary. Find each partner, then add.
In 768459 we compare two digits, the 4 and the 5. How many times the value of the 5 is the value of the 4?

spec.note: Compare the 4 and the 5

beats.say: Count from the right: 9 ones, 5 tens, 4 hundreds. So what is the 4 worth?

ask.ifNot: 9 is in the ones, 5 is in the tens and 4 is in the hundreds. 4 hundreds is 400.

beats.say: 4 hundreds is 400. And the 5 is in the tens, so it is worth 50.
How many times means: how many lots of 50 fit into 400? So we divide.
Cross off one zero from each, and we have 40 divided by 5. That is 8.
So the 4 is worth 8 times as much as the 5.
Careful: the hundreds seat is 10 times the tens seat, so 10 looks tempting. But the digits are different, so we must use 400 and 50.
Check: 50 times 8 is 400. It works.
Letters on top this time. M, N, Q and P are all the same number, and we want the greatest fraction.
The same top means each fraction takes the same number of pieces. So the only thing that matters is how big each piece is.
Here is one piece of each kind. Which pieces are the biggest?

ask.ifNot: Look at the bars. Cutting a bar into fewer pieces leaves bigger pieces. The sevenths bar is cut into the fewest.

beats.say: Fewer pieces means bigger pieces. So with the same top, the smallest bottom gives the greatest fraction.
The smallest bottom is 7. So Q over 7 is the greatest fraction.
Let's test it with a number. If every letter is 1, then 1 over 7 is a bigger slice than 1 over 12. Yes, it fits.
Did 12 tempt you? It is the biggest number, but it gives the smallest pieces. Same top: smaller bottom, greater fraction.
This sum should come to 40, but it needs one bracket to make it true. Let us find where the bracket goes.
First, try it with no bracket at all. Times first: 3 times 25 is 75. Then 75 take away 13, plus 4, comes to 66. Too big.
We want 40, not 66. So the 3 must multiply something smaller than 25. Which bracket does that?

ask.ifNot: A bracket round 25 minus 13 is worth less than 25. Then the 3 multiplies a smaller number.

beats.say: Try it. Bracket first. 25 take away 13 is 12.
Then the times. 3 times 12 is 36.
Then the plus. 36 plus 4 is 40. That is our number!
So the bracket goes round 25 minus 13.
What about the other brackets? Round 13 plus 4, we get 75 take away 17, which is 58. Round all three numbers, we get 3 times 16, which is 48. Neither is 40.
The key idea: a bracket changes which job is done first. Try it, work it through, and see if it lands on the target.
The series goes 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, and on. We want the 11th number in it.
First find the jump. 10 minus 7 is 3, and 13 minus 10 is 3 too. So each number is 3 more than the one before.
We could keep going one step at a time, but that is slow. From the 1st number to the 11th, how many jumps do we make?

ask.ifNot: From the 1st to the 2nd is 1 jump. From the 1st to the 3rd is 2 jumps. The jumps are always 1 fewer than the place number.

beats.say: Careful, this is the trap. The 1st number is there before any jump. So we make 1 fewer jump than 11. That is 10 jumps.
10 jumps of 3. 10 times 3 is 30.
The jumps cover 30. What do we do with the 30?

ask.ifNot: The jumps start at the 1st number, which is 7. So the 30 is added on to 7.

beats.say: 7 plus 30 is 37. So the 11th number is 37.
Test the idea on the 5th number, which we can see. 4 jumps of 3 make 12, and 7 plus 12 is 19. It matches.
So remember: the 11th number is only 10 jumps from the 1st. Count the jumps, not the numbers.
Find the one-digit prime numbers, add them, and then square the total.
Which list shows all the one-digit primes?

ask.ifNot: 1 is not prime, because it has only one factor. And 9 is 3 times 3, so it is not prime either.

beats.say: The one-digit primes are 2, 3, 5 and 7. Add them up, and we get 17.
Now square 17. That means 17 times 17. 17 times 10 is 170, and 17 times 7 is 119. Together they make 289.
Our answer is 289. Now look at the choices: 361, 324, 441, or none of these. Which do we pick?

ask.ifNot: Our answer is 289. It is not 361, 324 or 441. So we pick none of these.

beats.say: 289 is not in the list, so the answer is none of these. When your working checks out, trust it.
See where the other choices come from. Count 1 as a prime and the sum is 18, which gives 324. Count 9 as a prime and the sum is 21, which gives 441.
Three small jobs hide in this question. Find two special numbers, add them, and then look for the 9 in the total.
The greatest 4-digit number is easy. Fill every seat with a 9, and we get 9999.
Now the greatest 2-digit prime. Which of these is it?

ask.ifNot: 99 can be divided by 3, and 98 can be divided by 2, so they are not prime. 97 cannot be divided by anything except 1 and itself.

beats.say: Start at 99 and walk down. 99 is 3 times 33. 98 is 2 times 49. 97 passes every test, so 97 is our prime.
Now add. 9999 is just 1 less than 10000. So add 97 to 10000 and take 1 away. We get 10096.
Here is the trap. The question is not about the 9s we started with. We must look for the 9 in the total, 10096.

spec.note: Where is the 9 now?

beats.say: In 10096, count from the right: 6 ones, then 9 tens. So the 9 is worth 9 times 10, which is 90.
So: do every job in order, and only then answer the question that was asked.
We must divide the L C M of 36 and 84 by their H C F. That is three jobs: find the H C F, find the L C M, then divide.
Start by breaking each number into prime factors, the building blocks it is made of.
36 is even, so 2 comes out first. Keep splitting, and 36 is 2 times 2 times 3 times 3.
Take 84. Keep pulling out the smallest prime that fits: 2 twice, then 3, and 7 is left. So 84 is 2 times 2 times 3 times 7.
First the H C F. It is built only from the primes that both numbers have. Which of these is exactly what 36 and 84 share?

ask.ifNot: Look for the primes that sit on both lines. A prime that only one number has cannot divide the other one, so it stays out.

beats.say: Both lines have two 2s and a 3. 2 times 2 times 3 is 12, so the H C F is 12.
Now the L C M. It must hold all of 36 and all of 84. So we take each prime the most times it shows up in one number: two 2s, two 3s and one 7. Multiply them, and we get 252.
A quick check on the L C M. 252 divided by 36 is 7, and 252 divided by 84 is 3. Both are exact.
We have the H C F, 12, and the L C M, 252. Now the last job. What do we work out to finish?

ask.ifNot: The question says the L C M divided by the H C F. So the L C M goes first, and we divide it by the H C F.

beats.say: 252 divided by 12 is 21. That is our answer.
Here is something neat. 36 is 12 times 3, and 84 is 12 times 7. The leftover parts, 3 and 7, multiply to give 21: our answer again.
So the plan: prime factors first, then the H C F from the shared primes, the L C M from all of them, and last of all the divide.

board.text: Perimeter of square = perimeter of triangle
Triangle side = 16 cm. Area of square = ?

spec.note: A square has the same perimeter. Area of the square = ?

beats.say: A square and an equilateral triangle have equal perimeters. The triangle's sides are 16 centimetres each. What is the area of the square?

ask.ifNot: The only thing the two shapes share is the perimeter. So we begin with the triangle's perimeter.

beats.say: We can't use 16 for the square. That is the triangle's side. So what should we find first?
All 3 sides of the triangle are 16 centimetres. 3 times 16 is 48.
The square has that same perimeter, 48, shared among 4 equal sides. 48 divided by 4 is 12.
Now the area of the square is side times side. 12 times 12 is 144.
So the area of the square is 144 square centimetres.
Check the perimeters. Square: 4 times 12 is 48. Triangle: 48 as well. They match.
Remember the path: triangle's perimeter, then the square's side, then the square's area.
Here is our equation. 16 y, minus 36, equals 4 y, plus a bracket.
Start with the bracket. It has only plain numbers in it. 8 times 9 is 72.
Now y is on both sides. What do we take from both sides?

ask.ifNot: We take away the smaller lot of y, which is 4 y. Then the right side has no y left.

beats.say: 16 y take away 4 y is 12 y. So 12 y, minus 36, equals 72.
What next?

ask.ifNot: The 36 is being taken away on the left. To undo that, we add 36 to both sides.

beats.say: 72 plus 36 is 108. So 12 y equals 108.
Now divide both sides by 12. Try 9: 10 times 9 is 90, and 2 times 9 is 18. Together that is 108.
So 12 times 9 is 108, and y equals 9.
Let's check. Left: 16 times 9, minus 36, is 108. Right: 4 times 9, plus 72, is also 108. Both sides match.
So work out any plain bracket first. Then gather the letters, undo the taking away, and divide.
We add 2012 and 689. Then we take away a mystery number, and 1789 is left. What is the mystery number?
First find the sum. 2012 is 2000 and 12. 2000 plus 689 is 2689. Then 12 more makes 2701.
We have 2701, and we want to be left with 1789. How do we find what to take away?

ask.ifNot: The number to take away is the gap between 2701 and 1789. To find a gap, take the smaller from the bigger.

beats.say: Find the gap by counting up from 1789. Add 11 to reach 1800. Add 200 to reach 2000. Then add 701 to reach 2701.
Now add up the three hops. 11 and 200 and 701 make 912.
So we must subtract 912.
Check by adding back. 1789 plus 912 takes us to 2701 again. It fits.
So: do the sum first. Then the number to take away is the gap between what you have and what you want.
A shopkeeper sells 1 gross of eggs for 864 rupees. We want the cost of 1 score of eggs.
Gross and score are old names for numbers. A gross is 12 dozen, and a dozen is 12. So a gross is 12 times 12, which is 144.
And how many is a score?

ask.ifNot: A score is 20. A dozen is the one that is 12.

beats.say: So 144 eggs cost 864 rupees, and we want the price of 20 eggs. First we find the price of 1 egg.
144 times 5 is 720. One more 144 makes 864. So that is 6 lots, and 1 egg costs 6 rupees.
Now 20 eggs. 20 times 6 is 120.
So 1 score of eggs costs 120 rupees.
The plan: turn the number words into numbers, find the price of 1, then multiply.
In a magic square, every row, every column and both diagonals add up to the same total. We must find m plus n.

spec.note: A magic square. Find m + n

beats.say: We don't know the total yet. But look at two lines that both pass through x: the middle row 4, x, m, and the diagonal 6, x, 16.
Both lines have the same total, and both contain x. So what must be equal?

ask.ifNot: Take x away from both lines. What is left must still be equal: 4 plus m on one line, 6 plus 16 on the other.

beats.say: 6 plus 16 is 22. So 4 plus m is 22 too, and m is 18.
Now for the magic total. Here is a fact about every 3 by 3 magic square: each line adds up to 3 times the middle number.
The diagonal is 22 plus x, and that must be 3 lots of x. So 22 is 2 lots of x. That makes x 11, and the magic total 3 times 11, which is 33.
The first column is n, 4 and 16, and it must add up to 33. So what is n?

ask.ifNot: 4 plus 16 is 20. And 33 take away 20 is 13.

beats.say: 4 plus 16 is 20, and 33 take away 20 is 13. So n is 13.
m is 18 and n is 13. So m plus n is 31.
Here is the finished square. Every row, column and diagonal adds up to 33.

spec.note: Every line adds up to 33

beats.say: In a magic square, compare two lines that share a box. And remember: each line is 3 times the middle number.
This is a long chain of adding and taking away. Here is a neat trick: collect the numbers we add in one group, and the numbers we take away in another.
Which numbers are being taken away?

ask.ifNot: Look for the minus signs. There is a minus in front of 1.9 and a minus in front of 3.2.

beats.say: So 1.9 and 3.2 are taken away. The other three, 1.8, 2.3 and 2.7, are added.
First the numbers we add. 2.3 and 2.7 are friends: together they make exactly 5. Then 5 and 1.8 make 6.8.
Next the numbers we take away. 1.9 and 3.2 make 5.1.
We have added 6.8 in all, and we must take away 5.1 in all. What is 6.8 take away 5.1?
