ask.ifNot: Divide and times go before plus. So the plus waits until both of them are done.

beats.say: The plus waits. 25 divided by 5 is 5. And 4 times 3 is 12.
Now the plus gets its turn. 5 plus 12 is 17.
If we had added the 5 and the 4 first, and then multiplied by 3, we would have got a different number. The 4 belongs to the times.
So: bracket first, with times before plus inside it. Then divide and times. The plus comes last.
Express the time 3 hours 45 minutes as a decimal number of hours.
The 3 whole hours are easy. They stay as 3. The puzzle is the 45 minutes: what part of an hour is that?
An hour has 60 minutes. So 45 minutes is what fraction of an hour?

ask.ifNot: Minutes are parts of 60, not parts of 100. So 45 minutes is 45 out of 60.

beats.say: 45 minutes is 45 out of the 60 minutes in an hour.
Make the fraction simpler. Divide the top and the bottom by 15. 45 divided by 15 is 3, and 60 divided by 15 is 4. So it is three quarters.
Three quarters is the same as 75 hundredths. As a decimal, that is 0.75.
Now put the 3 whole hours back. 3 plus 0.75 is 3.75.
So 3 hours 45 minutes is 3.75 hours.
The trap is to copy the 45 after the point. But 45 minutes is not 45 hundredths of an hour. Always put the minutes over 60 first.
G plus 12 is an even number. We want the 6th even number prior to it. Prior means before.
Which number do we start counting back from?

ask.ifNot: The even number in the question is G plus 12, the whole thing. That is our starting point, not G on its own.

beats.say: We start at G plus 12. Even numbers are 2 apart, so each step back takes away 2.
How much do 6 steps back take away?

ask.ifNot: Each step back is worth 2, not 1. Six steps of 2 make 12.

beats.say: 6 times 2 is 12. So we take 12 away from G plus 12.
Plus 12, then minus 12. They cancel each other, and nothing extra is left. Just G.
So the 6th even number before G plus 12 is G itself.
Check with a number. If G were 20, then G plus 12 is 32. Going back 12 from 32 brings us to 20. Back at G.
The trap is to count back from G and get G minus 12. Always start from the number the question gives you.
We use 7, 4, 3 and 0, once each, to make 4-digit even numbers. How many can we make?

board.text: Digits 7, 4, 3, 0 once each: how many 4-digit even numbers?

beats.say: An even number ends in an even digit. Which of our digits can go in the last seat?

ask.ifNot: Even digits are 0, 2, 4, 6 and 8. From our four digits, 0 and 4 are even. So the last digit is 0 or 4.

beats.say: Group one: the number ends in 0. Then 7, 4 and 3 fill the first three seats in any order. That gives 6 numbers.
Group two: the number ends in 4. The digits left are 7, 3 and 0.
Careful, here is the trap. The first seat cannot be 0, or it is not a 4-digit number. So the first digit is 7 or 3.
That gives 7034, 7304, 3074 and 3704. Just 4 numbers.
Add the two groups: 6 plus 4 is 10.
So: split into cases by the last digit, and leave out anything that starts with 0.
A cinema hall with rows named by letters. To count the people, we first need to know how many rows there are.

board.text: Rows A to Q, 17 seats each. Rows A to H: 3 empty each.

beats.say: The rows go from A to Q. Count along the alphabet on your fingers. How many letters is that?

ask.ifNot: Q is the 17th letter of the alphabet. So rows A to Q make 17 rows.

beats.say: Q is the 17th letter, so there are 17 rows. And each row has 17 seats.
17 rows of 17 seats. 17 times 10 is 170, and 17 times 7 is 119. Together, 289 seats.
Now the empty seats. Rows A to H each have 3 empty, and H is the 8th letter. How many seats are empty?

ask.ifNot: Only rows A to H have empty seats. That is 8 rows, with 3 empty seats in each. So 8 times 3.

beats.say: 8 times 3 is 24. So 24 seats are empty.
Take the empty seats away from all the seats. 289 take away 24 is 265.
So 265 people are seated. The trap was in the letters: A to Q is 17 rows, and A to H is 8 rows. Count them carefully.
A boy has six cards: three 4s and three 9s. He uses 5 of them to make a 3-digit number and a 2-digit number. Which choice can be their difference?
Every digit is a 4 or a 9. So the ones digit of the answer comes from a 4 or a 9, take away a 4 or a 9. What can it be?

ask.ifNot: 4 take away 4 is 0, and 9 take away 9 is 0. 9 take away 4 is 5. So only 0 or 5 can appear.

beats.say: Equal digits leave 0. 9 take away 4 leaves 5. And 4 take away 9 borrows a ten: 14 take away 9 is 5. So the answer ends in 0 or 5.
Now the size. Suppose the 3-digit number starts with 4. The smallest difference is 444 take away 99, which is 345. The largest is 499 take away 44, which is 455.
So 150 is too small. And if the 3-digit number starts with 9, the difference is at least 944 take away 99, which is 845. 550 falls in the gap.
Only 450 is left. But can he really make it? Which of these works with his cards?

ask.ifNot: 494 take away 44 does make 450, but it needs four 4s, and he has only three. 499 take away 49 uses two 4s and three 9s.

beats.say: 499 take away 49 is 450. It uses two 4s and three 9s, and he has those cards. So the difference can be 450.
When you can't try every case, test the last digit and the size. Then make sure the choice that is left can really be built.
Here is a puzzle with a star. 19 over star, plus 17 over star, equals 2. The star is the same number both times.
Both fractions have the same bottom number, the star. When the bottoms are the same, we just add the tops.
19 plus 17 is 36. So 36 over star equals 2.
36 over star means 36 divided by star. So 36 is shared into equal groups, and each group gets 2.
36 divided by which number gives 2?

ask.ifNot: If each group gets 2, we need to know how many 2s make 36. That is 36 divided by 2, which is 18.

beats.say: 36 divided by 2 is 18. So the star is 18.
Let's check. 19 over 18, plus 17 over 18, is 36 over 18. And 36 divided by 18 is 2. It works!
Careful with 36. It is only the sum of the tops. With 36 on the bottom, the answer would be 1, not 2.
So with the same bottom number, add the tops first. Then ask: divided by what gives the answer?
Twelve dozen notebooks are piled up, and each one is 5 millimetres thick. How high is the pile?

board.text: 12 dozen notebooks, each 5 mm thick. Height?

beats.say: First, how many notebooks is twelve dozen? A dozen is 12.

ask.ifNot: Twelve dozen means 12 lots of 12. That is 12 times 12.

beats.say: 12 times 12 is 144. So there are 144 notebooks.
Each is 5 millimetres thick, so we need 144 times 5. A trick: 144 times 10 is 1440, and 5 is half of 10, so halve it. 720 millimetres.
Now look at the choices. 720 millimetres is not there, but one choice is in centimetres. 10 millimetres make 1 centimetre.
720 divided by 10 is 72. So the pile is 72 centimetres high.
So do not rush to 'none of these'. Sometimes the answer is hiding in a different unit.
Here is our equation. 97, minus 17 x, equals 5 x, plus 31. The x is on both sides.
On the left, 17 x is being taken away. Let's clear it, so that all the x are together on the right.
How do we clear the minus 17 x?

ask.ifNot: The 17 x is being taken away. To undo taking away, we add. So we add 17 x to both sides.

beats.say: We add 17 x to both sides. The left is just 97. On the right, 5 x and 17 x make 22 x.
Now what do we do with the plus 31?

ask.ifNot: The 31 is added on the right. To undo adding, we take away. So 31 comes off both sides.

beats.say: 97 minus 31 is 66. So 66 equals 22 x.
22 times x is 66. Try 3: 22 times 3 is 66. So x equals 3.
Let's check. Left: 17 times 3 is 51, and 97 minus 51 is 46. Right: 5 times 3 is 15, and 15 plus 31 is 46. Both match!
So when something with x is being taken away, add it to both sides. Then all the x sit together.
The 1st of January 2006 fell on a Sunday. On which day did the 1st of January 2010 fall?

spec.note: 1st January, year by year

beats.say: From 2006 to 2010 we pass through 4 whole years. Each one pushes the 1st of January forward. But by how much?
52 weeks make 364 days. An ordinary year has 365 days, so it is 52 weeks and 1 day. It pushes the day on by 1.
A leap year has 366 days, which is 52 weeks and 2 days. So a leap year pushes the day on by 2.
Which of the years 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2009 is a leap year?

ask.ifNot: A leap year divides exactly by 4. Look at the last two digits, 08, which is just 8. And 8 is 4 times 2, so 2008 is the one.

beats.say: 2008 is the leap year. So the pushes are 1, 1, 2 and 1.
Add the pushes. 1 plus 1 plus 2 plus 1 is 5 days.
Count 5 days on from Sunday: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday.
If you push just 1 day for every year, you land on Thursday. The leap year 2008 is the step that is easy to miss.
The angle measures 35 degrees. We have two jobs: find its complementary angle and its supplementary angle. Then we add them.

ask.ifNot: A square corner is a right angle, a quarter turn. That is 90 degrees. 180 is for a straight line.

beats.say: First the complement. Complementary angles fit together into a square corner. How much do they make together?
So the complement is 90 take away 35. 90 take away 30 is 60, and 5 more away leaves 55.

ask.ifNot: The two angles on the line make 180 together. So take 35 away from 180.

beats.say: Now the supplement. Supplementary angles sit together on a straight line, and a straight line is 180 degrees. Which sum gives the supplement?
180 take away 35. Here is a quick way: 180 is 90 more than 90, so the supplement is 90 more than the complement. 55 and 90 make 145.
Careful now. The question wants the sum of the two partners. Not the angle itself. Just the complement and the supplement.
55 plus 145. The tens first: 50 and 140 make 190. Then the ones: 5 and 5 make 10. Altogether, 200.
So the sum is 200 degrees.
C for complementary, C for corner: 90. S for supplementary, S for straight line: 180. Find both partners, then add them.
We need the sum of the L C M and the H C F of 24 and 32. That is three jobs: find the H C F, find the L C M, then add them.
Start by breaking each number into prime factors, the building blocks it is made of.
Take 24. Keep pulling out the smallest prime that fits: 2 three times, and 3 is left. So 24 is 2 times 2 times 2 times 3.
Take 32. It is made only of 2s: 2 times 2 times 2 times 2 times 2.
First the H C F. It is built only from the primes that both numbers have. Which of these is exactly what 24 and 32 share?

ask.ifNot: Look for the primes that sit on both lines. A prime that only one number has cannot divide the other one, so it stays out.

beats.say: Both lines have three 2s. 2 times 2 times 2 is 8, so the H C F is 8.
Now the L C M. It must hold all of 24 and all of 32. So we take each prime the most times it shows up in one number: five 2s and one 3. Multiply them, and we get 96.
A quick check on the L C M. 96 divided by 24 is 4, and 96 divided by 32 is 3. Both are exact.
We have the H C F, 8, and the L C M, 96. Now the last job. What do we work out to finish?

ask.ifNot: Sum means add. And it is the L C M and the H C F that we add, not the two numbers we started with.

beats.say: 96 plus 8 is 104. That is our answer.
Read the question with care: sum means add, difference means subtract. And do finish the last step. The L C M on its own is not the answer.
Tom puts 100 marbles into four boxes. Each box has 2 more marbles than the one before.
Compare every box with the first one. The second has 2 more. The third has 4 more. The fourth has 6 more.
How many extra marbles is that altogether?

ask.ifNot: The extras are 2, 4 and 6. Add all three: 2 plus 4 plus 6 is 12.

beats.say: 2 plus 4 plus 6 is 12. Take those 12 extras away, and all four boxes are equal. 100 minus 12 is 88.
Now 88 marbles are shared equally among 4 boxes. 88 divided by 4 is 22. So the first box has 22.
Each box has 2 more than the one before. So the boxes hold 22, 24, 26 and 28.
Careful! Read the question again. Which boxes does it ask about?

ask.ifNot: The question says the total in the first 3 boxes. So we leave out the fourth box, the one with 28.

beats.say: The first three boxes are everything except the last box. 100 minus 28 is 72.
So find every box first. Then answer exactly what was asked: here, only the first three boxes.
We need to write 1789 the Roman way. Romans had no place seats like ours, so first we break the number into parts.
Split it by place: 1000, 700, 80 and 9.
Here are the 7 Roman letters and what each one is worth. Keep them in view.

spec.note: and V = 5, I = 1

beats.say: 1000 is simply M.
Now the 700. How do the Romans write 700?

ask.ifNot: 700 is 500 and 2 more hundreds. The big letter D comes first, and then the two Cs.

beats.say: 700 is 500 and 2 more hundreds, so we write D C C.
80 is 50 and 3 more tens, so we write L X X X. 9 is 1 less than 10, so the smaller letter goes in front: I X.
Now join the parts in order, biggest first: M, D C C, L X X X, I X.
The trap here is to write each digit on its own: 1, 7, 8, 9. Roman numerals show the full value of each part, like 1000 and 700.
So the plan for any number: split it by place, write each part in Roman letters, then join them from left to right.
A palindrome reads the same backwards. A 3-digit palindrome is added to 2018, and the total is a 4-digit palindrome. We want the sum of the 3-digit number's digits.
First, how big is the total? The smallest 3-digit palindrome is 101 and the largest is 999. So the total is between 2119 and 3017.
Could the total start with 3? The only palindrome that small is 3003. But 3003 take away 2018 is 985, and 985 is not a palindrome.
So the total starts with 2. It is a palindrome, so it ends with 2 as well. Now, 2018 ends in 8. So what must our 3-digit number end in?

ask.ifNot: 8 plus 4 makes a number that ends in 2. So the ones digit must be 4.

beats.say: 8 plus 4 is 12, which ends in 2. So our palindrome ends in 4, and it must start with 4 too. It looks like 4, something, 4.
Try the middle digit. 404 gives 2422. 414 gives 2432. 424 gives 2442. Only the last one reads the same backwards!
So the 3-digit palindrome is 424. Its digits are 4, 2 and 4, and they add up to 10.
Use the ends first. The size gave us the first digit of the total, and the ones digits gave us the last digit. Then only a few tries were left.
Each bean weighs 2.5 grams, and all the beans in the bag weigh half a kilogram. How many beans are there?

board.text: Bean: 2.5 g. Bag: half a kg. How many beans?

beats.say: One weight is in grams and the other is in kilograms. What do we do first?

ask.ifNot: We can only compare weights that are in the same unit. Let's change the bag's weight into grams.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams, and half of 1000 is 500. So the beans weigh 500 grams.
Now, 2.5 is an awkward number to divide by. Here is a trick: take 2 beans together. 2.5 plus 2.5 is 5 grams.
So every pair of beans weighs 5 grams. How many 5s are there in 500?

ask.ifNot: 5 goes into 5 once. So into 500 it goes 100 times.

beats.say: 500 divided by 5 is 100. That is 100 pairs of beans.
Careful: 100 is the number of pairs, not beans. Each pair is 2 beans, so we double it. 200 beans.
Check: 200 beans at 2.5 grams each is 500 grams. It fits. Same units first, then count how many fit.
James eats half the cake on Saturday. On Sunday he eats two thirds of the remainder. What fraction of the cake is left for Monday?

board.text: Sat: 1/2 of the cake.  Sun: 2/3 of the remainder.

beats.say: Saturday first. James eats half the cake, so half is left.
On Sunday he eats two thirds of the remainder. Two thirds of what?

choices: of the half that is left
ask.ifNot: Remainder means what is left over. After Saturday only half a cake is left, so Sunday's two thirds comes out of that half.

beats.say: So we cut the half that is left into 3 equal parts. He eats 2 of them, and 1 part stays for Monday.
Here is the key question. Each of those small parts is what fraction of the whole cake?

ask.ifNot: Cut the other half into 3 parts as well. Now the whole cake has 6 equal parts. So each part is 1 over 6 of the cake.

beats.say: The whole cake would have 6 of these parts. So each part is 1 over 6 of the cake.
He ate 2 of the 3 parts on Sunday, and 1 part is left. So 1 over 6 of the cake is left for Monday.
Check: he ate 3 sixths on Saturday and 2 sixths on Sunday. With the 1 sixth left, that makes the whole cake.
The trap is one third: that is the part of the half, not of the whole cake. Always ask: a fraction of what?
4 pairs of numbers. We add each pair, and look for a total that is a square number.

board.text: Which pair adds up to a square number?

beats.say: First pair: 91 plus 19 is 110.
Is 110 a square number? 10 times 10 is 100 and 11 times 11 is 121.

choices: No, it falls between two squares
ask.ifNot: 110 is more than 100 but less than 121. There is no whole number between 10 and 11, so 110 is not a square.

beats.say: 110 sits between 100 and 121, so it is not a square. Next pair: 157 plus 68 is 225.
225 is 15 times 15. A square number!
Let us check the others, to be sure. 59 plus 52 is 111, and 76 plus 78 is 154. Neither is a square.
So the pair is 157 and 68.
A tip: learn the squares of the numbers up to 15 by heart. Then you spot 225 at once.
A square. Each side measures 3 a plus 2 b. We want its perimeter.

spec.note: Perimeter = ?

beats.say: How do we get the perimeter of a square from its side?

ask.ifNot: A square has 4 equal sides. Walking round, you pass all 4. So the perimeter is 4 times the side.

beats.say: 4 times, 3 a plus 2 b. 4 times 3 a is 12 a. 4 times 2 b is 8 b.
So the perimeter is 12 a plus 8 b. But look at the choices. 12 a plus 8 b is not there! Do not panic. It may be hiding in another form.
Open each choice and see. The first one: 2 times, 3 a plus 2 b, is 6 a plus 4 b. That is only 2 sides, so it is too small.
Now this one: 2 times, 6 a plus 4 b. What does it open out to?

ask.ifNot: The 2 multiplies both parts. 2 times 6 a is 12 a. And 2 times 4 b is 8 b.

beats.say: 2 times 6 a is 12 a, and 2 times 4 b is 8 b. That is exactly our perimeter, in disguise.
And the choices with 5 a b cannot be right. 3 a and 2 b are different letters, so they never join into one term.
Work out your own answer first. If it is not among the choices, open the brackets in each choice and compare. Here it is 2 times, 6 a plus 4 b.
The series is 519, 398, 277, 156, and then a star. The numbers are shrinking. Let's find the next one.

spec.note: How big is each jump? What comes next?

beats.say: Find the first drop. 519 minus 398 is 121.
Before we trust that, what should we do?

ask.ifNot: One drop does not make a rule. Test the other neighbours to see if the drop is always 121.

beats.say: 398 minus 277 is 121. 277 minus 156 is 121. The drop is 121 every time.
So take 121 away from 156. Take away 100 first to get 56. Then take away 21 to get 35.
So the star stands for 35.
Check by adding back. 35 plus 121 is 156. It fits.
Find the jump, check it on every pair, then make one more jump. And with big numbers, subtract in easy pieces.

board.text: Rectangle 3 cm by 1 cm, cut into 3 squares.

spec.note: Cut into 3 square pieces

beats.say: A rectangle 3 centimetres long and 1 centimetre broad is cut into 3 square pieces. How much more is the total perimeter of the squares than the perimeter of the rectangle?
Each piece is a square of side 1 centimetre. One square has a perimeter of 4 times 1, which is 4.

ask.ifNot: One square has 4 centimetres. There are 3 squares, so we need 3 lots of 4.

beats.say: There are 3 squares. What is their total perimeter?
3 times 4 is 12 centimetres.
Now the rectangle. 3 plus 1 is 4, and double is 8 centimetres.
12 minus 8 is 4. The squares have 4 centimetres more.
Where did the extra come from? Each cut opens 2 new edges of 1 centimetre. 2 cuts, so 2 times 2 is 4. It matches.
Cutting never changes the area, but it always adds perimeter, because new edges appear.

board.text: Isosceles triangle with one angle of 57°.
Which can be another of its angles?

beats.say: One angle of an isosceles triangle is 57 degrees. Which of these can be another angle of the triangle?
An isosceles triangle has 2 equal angles, the twins, and 1 odd angle. The 57 could be a twin, or it could be the odd one. We try both.
Case 1: 57 is a twin. The angles are 57, 57 and one more. 57 plus 57 is 114, and 180 minus 114 is 66.
So in case 1 the other angles are 57 and 66. Neither of those is among the choices. On to case 2.

ask.ifNot: The 3 angles make 180. Take away the 57, and the twins share what is left.

beats.say: Case 2: 57 is the odd one. What do the twins share between them?
123. Careful: 123 is one of the choices, but it is both twins together, not one angle.
Each twin is half of 123. Half of 122 is 61, so half of 123 is 61 and a half. We write that as 61.5.
An angle does not have to be a whole number. Check: 57 plus 61.5 plus 61.5 makes 180.
So another angle of the triangle can be 61.5 degrees.
And 33? That is 90 minus 57. It would give a right-angled triangle with no twins at all. So for isosceles puzzles, try the angle as a twin, then as the odd one.
We want to write 9 and one eighth as a decimal.

spec.note: 9 wholes and this 1/8: write it as a decimal

beats.say: The 9 wholes stay just as they are. Only the fraction part, one eighth, has to be changed.
Let's turn one eighth into thousandths. 8 times what makes 1000?

ask.ifNot: 8 times 100 is not enough. 8 times 125 makes exactly 1000.

beats.say: So multiply the top and the bottom by 125. One eighth is 125 thousandths.
How do we write 125 thousandths as a decimal?

ask.ifNot: Thousandths take three digits after the point. So 125 thousandths is 0.125.

beats.say: Now put the 9 wholes back. 9 and 0.125 make 9.125.
The trap is to write the 1 and the 8 straight after the point. A fraction is a division, so we have to work it out.
Another way to see it: one quarter is 0.25, and one eighth is half of that. Keep the whole number, and change only the fraction.
This sum should come to 13. One bracket will make it true. Where does it go?
First, with no bracket. 48 divided by 8 is 6. Then 6 take away 2 is 4, and 4 plus 5 is 9. Too small.
We need a bigger answer. Here is an idea. If we divide 48 by a smaller number, what happens to the answer?

ask.ifNot: Share 48 among fewer people and each one gets more. Dividing by a smaller number gives a bigger answer.

beats.say: So let us make the number after the divide sign smaller. Put the bracket round 8 minus 2.
Bracket first. 8 take away 2 is 6.
Then the divide. 48 divided by 6 is 8.
Then the plus. 8 plus 5 is 13. That is our number!
So the bracket goes round 8 minus 2.
A bracket round 48 divided by 8 changes nothing, because the divide goes first anyway. A bracket is only useful when it changes the order.
We need the sum of two expressions: 5 m minus 3 n, and 7 m minus 2 n. Sum means add them.
Which terms can be put together?

ask.ifNot: Only like terms join, and like terms have the same letter. So the m terms go together, and the n terms go together.

beats.say: The m family first. 5 m and 7 m make 12 m.
Now the n family. Look at the signs. 3 n is taken away. Then 2 n is taken away as well.
Taking away 3 n, and then taking away 2 n more. Altogether, how much is taken away?

ask.ifNot: Think of sweets. I take 3 of your sweets, then 2 more. I have taken 5 altogether. So 5 n is taken away.

beats.say: 3 n and 2 n are both taken away, so 5 n is taken away in all.
So the sum is 12 m minus 5 n.
Test with m as 1 and n as 1. The first bracket is 5 minus 3, which is 2. The second is 7 minus 2, which is 5. Together 7. And 12 minus 5 is 7.
Two take aways do not turn into a plus. They make one bigger take away. The sum is 12 m minus 5 n.
Write down every prime number between 1 and 100. How many times is the digit 2 used? We need the primes that have a 2 in them.

board.text: Primes from 1 to 100: how many times is 2 used?

beats.say: A 2 can sit in the ones place or in the tens place. Take the ones place first. Any number that ends in 2 is even.
Which is the only prime number that ends in 2?

ask.ifNot: 12 and 22 are even, so 2 divides them and they are not prime. The only even prime is 2 itself.

beats.say: So the ones place gives us one 2: the prime number 2.
Now the tens place: the numbers from 20 to 29. The even ones are not prime. That leaves the odd ones: 21, 23, 25, 27 and 29.
Careful here. 21 is 3 times 7. 25 is 5 times 5. 27 is 3 times 9. None of those is prime.
23 and 29 are prime, and each has one 2. So the primes with a 2 are 2, 23 and 29. That is 3 times.
The trap is counting numbers like 12 and 22. They have a 2 in them, but they are not prime. And do not forget the prime 2 itself.
6 years ago, the ages of a husband and wife added up to 48. Now the husband, wife and son add up to 63. What will the son's age be, 6 years hence?
Three different times are mixed up here: 6 years ago, now, and 6 years from now. The word hence means from now. Let us bring everything to now first.
6 years ago the husband and wife added up to 48. What do the two of them add up to now?

ask.ifNot: The husband is 6 years older now, and the wife is 6 years older too. So add 6 twice.

beats.say: 48, plus 6 for the husband, plus 6 for the wife. That is 60. This is the trap: two people, so we add 6 twice.
Now all three add up to 63. Take away the parents' 60 and the son is left. 63 minus 60 is 3. The son is 3 years old now.
Is 3 our answer?

ask.ifNot: Read the last line again. It asks for the son's age 6 years from now, not his age today.

beats.say: 6 years from now he will be 3 plus 6, which is 9. So the son will be 9 years old.

board.text: The son will be 9 years old

beats.say: So bring every sum to the same time first. And when time moves, add the years once for each person.
Four Roman numerals, and we want the largest. But be careful: not all of them are proper numerals.

board.text: Which Roman numeral has the largest value?

beats.say: C C D has big letters in it. But two Cs stand in front of the D. Is that allowed?

choices: No, only one letter may go in front
ask.ifNot: Only one smaller letter may stand in front of a bigger one. So C C D is not a proper numeral. 300 is written C C C.

beats.say: So C C D is out. And X X X X I X has X four times in a row, which is not allowed either. Out as well.
Now the proper ones. In X L V I, X L is 10 less than 50, so it is 40. Then V I is 6. That makes 46.
X X V I I I is two tens, a five and three ones. That is 28.
46 is more than 28. So the largest is X L V I.
Notice that X L V I is the shortest proper numeral here, and still the largest. Length tells you nothing.
So: rules first, values second.
8 points, named A to H, are marked on a circle. We join every pair. How many line segments can we draw?

board.text: Points A to H on a circle. Join every pair.

spec.note: Every pair of points can be joined, not just neighbours

beats.say: Start at A. It can be joined to B, C, D, E, F, G and H. That is 7 segments.
Now B. It also joins 7 other points. But one of those segments is already drawn. Which one?

ask.ifNot: We already drew the segment from A to B. Going from B back to A is the very same segment, so we must not count it again.

beats.say: So B gives only 6 new segments. C gives 5 new ones, D gives 4, and it keeps shrinking by 1.

board.text: From B: 6   From C: 5   From D: 4

beats.say: E gives 3, F gives 2, and G gives 1. And H? All its segments are drawn already.

board.text: From E: 3   From F: 2   From G: 1   From H: 0

beats.say: Now add them up. 7 plus 6 plus 5 plus 4 plus 3 plus 2 plus 1.
That makes 28. So 28 line segments can be drawn.
A quick check: 8 points, times 7 partners each, then halved because each segment has two ends. That is 28 again.
The 19th of April 2018 was a Thursday. Which days appeared 5 times in that month?

board.text: 19th April 2018 = Thursday. Which days came 5 times?

spec.note: April 2018. Which days came 5 times?

beats.say: April has 30 days. 4 full weeks make 28 days, so 2 days are left over.
In 4 full weeks every day comes 4 times. The 2 extra dates, the 29th and 30th, give two days a 5th turn. They fall on the same days as the 1st and 2nd.
So we need the day of the 1st of April. Go back from Thursday the 19th in sevens: the 12th and the 5th are Thursdays too.
The 5th is a Thursday. Count back day by day. What day is the 1st?

ask.ifNot: Step back from Thursday the 5th. The 4th is Wednesday, the 3rd is Tuesday, the 2nd is Monday, and the 1st is Sunday.

beats.say: The 4th is a Wednesday, the 3rd a Tuesday, the 2nd a Monday, and the 1st a Sunday.
So the 29th is a Sunday and the 30th is a Monday. Those are the two days that came 5 times.
Check the Sundays: the 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th. Five of them.
A month of 30 days has just 2 extra days. So exactly 2 days come 5 times: the days of the 1st and the 2nd.
We are hunting for a pair of fractions that are not equal in value. Let's test the pairs one by one.
First pair: 14 over 21 and 8 over 12. Divide 14 and 21 by 7. Divide 8 and 12 by 4. Both become two thirds, so they are equal.
Another pair: 15 over 20 and 9 over 12. Divide by 5, and divide by 3. Both become three quarters. Equal too.
Now 7 over 15 and 14 over 45. The top went from 7 to 14, so it was doubled. Was the bottom doubled too?

ask.ifNot: Double 15 is 30. But the bottom here is 45, which is 15 times 3. So the top and the bottom were not treated the same.

beats.say: Double 15 is 30. So 7 over 15 equals 14 over 30. But this pair has 14 over 45.
The top was multiplied by 2, but the bottom by 3. That breaks the rule, so this pair is not equivalent.
And since we did find an odd pair, the choice that says none of these is out.
The rule for equal fractions: multiply or divide the top and the bottom by the very same number.
Two numbers are given in words. We write them in figures, subtract, and then find the digit in the ten thousands place.

board.text: Difference of the two numbers: ten thousands digit = ?

beats.say: Ninety seven lakh, forty three thousand, seven hundred fifty three. In figures that is 97,43,753.
Forty nine thousand, six hundred eighty two is 49,682.
Now subtract. Line the numbers up by place, ones under ones, and take care with the borrowing.
The difference is 96,94,071. Counting from the right, which seat is the ten thousands place?

ask.ifNot: Count them: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands. That is the 5th seat from the right.

beats.say: Count the seats of 96,94,071 from the right: 1, 7, 0, 4, and then 9.

spec.note: The ten thousands place

beats.say: So the digit in the ten thousands place is 9.
Careful: there are two 9s in the answer, and a 0 too. Always count the seats from the right, one at a time.
Use every one-digit prime number, once each, to make the greatest odd number.

board.text: Use all the one-digit primes. Greatest odd number = ?

beats.say: First, which are the one-digit primes?

ask.ifNot: 9 is 3 times 3, so it is not prime. 1 is not prime either. And do not forget 2, the only even prime.

beats.say: So our digits are 2, 3, 5 and 7.
For the greatest number, we put the biggest digits first. That would give 7532. But look at the end: it finishes in 2, so it is even.
The number must be odd. Keep 7 and 5 at the front. Which digit must go last: 3 or 2?

ask.ifNot: An odd number must end in an odd digit. 2 is even, so the 3 goes last.

beats.say: So 7, then 5, then 2, and 3 at the end. The greatest odd number is 7523.
Two traps. 9 is not prime, so it cannot be used. And 7325 is odd too, but it is smaller, because 5 hundreds beats 3 hundreds.
Look at 73251. Two of its digits change places, and then 6 must divide the new number exactly. Which two digits?
6 is 2 times 3. So a number that 6 divides must pass two tests: the test for 2, and the test for 3.
Test for 3: add the digits. 7 plus 3 plus 2 plus 5 plus 1 is 18, and 18 is in the 3 times table. Swapping digits never changes the sum, so this test is always passed.
Test for 2: the number must be even. So what kind of digit must be at the end?

ask.ifNot: Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. So the last digit has to be even.

beats.say: Look at the digits: 7, 3, 2, 5, 1. Only one of them is even: the 2. So the 2 must move to the end, where the 1 is now.
Swap the 2 and the 1, and we get 73152. It ends in 2, so it is even, and its digits still add to 18.
The trap is swapping the 2 with some other digit, or leaving it where it is. Then the number still ends in an odd digit, and 6 can never divide an odd number.
Remember: divisible by 6 means divisible by 2 and by 3. Check the digit sum for 3, and the last digit for 2.
Here is our equation. 15, minus 3 x, equals x, minus 9. Something is being taken away on each side.
Here is the key idea. Things that are taken away are cleared by adding. Let's start with the minus 3 x.
What do we do to both sides to clear the minus 3 x?

ask.ifNot: The 3 x is being taken away. Adding 3 x puts it back, and the two cancel. So we add 3 x to both sides.

beats.say: We add 3 x to both sides. The left is just 15. On the right, x and 3 x make 4 x.
Now the minus 9 on the right. How do we clear it?

ask.ifNot: Same idea again. The 9 is being taken away, so we clear it by adding 9 to both sides.

beats.say: 15 plus 9 is 24. So 24 equals 4 x.
Careful: x and 3 x made 4 x, so we divide by 4, not by 2. 24 divided by 4 is 6. So x equals 6.
Let's check in our middle line. 4 times 6 is 24, and 24 minus 9 is 15. It works!
So whenever something is being taken away, clear it by adding the same thing to both sides.

board.text: 8 circles in a rectangle: 2 rows of 4

spec.note: One circle fits in each square. Radius = 6 cm. Perimeter = ?

beats.say: Eight equal circles sit in a rectangle in 2 rows of 4, touching each other and the sides. Each radius is 6 centimetres. Find the perimeter of the rectangle.

ask.ifNot: 6 centimetres only reaches from the centre to the edge. From edge to edge is the diameter, two radii.

beats.say: The circles fill the rectangle from side to side. How much room does one circle take, from edge to edge?

spec.note: Diameter = 2 × 6

beats.say: That's the first trap: use the diameter, not the radius. 2 times 6 is 12 centimetres.

spec.note: The length holds 4 circles, the breadth holds 2

beats.say: The length holds 4 circles: 4 times 12 is 48. The breadth holds 2 circles: 2 times 12 is 24.

ask.ifNot: One length and one breadth cover only two of the four sides. The other two sides are still to come.

beats.say: Now the perimeter. Length plus breadth is 48 plus 24, which is 72. Are we finished?
72 is only halfway round. That's the second trap! Double it: 2 times 72 is 144.
The perimeter of the rectangle is 144 centimetres.
Two things to remember: a circle takes up its diameter, and a perimeter goes round all four sides.
We use 3, 4, 5 and 7, once each. We count the numbers that are odd and also greater than 5000.

board.text: Digits 3, 4, 5, 7 once each: odd numbers above 5000?

beats.say: Two rules. To be greater than 5000, the first digit must be 5 or 7. To be odd, the last digit must be 3, 5 or 7.
Suppose the first digit is 5. Which digits can go last?

ask.ifNot: The 5 is already used in the first seat, and each digit is used only once. So the last digit can be 3 or 7.

beats.say: This is the key idea. A digit used in front cannot be used again at the end.
Start with 5 and end with 3: the middle is 4 and 7, in 2 orders. Start with 5 and end with 7: the middle is 3 and 4, in 2 orders.
That is 4 numbers starting with 5. Starting with 7 works the same way: the last digit is 3 or 5.
4 numbers start with 5 and 4 start with 7. That makes 8.
So: fix the first digit, then the last, then count the middle. And never use a digit twice.
Star over 19 equals 6 and 15 over 19. Which number is the star?
6 and 15 over 19 is a mixed number. We must turn it into nineteenths only. The star is how many nineteenths there are altogether.
How many nineteenths are in 1 whole?

ask.ifNot: A whole cut into 19 equal pieces has 19 of them. So 1 whole is 19 nineteenths.

beats.say: So 6 wholes are 6 times 19. Let's split it up: 6 times 10 is 60, and 6 times 9 is 54. Together that is 114.
We have 114 nineteenths from the wholes. What about the 15 over 19?

ask.ifNot: The mixed number has 15 extra nineteenths, as well as the 6 wholes. So we add 15.

beats.say: 114 plus 15 is 129.
So the star is 129.
The rule: wholes times the bottom, plus the top. That gives the new top, and the bottom stays the same.
We multiply the decimal 0.0357 by 100.
100 has two zeros. So what does multiplying by 100 do to the digits?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying makes a number bigger, so the digits move left, into bigger places. Two zeros means two places.

beats.say: Let's go one place at a time. One place to the left: 0.0357 becomes 0.357.

spec.note: One place: 0.0357 becomes 0.357

beats.say: Now one more place to the left. What does 0.357 become?

ask.ifNot: Each digit moves just one place more. The 3 moves from the tenths into the ones, and no new digit appears between the others.

beats.say: 0.357 becomes 3.57. So the answer is 3.57.

spec.note: One more place: 0.0357 × 100 = 3.57

beats.say: Look at the digits: 3, 5, 7, in the same order, with nothing new between them. Only their places have changed.
A quick check: 0.0357 is close to 0.04, and 0.04 times 100 is 4. Our 3.57 is near 4. To multiply by 100, move every digit two places to the left.
Five eights and four different signs! It looks like a riddle, but the BODMAS rule sorts it out.
Which two jobs go first?

ask.ifNot: Times and divide go before plus and minus. So 8 times 8, and 8 divided by 8, go first.

beats.say: Box the times and the divide.
8 times 8 is 64. And 8 divided by 8 is 1.
Write the sum again, with 64 and 1 where the boxes were. The 8 at the front is still there.
Left to right now. 8 plus 64 is 72.
And 72 take away 1 is 71.
Two traps here. Going straight along from the left gives a different answer. And do not forget that first 8: it still has to be added.
So: times and divide first, then plus and minus from left to right.
A four-digit number: 9, star, 8, star. Both stars are the same digit, and 9 divides the number exactly. Which digit is the star?

spec.note: Both stars are the same digit.

beats.say: The test for 9: add up all the digits. If the total is in the 9 times table, then 9 divides the number.
The digits we know are 9 and 8. They add up to 17.
The two stars are the same digit. So together they add up to double that digit, and a double is always an even number.
The total must land in the 9 times table: 18, 27 or 36. For that, the stars must add 1, 10 or 19. Which of those can two equal digits make?

ask.ifNot: Two equal digits always add up to an even number. 1 and 19 are odd, so it must be 10.

beats.say: The two stars add up to 10, and half of 10 is 5. So each star is 5.
Let's check. The digits add up to 27, which is in the 9 times table. And the number is 9,585, which is 9 times 1065.
One trap: adding 1 just once would reach the 9 times table. But the star is there twice, so whatever we add is added twice.
In how many ways can 136 be written as one number times another? Each way is a pair of factors of 136.

spec.note: How many pairs multiply to 136?

beats.say: Start small. 1 times 136 is the first way. 136 is even, and half of it is 68. So 2 times 68 is the second way.
Try 3. The digits of 136 add up to 10, which is not in the 3 times table. So 3 does not divide it.
Try 4. For 4, look at the last two digits: 36. Does 4 divide 36?

ask.ifNot: 4 times 9 is 36. So 4 divides 136 as well.

beats.say: 4 times 34 is 136. Then 5, 6 and 7 do not divide 136. But 8 does: 8 times 17 is 136.
After 8, the next factor is 17, and that is already on the board as a partner. Going on would only repeat the pairs backwards.
So there are 4 ways.
Two traps. 17 times 8 is the same way as 8 times 17, so do not count it twice. And do not leave out 1 times 136.
We need to write 1997 the Roman way. Romans had no place seats like ours, so first we break the number into parts.
Split it by place: 1000, 900, 90 and 7.
Here are the 7 Roman letters and what each one is worth. Keep them in view.

spec.note: and V = 5, I = 1

beats.say: 1000 is simply M. 900 is 100 less than 1000, so the smaller letter goes in front: C M.
Now the 90. How do the Romans write 90?

ask.ifNot: A letter can repeat only 3 times, so L X X X X is not allowed. 90 is 10 less than 100: X before C.

beats.say: 90 is 10 less than 100, so the smaller letter goes in front: X C.
7 is 5 and 2 more, so we write V I I.
Now join the parts in order, biggest first: M, C M, X C, V I I.
The same rule made our 900. Not D C C C C, but C before M. Short and neat.
So the plan for any number: split it by place, write each part in Roman letters, then join them from left to right.

board.text: Which pair of angles is complementary?

beats.say: 4 pairs of angles, and only one pair is complementary. Let's test them one at a time.

ask.ifNot: A square corner is a right angle, and a right angle is 90 degrees. So the pair must add up to 90.

beats.say: Complementary angles fit together into a square corner. So what must the pair add up to?
First pair: 55 and 45. The two 5s make 10, and 50 and 40 make 90. So that is 100. Too big.

ask.ifNot: 80 from the tens, and 10 more from the two 5s. 80 and 10 make 90.

beats.say: Second pair: 65 and 25. The two 5s make 10 again, and 60 and 20 make 80. So what is the total?
65 plus 25 is exactly 90. That is the pair we want.
A careful mathematician checks the rest. 35 and 48 make 83. 17 and 63 make 80. Neither is 90.
So the complementary pair is 65 degrees and 25 degrees.
The first pair was the tempting one, because 55 and 45 look so neat. But they make 100. Always do the adding.
We add something to 710 to reach a square number. So we need the first square above 710.

spec.note: How far is the next square?

beats.say: Where to start? 25 times 25 is 625, too small. 30 times 30 is 900, too big.
Try 26. 26 times 26 is 676. Still below 710.
676 is still below 710. What should we try next?

ask.ifNot: We need a square above 710, so we go up one more, to 27 times 27.

beats.say: 27 times 27: 27 times 20 is 540 and 27 times 7 is 189. Together, 729. That is above 710!
The gap from 710 up to 729 is 19.
Check: 710 plus 19 is 729, which is 27 times 27.
Careful: landing near 729 is not enough. A square has to be hit exactly.
p is 7, and q is p minus 3. We want the value of 5 p, plus 6 q, minus 12.
Before we can use q, we need its number. What is q?

ask.ifNot: q is p minus 3. And p is 7. So q is 7 minus 3.

beats.say: q is 7 minus 3, which is 4.
Now 5 p. That is 5 times 7, which is 35. Careful: that is only the first part, not the answer.
Next, 6 q. That is 6 times 4, which is 24.
We have 35 and 24, and there is still the 12. How do they go together?

ask.ifNot: Look at the signs in the expression. There is a plus in front of 6 q, and a minus in front of 12. So add 24, then take away 12.

beats.say: 35 plus 24 is 59. Then 59 minus 12 is 47.
So the value is 47. Find q first, work out each part, then join the parts with their own signs.
The series is 5, 14, 25, 38, then a star, then 70 and 89. This time the hidden number is in the middle.
Find the jumps we can see. 5 to 14 is 9. 14 to 25 is 11. 25 to 38 is 13.
The jumps are 9, 11, 13. What is the next jump?

ask.ifNot: Each jump is 2 more than the one before. After 13 comes 15.

beats.say: The jumps grow by 2, so the next one is 15. And 38 plus 15 is 53.
Here is the good part. The numbers after the star let us check. The next jumps should be 17 and 19.
53 plus 17 is 70. And 70 plus 19 is 89. Both match the series!
So the star stands for 53.
A number in the middle has to fit on both sides. Always test your answer against the numbers that come after it.
Here is our equation. 31, minus T, equals 2 T, plus 7. The letter T is on both sides.
On the left, one T is being taken away. Let's clear it, so that all the T are on the right.
What do we add to both sides?

ask.ifNot: One T is being taken away on the left. Adding one T to both sides cancels it.

beats.say: We add T to both sides. The left is just 31. On the right, 2 T and 1 more T make 3 T.
Next, the plus 7. What do we do?

ask.ifNot: The 7 is added on the right. To undo adding, we take away. So 7 comes off both sides.

beats.say: 31 minus 7 is 24. So 24 equals 3 T.
Careful: 24 is 3 T, not T. We divide both sides by 3. 24 divided by 3 is 8. So T equals 8.
Let's check. Left: 31 minus 8 is 23. Right: 2 times 8, plus 7, is also 23. Both sides match.
So bring the letters together first, by adding the one that is taken away. Then solve the two steps.

board.text: Square: perimeter 36 cm. 3 squares joined in a row.

spec.note: Each square has a perimeter of 36 cm

beats.say: A square has a perimeter of 36 centimetres. Three such squares are joined in a straight row to make a rectangle. What is the rectangle's perimeter?
Tempting idea: 3 squares, so 3 times 36. Do you think that's right? Think about the edges where the squares join.
That's the trap! Where two squares join, those edges end up inside the rectangle. They are not on the boundary any more.
So let's find the real sides. One side of a square is 36 divided by 4, which is 9 centimetres.

ask.ifNot: Three sides of 9 centimetres sit end to end along the length. So we need 3 lots of 9.

beats.say: Three squares side by side. How long is the rectangle?
3 times 9 is 27. The rectangle is 27 centimetres long and still 9 centimetres wide.
27 plus 9 is 36. That is halfway round. Double it: 72.
The perimeter of the rectangle is 72 centimetres.
So when shapes are joined, don't add their perimeters. Find the new sides, then go round the outside.
In this 3 by 3 magic square, every row, column and diagonal adds up to 54. Which number can be in the central box?

board.text: 3 by 3 magic square.  Every line adds up to 54.

spec.note: Every line of 3 boxes adds up to 54

beats.say: Let's learn from a magic square we know well. This one uses 1 to 9. Every line adds up to 15, and the centre is 5.

spec.note: Every line adds up to 15

beats.say: Look at 15 and 5. How is the centre related to the line total?

choices: it is one third of it
ask.ifNot: 3 times 5 is 15. So the centre is the line total divided by 3.

beats.say: 15 divided by 3 is 5. And this is true for every 3 by 3 magic square: the centre is the line total divided by 3.
So divide 54 by 3. Split 54 into 30 and 24. 30 divided by 3 is 10, and 24 divided by 3 is 8. Together that is 18.
Check: three 18s make 54. So the central box holds 18.
Careful not to halve the total. A line has 3 boxes, so the centre is one third of it, not one half.
Remember this for any 3 by 3 magic square: the line total is 3 times the centre, and the centre is the line total divided by 3.
Two mystery numbers with three digits each. One ends in 7, the other ends in 6. Which choice could be their product?
We cannot multiply them, but we can rule choices out, like detectives. Here are the four.
Clue one: the last digit. 7 times 6 is 42. So what must the product end in?

ask.ifNot: 7 times 6 is 42, and 42 ends in 2. So the product must end in 2.

beats.say: It must end in 2. But 51276 ends in 6, so cross it off.
Clue two: the size. Each number has three digits, so each is at least 100. And 100 times 100 is 10000, which has five digits.
So the product has at least five digits. 1342 has only four. Too small, so cross it off.
Each number is also less than 1000. And 1000 times 1000 is 1000000, which has seven digits. So the product has fewer than seven digits.
9933012 has seven digits. Too big, so cross it off.
Only 312312 is left. It ends in 2, and it has six digits, which is just right.
The key idea: check the last digit, then count the digits. No long multiplying needed.
A boy celebrated his 10th birthday on the 15th of April 2019, which was a Monday. On which day of the week will his 12th birthday fall?

spec.note: 10th birthday on a Monday. 12th birthday: ?

beats.say: The 10th birthday is in 2019. In which year is the 12th birthday?

ask.ifNot: From the 10th birthday to the 12th is 2 years. 2019 plus 2 is 2021.

beats.say: 2019 plus 2 is 2021. So we move forward two years, one at a time.
An ordinary year moves a date on by 1 day of the week. But if a 29th of February lies in between, the date moves on by 2.

board.text: No leap day: + 1.    29 February in between: + 2

beats.say: From April 2019 to April 2020, do we pass a 29th of February?

ask.ifNot: 2020 is a leap year, and its February comes before April. So the 29th of February 2020 lies between the two birthdays.

beats.say: So the first year moves the day on by 2. Monday becomes Wednesday. That is the 11th birthday.
From April 2020 to April 2021 there is no leap day. The day moves on by 1, and Wednesday becomes Thursday.
Check: 2 plus 1 is 3 days on from Monday. Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday. Go one year at a time, and look for a leap day in between.

board.text: Two angles are given. Which triangle is isosceles?

beats.say: Each choice gives 2 angles of a triangle. Which pair can belong to an isosceles triangle?
Isosceles means 2 equal angles. We see only 2 of the 3 angles each time, so we find the hidden third angle and look for a twin.
A: 90 plus 50 is 140, and 180 minus 140 is 40. The angles are 90, 50 and 40. All different.
B: 80 plus 40 is 120, and 180 minus 120 is 60. The angles are 80, 40 and 60. All different again.

ask.ifNot: The third angle is 180 minus 125. That leaves 55.

beats.say: C: 55 plus 70 is 125. What is the third angle?
55! And the pair already has a 55. A twin. The angles are 55, 70 and 55.
Check D to be safe. 60 plus 40 is 100, and 180 minus 100 is 80. All different.
So the pair is 55 degrees and 70 degrees.
The twin was hiding in the third angle. Always find it before you decide.
Ajay writes the multiples of 4 up to 100. Vijay writes the multiples of 5 up to 100. How many numbers are in both notebooks?

board.text: Multiples of 4 and of 5, up to 100. In both = ?

beats.say: A number in both notebooks is a multiple of 4 and of 5. Count up in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. The first one that 4 divides is 20.
So the numbers in both notebooks go up in steps of what?

ask.ifNot: Every number in both tables is a multiple of 20, the lowest common multiple. So they go up in steps of 20.

beats.say: That is 5 numbers. Or work it out: 100 divided by 20 is 5.
Two traps. 10 is in Vijay's notebook but not in Ajay's, so do not count in tens. And 20 is the smallest common number, not how many there are.
So for numbers in two tables at once: find the L C M, and count its multiples.
A square. Each side is 4 x minus 3 y centimetres. We want an expression for its perimeter.

spec.note: Perimeter = ?

beats.say: A square has 4 equal sides. So its perimeter is 4 times one side.
Look at the 4 outside the bracket. What does it multiply?

ask.ifNot: All four sides are the whole of 4 x minus 3 y. So every part of the side is multiplied by 4.

beats.say: 4 times 4 x is 16 x.
And 4 times 3 y is 12 y.
In each side, 3 y is taken away. So in the perimeter, is 12 y added or taken away?

ask.ifNot: Each of the 4 sides loses 3 y. Four lots of losing 3 y is losing 12 y. So the minus stays.

beats.say: So the perimeter is 16 x minus 12 y centimetres.
Test with x as 1 and y as 1. A side is 4 minus 3, which is 1, so the perimeter is 4. Our answer gives 16 minus 12, also 4.
x and y are different letters, so they stay apart. Multiply each by 4, and keep the minus between them.
7 kilograms 70 grams. Let's write that weight as a single decimal number of kilograms.
The 7 kilograms stay. Only the 70 grams need changing. 1000 grams make 1 kilogram, so we divide 70 by 1000.
What is 70 divided by 1000?

ask.ifNot: Dividing by 1000 slides the digits 3 places to the right. The 7 lands in the hundredths place.

beats.say: 70 divided by 1000 is 0.07. The 7 sits in the hundredths place.
Careful, this is where many people slip. 0.70 kilograms would be 700 grams, ten times too much. And 0.007 would be just 7 grams.
Now add the 7 whole kilograms. 7 plus 0.07 is 7.07.
So 7 kilograms 70 grams is 7.07 kilograms.
So the rule is: divide the grams by 1000, then check the place of every digit before you choose.
Three and a quarter dozen. That means 3 whole dozens, and then a quarter of a dozen more. We do each part.
One dozen is 12. So 3 dozen is 3 times 12, which is 36.
Now a quarter of a dozen. A quarter means one of 4 equal parts. So what is a quarter of 12?

ask.ifNot: Split 12 into 4 equal parts. 12 divided by 4 is 3. So a quarter of a dozen is 3.

beats.say: 12 divided by 4 is 3. So a quarter of a dozen is 3 articles.
Now put the two parts together. 36 plus 3 is 39.
Careful with the trap. A quarter does not mean add 4. It means divide by 4.
So: the whole dozens first, then the part of a dozen, then add them.
Find the H C F of 39 and 65. H C F means highest common factor: the biggest number that divides both 39 and 65 exactly.
Before we start, a quick thought. Could the H C F be bigger than 39?

ask.ifNot: A factor has to fit inside the number it divides. So the H C F can never be bigger than 39, the smaller of our two numbers.

beats.say: Here is the plan. These numbers have only a few factors, so we list every factor of each one. Then we look for the biggest number in both lists.
Factors come in pairs that multiply to make 39: 1 times 39 and 3 times 13. So the factors of 39 are 1, 3, 13 and 39.
Do the same for 65. The pairs are 1 times 65 and 5 times 13. That gives the factors of 65: 1, 5, 13 and 65.
Now look along both lists. Which is the biggest number that is in both of them?

ask.ifNot: It has to be in both lists, not just one. Check each number against the other list, and take the biggest one that is in both.

beats.say: The numbers in both lists are 1 and 13. These are the common factors, and the biggest is 13. Careful: 39 is in its own list, but it does not divide 65, so it is out.
In the picture, the middle part holds the factors they share. The biggest one there is 13, so the H C F is 13.

spec.note: The middle holds the common factors.

beats.say: Let's check. 39 divided by 13 is 3, and 65 divided by 13 is 5. Nothing is left over either time.
So the plan for an H C F like this one: list the factors of each number, find the ones in both lists, and take the biggest. Your turn next!

board.text: Angle between the hands = 45°. What time is it?

beats.say: The teacher's watch shows an angle of 45 degrees between its hands. We have 4 times to choose from, so let's test them.
On a clock, the full turn of 360 degrees is shared by 12 numbers. So each gap between two numbers is 30 degrees.
45 degrees is one whole gap of 30, and half a gap, 15, more. So we want hands that are 1 and a half gaps apart.

ask.ifNot: In half an hour, the hour hand goes half of the way to the next number. So at half past 7 it sits halfway between the 7 and the 8.

beats.say: Three of the times are half past something. At half past, the minute hand is on the 6. But where is the hour hand at half past 7?
That is the trap: the hour hand does not wait on the 7. Now count from the 6. From 6 to 7 is one gap. Then half a gap more. 1 and a half gaps!
And 1 and a half gaps is 45 degrees. So half past 7 fits.
Now the others. At half past 8 the hour hand is one gap further on: 2 and a half gaps, 75 degrees. At half past 2 it is 3 and a half gaps from the 6. Both are too wide.
And at quarter past 1, the minute hand is on the 3 and the hour hand is a little past the 1. That is nearly 2 gaps, which is more than 45 degrees.
So the time is 7:30.
With clock angles, count gaps of 30 degrees. And always ask: where has the hour hand crept to?
Here is 3,62,489. We want to know how much its 6 is really worth.

spec.note: How much is the 6 worth?

beats.say: Count the seats from the right: 9 is in the ones, 8 in the tens, 4 in the hundreds and 2 in the thousands.
The 6 comes next. Which seat is it in?

ask.ifNot: After the thousands seat comes the ten-thousands seat. The 2 is in the thousands, so the 6 is in the ten-thousands.

beats.say: The ten-thousands seat is worth 10,000. So we multiply 6 by 10,000.
6 times 10,000 is 60,000. That is the place value of the 6.
Careful: 6 on its own is just the face value. The place value counts the seat as well.
A quick check: 4 digits come after the 6, so its value is a 6 followed by 4 zeros.
The successor of a number is the very next number. So we add 1 to 99,999.
What happens to a 9 when we add 1 to it?

choices: it becomes 10 in the same seat
ask.ifNot: 9 plus 1 is 10. A seat can hold only one digit, so we write 0 and carry the 1 to the next seat.

beats.say: The 9 in the ones becomes 0 and carries 1. That carry turns the next 9 into 0 as well, and so on, like falling dominoes.
All five 9s become 0, and the last carry makes a brand new 1 in front.
So the successor is 1,00,000. That is one lakh.
Notice that it has 6 digits now. The largest 5-digit number, plus 1, is the smallest 6-digit number.
Careful: 99,998 is the number before. Successor means after, so we add.
4 numbers that look very alike. To find the largest, we compare them seat by seat, starting from the left.
All four start with 4 and then 5. So the first two seats are a tie, and we move on to the hundreds.
The hundreds digits are 0, 3, 3 and 2. Which numbers are still in the race?

ask.ifNot: The biggest hundreds digit is 3. Two numbers have it: 45,302 and 45,320.

beats.say: 3 is the biggest hundreds digit, so 45,032 and 45,203 drop out.
Now compare the tens of the two that are left. 45,302 has 0 tens. 45,320 has 2 tens.
So the largest is 45,320.
So the plan: start at the left, and move one seat to the right only when there is a tie.
Here is a Roman numeral: C D X L I V. We need to turn it into our own numbers.
Here is what each Roman letter is worth.

spec.note: and V = 5, I = 1

beats.say: The secret: when a smaller letter stands before a bigger one, we take it away. This numeral is made of 3 pairs like that.
Take the first pair. C is 100 and D is 500, and the C comes first. So what is C D worth?

ask.ifNot: The smaller letter is in front, so we take it away: 500 minus 100 is 400.

beats.say: 500 minus 100 is 400. So C D is 400.
The next pairs work the same way. X L is 50 minus 10, which is 40. I V is 5 minus 1, which is 4.
Now add the three parts: 400 and 40 and 4.
So C D X L I V is 444.
Careful: if you add every pair instead of taking away, each part comes out too big. Smaller letter in front means take away.
We need to write 789 the Roman way. Romans had no place seats like ours, so first we break the number into parts.
Split it by place: 700, 80 and 9.
Here are the 7 Roman letters and what each one is worth. Keep them in view.

spec.note: and V = 5, I = 1

beats.say: 700 is 500 and 2 more hundreds, so we write D C C.
Now the 80. How do the Romans write 80?

ask.ifNot: 80 is 50 and 3 more tens. So we write L, and then three Xs.

beats.say: 80 is 50 and 3 more tens, so we write L X X X.
9 is 1 less than 10, so the smaller letter goes in front: I X.
Now join the parts in order, biggest first: D C C, L X X X, I X.
Count the Xs carefully. L X X is only 70, and X C is 90.
So the plan for any number: split it by place, write each part in Roman letters, then join them from left to right.
We round 4,567 to the nearest hundred. First: which two hundreds does it sit between?

spec.note: Which hundred is nearer?

beats.say: It is between 4,500 and 4,600.
To choose between them, which digit of 4,567 do we look at?

ask.ifNot: To round to the hundreds, look at the digit just to the right of the hundreds. That is the tens digit, 6.

beats.say: The tens digit is 6. The rule: 5 or more, round up. Less than 5, round down.
6 is more than 5, so we round up to 4,600.
It makes sense: 4,567 is past the halfway mark, 4,550, so it is nearer to 4,600.
Careful: 4,570 is rounding to the nearest ten. For the nearest hundred, the last two digits both become 0.
How many digits does 5,43,21,678 have? The commas make it easy to count in groups.
The commas split the number into 4 groups: 5, then 43, then 21, then 678.
How many digits are in the last group, 678?

ask.ifNot: 6, 7 and 8. That is 3 digits. In the Indian system the last group always has 3 digits.

beats.say: So the groups have 1, 2, 2 and 3 digits. Add them up.
The number has 8 digits.
Careful: commas are not digits. Count only the digits between them.
Check: write it without commas, 54321678, and count. 8 digits.
Expanded form means we break 30,507 into the value of each digit, and write the values as a sum.
The 3 is in the ten-thousands place, so it is worth 30,000.
Next is a 0 in the thousands place. What does it add to the number?

ask.ifNot: 0 thousands is nothing at all. The zero only holds the seat, so that the 3 stays in the ten-thousands place.

beats.say: A zero adds nothing, so we skip it. The 5 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 500.
Another 0 in the tens, so we skip again. The 7 is in the ones, so it is worth 7.
Put the three values together as a sum.
Careful: 30,000 plus 507 also makes 30,507, but 507 is not fully broken up. Expanded form splits every digit.
Ascending means going up, smallest first. All 4 numbers use the same digits, so we compare them seat by seat.
All four have 5 thousands, so that is a tie. Look at the hundreds digits: 4, 3, 4 and 2.
Which number has the smallest hundreds digit?

ask.ifNot: The hundreds digits are 4, 3, 4 and 2. The smallest is 2, and that belongs to 5,234.

beats.say: 5,234 is the smallest, with 2 hundreds. Next is 5,342, with 3 hundreds.
Two numbers have 4 hundreds: 5,432 and 5,423. Break the tie with the tens. 2 tens is less than 3 tens, so 5,423 comes first.
So from smallest to largest, here is the order.
Careful: descending is the other way round, largest first. Always check which order is asked for.
Three signs in one sum: a minus, a times and a plus. The trick is knowing where to start.
So, which bit goes first?

ask.ifNot: Times goes before plus and minus, even when it sits in the middle. So we begin with 3 times 7.

beats.say: Times is the boss here. It goes before plus and minus, so put a box round 3 times 7.
3 times 7 is 21. Write 21 in its place, and copy everything else just as it was.
Now only a minus and a plus are left. Which do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 48 take away 21.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 48 take away 21 is 27.
And now the plus. 27 plus 14 is 41.
Did you spot the trap? Going left to right from the very start would mean taking away before multiplying, and that gives a different number.
So remember: times first, then plus and minus from left to right.
We have the digits 7, 0, 3 and 5, and we use each one once. We want the largest number we can build.
Which seat matters most for making a number large?

ask.ifNot: The seat on the far left is worth the most. One thousand beats all the hundreds, tens and ones we could put here.

beats.say: So the biggest digit, 7, goes in the thousands seat.
Then the next biggest, 5, in the hundreds. Then 3 in the tens. And 0 is left for the ones.
The largest number is 7,530.
Careful: 7,503 looks close. But 3 tens and 0 ones is more than 0 tens and 3 ones.
So for the largest number, write the digits from biggest to smallest.
The predecessor is the number just before. So we take 1 away from 10,000.

spec.note: One step back

beats.say: Will the answer have 5 digits, like 10,000?

ask.ifNot: 10,000 is the smallest 5-digit number. Anything before it must have fewer digits, so the answer has 4 digits.

beats.say: 10,000 is the smallest number with 5 digits. One step back, and we land on the largest number with 4 digits.
The largest 4-digit number has a 9 in every seat.
So the predecessor is 9,999.
Check by adding back: 9,999 plus 1 is 10,000.
Careful: 10,001 is the successor, the number after. Predecessor means before.
In 4,562, the digit 5 has two values: a place value and a face value. We want the difference between them.

board.text: 4,562: place value of 5 − face value of 5 = ?

beats.say: Which of these is the face value of the 5?

ask.ifNot: Face value is the easy one. It is just the digit itself, wherever it sits. So the face value is 5.

beats.say: The face value is simply 5.
For the place value, find the seat. From the right: 2 ones, 6 tens, 5 hundreds. So it is 5 times 100, which is 500.
Now the difference: 500 minus 5 is 495.
Careful: 500 and 5 are both among the choices. But the question wants the difference between them.
So remember: place value uses the seat, and face value ignores it.
One of these four is not a proper Roman numeral. Each one puts a smaller letter in front of a bigger one, so let us check that rule.

board.text: Which is NOT a valid Roman numeral?

beats.say: A smaller letter in front means take away. But only I, X and C are allowed to do that.

board.text: May go in front to take away: I, X, C

beats.say: Which letters are never used to take away?

ask.ifNot: The letters V for 5, L for 50 and D for 500 are never put in front to take away.

beats.say: X L has X in front of L, and X is allowed. That is 50 minus 10, which is 40. Fine.
X I V has I in front of V. Allowed, and it is 14. I X is 9. Both are fine.
In V X, the V stands in front of X. But V is never used to take away. So V X is not valid.
And there is no need for it. 10 minus 5 is 5, and 5 already has its own letter, V.
To estimate this sum, we round each number to the nearest thousand first, and then add the round numbers.
To round 4,891 to the nearest thousand, which digit do we check?

ask.ifNot: Look one seat to the right of the thousands. That is the hundreds digit, which is 8.

beats.say: The hundreds digit is 8. That is 5 or more, so 4,891 rounds up to 5,000.
For 3,207 the hundreds digit is 2. That is less than 5, so it rounds down to 3,000.
Now add the round numbers. 5,000 plus 3,000 is 8,000.
Is that sensible? The exact sum is 8,098, which is close to 8,000. A good estimate.
Careful: one number went up and the other went down. Check each number on its own.
We read 23,45,678 in the Indian system. The commas show us the groups, which are called periods.
From the right, the first comma cuts off 3 digits: 678. Then come groups of 2 digits: 45, and then 23.
678 is the ones period and 45 is the thousands period. What is the period of the 23?

ask.ifNot: In the Indian system the periods go: ones, thousands, lakhs, crores. The third group from the right is lakhs.

beats.say: So 23 is in the lakhs period.
Read each group with its name: twenty-three lakh, forty-five thousand, six hundred seventy-eight.
Careful: million belongs to the international system. And a crore needs 8 digits, but this number has only 7.
So: split at the commas, name each period, and read from the left.
We count the even numbers between 11 and 21. Between means that 11 and 21 themselves are not included.

board.text: Even numbers between 11 and 21: how many?

spec.note: The numbers between 11 and 21

beats.say: Which is the first even number after 11?

ask.ifNot: 11 is odd. The very next number, 12, ends in 2, so it is even.

beats.say: Start at 12 and jump in twos: 12, 14, 16, 18, 20.
The next jump would land on 22, which is past 21. So we stop at 20.
Count them. There are 5 even numbers.
Careful: do not forget 20. It is less than 21, so it counts.
So: find the first one, jump in twos, and stop before you pass the end.
We use 9, 0, 3, 1 and 7, once each, to build the smallest 5-digit number.
The smallest digit is 0. Can 0 go in the first seat?

choices: No, then it is not a 5-digit number
ask.ifNot: A number that starts with 0 loses a digit, so it would only be a 4-digit number. The first seat needs the next smallest digit.

beats.say: So the first seat takes the next smallest digit, 1.
Now 0 can take the second seat. It is welcome anywhere except the front.
The rest go from smallest to biggest: 3, 7, 9.
The smallest number is 10,379.
Careful: 13,079 puts the 3 before the 0, and that makes it bigger. Get the 0 in as early as you can.
6 empty seats. We want the smallest number that fills all of them.
We want small digits. What is the smallest digit we can put in the first seat?

ask.ifNot: 0 is smaller, but a number cannot begin with 0. So the first seat gets a 1.

beats.say: The first seat takes 1, because a number cannot begin with 0.
Every other seat takes the smallest digit there is, 0.
With Indian commas, that is 1,00,000. One lakh!
A nice check: it is 1 more than 99,999, the largest 5-digit number.
Careful when you count the zeros: a 1, and then exactly 5 zeros.
Here is a long Roman numeral: M C M X C I X. Let us turn it into our own numbers, one part at a time.
Here is what each Roman letter is worth.

spec.note: and V = 5, I = 1

beats.say: First find the pairs where a smaller letter stands before a bigger one. Those are take away pairs: C M, X C and I X.
The M at the front stands alone, so it is 1000. Next comes C M. C is 100 and M is 1000. What is C M worth?

ask.ifNot: The smaller letter C is in front, so we take it away: 1000 minus 100 is 900.

beats.say: 1000 minus 100 is 900. So far we have 1000 and 900.
X C is 100 minus 10, which is 90. I X is 10 minus 1, which is 9.
Now add the four parts.
So M C M X C I X is 1,999.
Careful with X C. It is 90, not 40. 40 would be X L, with an L for 50.
So the plan: find the take away pairs, work out each part, then add the parts.
Two big numbers, and we want a number that lies between them.
Compare them from the left. Both start with the same three digits: 3, 4, 5. Only the endings differ: 678 and 680.
Which whole number comes between 678 and 680?

ask.ifNot: Count up from 678. The next number is 679, and then comes 680. So 679 is in between.

beats.say: 678, then 679, then 680. Only 679 fits in the gap.

spec.note: Look at the endings

beats.say: Now put the front digits back. The number is 3,45,679.
Check: it is 1 more than 3,45,678 and 1 less than 3,45,680.
Careful: 3,45,677 and 3,45,681 are close neighbours, but they sit outside the gap.
Here is our sum. It has three signs in it: a minus, a times and a plus.
Where do we begin?

ask.ifNot: It is tempting to start on the left. But multiplying always goes first, so 3 times 7 is our first job.

beats.say: Times is the boss here. It goes before plus and minus, so put a box round 3 times 7.
3 times 7 is 21. So 21 goes where the box was. The rest of the sum stays the same.
Now only a minus and a plus are left. Which do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 25 take away 21.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 25 take away 21 is 4.
And now the plus. 4 plus 1 is 5.
The trap in this sum is the minus at the front. It looks like the place to start, but the times must go first.
So remember: times first, then plus and minus from left to right.
In 4,372 we need two things: the place value of the 4 and the face value of the 7. Then we multiply them.
The 4 is the first digit of 4,372. What is its place value?

ask.ifNot: 4,372 has 4 digits, so the first seat is the thousands. 4 thousands is 4,000.

beats.say: The 4 is in the thousands place, so its place value is 4,000.
Face value is just the digit itself. So the face value of 7 is 7, even though it sits in the tens.
Product means multiply. 4 times 7 is 28, so 4,000 times 7 is 28,000.
Careful: do not use 70 for the 7. The question asks for its face value, not its place value.
So: read which value is asked for each digit, and then do the sum.
How many zeros does 5 crore have? Let us build up to a crore, step by step.

board.text: How many zeros are in 5 crore?

beats.say: One thousand has 3 zeros. One lakh has 5 zeros.
A crore is 100 lakh. Multiplying by 100 adds 2 more zeros. So how many zeros are in 1 crore?

ask.ifNot: A lakh has 5 zeros, and times 100 adds 2 more. 5 plus 2 is 7.

beats.say: 1 crore is a 1 followed by 7 zeros.
For 5 crore, the 1 simply becomes a 5. The zeros stay the same.
So 5 crore has 7 zeros.
Careful: the 5 in front changes nothing about the zeros. 5 crore, 7 crore, 9 crore: they all have 7 zeros.
We are told the digit in each seat. Let us put them into a place value chart, biggest seat first.
4 in the ten-thousands, 0 in the thousands, 3 in the hundreds, 0 in the tens and 8 in the ones.
Two seats hold a 0. Can we leave those zeros out when we write the number?

ask.ifNot: A zero adds nothing, but it keeps every other digit in its proper seat. Leave it out, and the 4 slides down to a smaller seat.

beats.say: Zeros are place holders. Without them the 4 would not stay in the ten-thousands place.
Read the seats from left to right. The number is 40,308.
Check by adding the values: 40,000 plus 300 plus 8.
Careful: 4,308 drops a zero and has only 4 digits. And 40,380 puts the 8 in the tens seat.
Which sign goes in the blank: greater than, less than, or equals? We compare the two numbers seat by seat, from the left.
Both have 5 digits. Both have 6 ten-thousands, and both have 5 thousands. Still a tie.
Now the hundreds. The first number has 4 hundreds and the second has 3. Which number is bigger?

ask.ifNot: 4 hundreds is more than 3 hundreds. Once one seat is bigger, the seats to its right cannot change the result.

beats.say: 4 hundreds beats 3 hundreds. We can stop here: the first number is greater.
The sign for greater than opens towards the bigger number.
Careful: the two numbers use the same digits. But it is the order of the digits that matters, not just which digits they are.
So: go from the left, and the first seat that differs decides.
What is the 8th multiple of 9? The multiples of 9 are the numbers in the 9 times table.
The 1st multiple is 9 times 1. The 2nd is 9 times 2. The 3rd is 9 times 3. See the pattern?
So which sum gives the 8th multiple of 9?

ask.ifNot: The 1st multiple is 9 times 1, and the 2nd is 9 times 2. So the 8th multiple is 9 times 8.

beats.say: 9 times 8 is 72. So the 8th multiple of 9 is 72.
Check by counting up in 9s, eight times: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72.
Watch the neighbours. 81 is 9 times 9, the 9th multiple. And 63 is 9 times 7, the 7th multiple.
So the multiple number tells you what to multiply by. Easy!
Just before means 1 less. So we take 1 away from 50,00,000.
50,00,000 ends in 6 zeros. When we take 1 away, what do those zeros become?

ask.ifNot: Think of a smaller sum: 10 minus 1 is 9. The zero has to borrow, and it turns into a 9.

beats.say: It is like 100 minus 1, which is 99. Every zero borrows from its neighbour and turns into a 9.
The 5 in front lends 1 and becomes 4. And all 6 zeros become 9s.
So the number just before is 49,99,999.
Careful: count the 9s. There must be 6 of them, so the answer still has 7 digits.
We use 5, 3, 8 and 1, once each. We want the largest number, but it must be even.
An even number must end in an even digit. Which of our digits are even?

ask.ifNot: 5, 3 and 1 are odd. The only even digit we have is 8.

beats.say: Only 8 is even. So 8 has to go in the ones seat, like it or not.
This is the trap. We would love to put 8 in front, but then the number would end in an odd digit.
The other digits fill the front, biggest first: 5, 3, 1.
The largest even number is 5,318.
Careful: 8,531 is the largest number from these digits, but it ends in 1, so it is odd.
Adding Roman numerals is hard. So we change them into our own numbers, add, and change back.
X I V is a ten and a four. That is 14.
X X V I I I is two tens, a five and three ones. That is 28.
Add them. 14 plus 28 is 42.
42 is 40 and 2. How do the Romans write 40?

ask.ifNot: A letter is never written 4 times in a row. 40 is 10 less than 50, so X goes in front of L.

beats.say: 40 is X L, and 2 is I I. So the total is X L I I.
Careful: X X X X I I adds up to 42 as well, but 4 Xs in a row are not allowed.
So: change to our numbers, add, and change back.
How many factors does 12 have? A factor of 12 is a number that divides 12 exactly, with nothing left over.
Here is a neat trick. Factors come in pairs that multiply to make 12. The first pair is easy: 1 times 12.
Next we try 2. 12 is even, so 2 is a factor. What is its partner?

ask.ifNot: The partner is the number we multiply 2 by to make 12. Half of 12 is 6, so the partner of 2 is 6.

beats.say: 2 times 6 is 12. That is our second pair.
Keep going in order. The next number that works is 3: 3 times 4 is 12.
When do we stop? The next factor after 3 is 4, and 4 is already on the board as a partner. So the pairs would only repeat.
Now count. We have 3 pairs, and each pair gives 2 different factors. How many factors is that?

ask.ifNot: Each pair holds 2 factors, and there are 3 pairs. So we double 3.

beats.say: 3 pairs, 2 factors in each, makes 6. So 12 has 6 factors. Here they all are, in order.
Remember the plan: go up in order, 1, 2, 3 and so on, and write each pair that works. Then count the numbers in the pairs.
Here is our sum. 62 take away 3. Look at the sign first. It is a minus, so we take away.
62 has only 2 ones, and we need to take away 3. So first take away 2, to land on the round number 60.
We have taken 2 so far, out of 3. How many more do we still have to take away?

ask.ifNot: 3 is 2 and 1. We have taken the 2, so 1 more is still to go.

beats.say: 3 is 2 and 1. The 2 is done, and the 1 is still waiting.
Now hop back 1 more from 60. That lands on 59.

spec.note: Then hop the last 1

beats.say: So 62 take away 3 equals 59.
Check by adding back. 59 plus 3 makes 62, the number we started with.
So when there are not enough ones, hop back to the round number first, then take away what is left.
Which of these is a prime number? A prime has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. So we look for factors, and cross out any number that has more.
35 and 15 both end in 5, so 5 divides them. 35 is 5 times 7, and 15 is 3 times 5. Neither is prime.
Now 21. Is 21 in the 3 times table?

ask.ifNot: 3 times 7 is 21. So 21 has factors other than 1 and itself.

beats.say: 21 is 3 times 7, so it is not prime either.
That leaves 29. It is odd. Its digits add up to 11, so 3 does not divide it. It does not end in 0 or 5. And 7 times 4 is 28, which just misses it.
Nothing divides 29 except 1 and 29. So 29 is the prime number.
So to test for a prime, try the small primes 2, 3, 5 and 7. If none of them goes in, a number this size is prime.
Which of these four numbers can be divided exactly by 3? There is a quick test, so we will not need long division.
The test for 3: add up the digits. If the total is in the 3 times table, then 3 divides the number.
5,123 gives 11. 4,532 gives 14. 8,206 gives 16. None of those totals is in the 3 times table.
Now 7,251. What do its digits add up to?

ask.ifNot: Add them one at a time: 7, then 2, then 5, then 1. You reach 15.

beats.say: The digits add up to 15, and 15 divided by 3 is 5, with nothing left over. So 7,251 is divisible by 3.
Let's check that the test told the truth. 3 times 2,417 is 7,251. It did!
So for 3, never mind how big the number is. Just add its digits and test the total.
Here is our sum. 63 plus 43.
Big numbers are friendlier in pieces. So we split each one into its tens and its ones.
Start with the tens. What is 60 plus 40?

ask.ifNot: 6 tens and 4 tens make 10 tens. And 10 tens is 100.

beats.say: 6 tens and 4 tens make 10 tens. That is 100.
Now the ones. 3 plus 3 is 6.
Now put the two parts together. 100 and 6 make 106.
So 63 plus 43 equals 106.
A quick check. 106 take away 43 is 63, right where we started. It fits.
So the plan is: split into tens and ones, add the tens, add the ones, then join them.
Which of these four numbers can be divided exactly by 4? Again there is a quick test.
The test for 4: look only at the last two digits. If they make a number in the 4 times table, then 4 divides the whole number.
