ask.ifNot: 2 tens doubled is 4 tens. 5 doubled is 10, which is one more ten. That makes 5 tens, and 5 tens is 50.

beats.say: Double 25 is 50.
Now double again. Double 50 is 100.
So 25 times 4 is 100.
This is a fact worth keeping in your head: four 25s make 100.
So to multiply by 4, double and double again.
Ria buys two kinds of things: notebooks and pens. We find the cost of each kind, then add.

board.text: 3 notebooks at 45 rupees.   2 pens at 12 rupees.

spec.note: 3 notebooks and 2 pens

beats.say: Start with the notebooks. 3 notebooks at 45 rupees each. Which sum?

ask.ifNot: Each of the 3 notebooks costs 45 rupees. So we need 3 lots of 45.

beats.say: 3 times 45. 3 times 40 is 120, and 3 times 5 is 15. Together, 135 rupees.
Now the pens. 2 pens at 12 rupees each. 2 times 12 is 24 rupees.
We have 135 rupees for notebooks and 24 rupees for pens. What is the last step?

ask.ifNot: She paid for both the notebooks and the pens. So we add the two costs together.

beats.say: 135 plus 24 is 159. Ria spent 159 rupees.
We can write the whole story on one line. Times first, then the plus.
So: work out each kind of thing on its own, then add the costs. The total is 159 rupees.
1,000 divided by 8. Dividing by 8 sounds hard, but halving is easy. And 8 is made of halvings.
8 is 2 times 2 times 2. So dividing by 8 is the same as halving three times.
First halving. Half of 1,000 is 500.
Second halving. What is half of 500?

ask.ifNot: Half of 5 hundreds is 2 and a half hundreds. That is 250.

beats.say: Half of 500 is 250.
Third halving. Half of 250. Half of 200 is 100, and half of 50 is 25. Together, 125.
So 1,000 divided by 8 is 125.
Check. 8 times 100 is 800, and 8 times 25 is 200. Together that is 1,000. It fits.
So to divide by 8, halve, halve, and halve again. The answer is 125.
81 plus 6. Let us work it out together. Look at the sign first. It is a plus, so we add.
81 is 80 and 1. Let us split it into its tens and its ones.
There is room in the ones place, so only the ones will change. What is 1 plus 6?

ask.ifNot: Start at 1 and count on 6 more. You land on 7.

beats.say: 1 one and 6 ones make 7 ones.
The tens have not changed, so put them back. 80 and 7 make 87.
So 81 plus 6 equals 87.
Let us check by going backwards. 87 take away 6 brings us back to 81.
The plan: split off the ones, add the ones, then put the tens back.
This question is about a rule, not about one sum. What happens when any number is multiplied by 1?
Let us try a few. Multiplying by 1 means one group. One group of 6 is just 6.
Try another. What is 9 times 1?

ask.ifNot: 9 times 1 means one group of 9. One group of 9 is just 9.

beats.say: One group of 9 is 9. It works for bigger numbers too. One group of 45 is 45.
Look down the board. Each time, the answer is the very number we started with.
So any number multiplied by 1 gives the same number.
Do not mix it up with adding 1, which makes a number one bigger. Multiplying by 1 changes nothing at all.
Another rule question. What happens when any number is multiplied by 0?
Picture 4 plates with nothing on any of them. How many sweets altogether? None. So 4 times 0 is 0.
Try a bigger one. 100 plates, all empty. How many sweets?

ask.ifNot: Every plate is empty. However many empty plates you have, there are still no sweets at all.

beats.say: Still none. 100 times 0 is 0.
It never matters how big the number is. Lots of nothing is still nothing.
So any number multiplied by 0 gives 0.
Do not mix it up with multiplying by 1, which gives the same number back. Multiplying by 0 always gives 0.
A chain of four instructions. We follow them one at a time, in order, and keep track on the board.
Start with 5. Double it. 5 times 2 is 10.
Add 3. 10 plus 3 is 13.
Now multiply by 4. Which number do we multiply?

ask.ifNot: Each instruction works on the newest number in the chain. Right now that is 13.

beats.say: 13 times 4. 10 times 4 is 40, and 3 times 4 is 12. Together, 52.
Is 52 the answer?

ask.ifNot: There is one more instruction in the chain: subtract 2.

beats.say: Last step. 52 take away 2 is 50.
So in a chain like this, do every step in order, each on the newest number, and do not stop early.
Three signs in one sum: a minus, a times and a plus. The trick is knowing where to start.
Which part do we work out first?

ask.ifNot: It is tempting to start on the left. But multiplying always goes first, so 4 times 7 is our first job.

beats.say: Times is the boss here. It goes before plus and minus, so put a box round 4 times 7.
4 times 7 is 28. So 28 goes where the box was. The rest of the sum stays the same.
Just a minus and a plus now. Which one comes first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 37 take away 28.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 37 take away 28 is 9.
And now the plus. 9 plus 3 is 12.
Did you spot the trap? Going left to right from the very start would mean taking away before multiplying, and that gives a different number.
The rule: multiply first. Then add and take away in order, from left to right.
Here is our sum. It has three signs in it: a minus, a times and a plus.
Which part do we work out first?

ask.ifNot: It is tempting to start on the left. But multiplying always goes first, so 2 times 2 is our first job.

beats.say: Times is the boss here. It goes before plus and minus, so put a box round 2 times 2.
2 times 2 is 4. So 4 goes where the box was. The rest of the sum stays the same.
Now only a minus and a plus are left. Which do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 14 take away 4.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 14 take away 4 is 10.
One job left, the plus. 10 and 14 make 24.
Did you spot the trap? Going left to right from the very start would mean taking away before multiplying, and that gives a different number.
The rule: multiply first. Then add and take away in order, from left to right.
Here is our sum. It has three signs in it: a minus, a times and a plus.
Which part do we work out first?

ask.ifNot: It is tempting to start on the left. But multiplying always goes first, so 6 times 3 is our first job.

beats.say: Times is the boss here. It goes before plus and minus, so put a box round 6 times 3.
6 times 3 is 18. Write 18 in its place, and copy everything else just as it was.
Just a minus and a plus now. Which one comes first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 42 take away 18.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 42 take away 18 is 24.
One job left, the plus. 24 and 7 make 31.
Did you spot the trap? Going left to right from the very start would mean taking away before multiplying, and that gives a different number.
So remember: times first, then plus and minus from left to right.
7 times some number makes 91. We need to find that hidden number.

spec.note: 7 equal parts make 91

beats.say: Which sum finds the hidden number?

ask.ifNot: 7 equal groups make 91. To find the size of one group, we divide 91 by 7.

beats.say: Divide undoes times. So we need 91 divided by 7.
Split 91 into two friendly pieces: 70 and 21. Both are in the 7 times table.
70 divided by 7 is 10. And 21 divided by 7 is 3.
10 and 3 make 13. So the hidden number is 13.
Check by multiplying. 7 times 13 is 91. It fits.
So to find a missing number in a times sum, divide. Here it is 13.
Here is 12.5 in a place-value chart. We want to divide it by 10.

spec.note: Divide by 10: where does each digit move?

beats.say: What does dividing by 10 do to a number?

ask.ifNot: Dividing shares a number out, so it gets smaller. Dividing by 10 makes it 10 times smaller.

beats.say: So every digit becomes worth ten times less. That means every digit moves one place to the right.
The 2 is in the ones place now. Where does it go?

ask.ifNot: One place to the right of the ones is the tenths place, just after the decimal point.

beats.say: The 1 ten becomes 1 one. The 2 ones become 2 tenths. The 5 tenths become 5 hundredths. That makes 1.25.
So 12.5 divided by 10 is 1.25.
Check by multiplying back: 1.25 times 10 is 12.5. One zero in 10, so the digits move one place.
This time we divide 12.5 by 100.

spec.note: Divide by 100: where does each digit move?

beats.say: 100 has two zeros. How many places do the digits move to the right?

ask.ifNot: Each zero stands for one division by 10, and each division by 10 moves the digits one place. Two zeros, two places.

beats.say: Let's take one place at a time. One place to the right: 12.5 becomes 1.25.
Now one more place to the right. What does 1.25 become?

ask.ifNot: The 1 moves from the ones into the tenths. Nothing is left in the ones place, so we write a 0 there.

beats.say: 1.25 becomes 0.125. The ones place is empty now, so a zero stands in front of the point.
So 12.5 divided by 100 is 0.125.
Check: 0.125 times 100 takes us back to 12.5. Count the zeros, and move the digits that many places to the right.
Now a big one: 12.5 divided by 10000.

spec.note: Divide by 10000: where does each digit move?

beats.say: How many zeros does 10000 have?

ask.ifNot: Count them one by one after the 1. There are 4 zeros.

beats.say: So dividing by 10000 is like dividing by 10 four times. Each time, every digit moves one place to the right.
The first two moves: 12.5 becomes 1.25, and then 1.25 becomes 0.125.
The third move. What does 0.125 become?

ask.ifNot: Every digit moves one place to the right, and a zero fills the empty tenths place. So 0.125 becomes 0.0125.

beats.say: That is three moves. One more to go: 0.0125 becomes 0.00125. Each move puts one more zero after the point.
So 12.5 divided by 10000 is 0.00125.
Check: 0.00125 times 10000 is 12.5. It is easy to move one place too few or too many, so count the zeros and count your moves.
28 divided by 5. This one does not come out as a whole number, so we will need a decimal.
How many whole fives fit into 28?

ask.ifNot: Count in fives up to 28. Five fives fit, but six fives would go past 28.

beats.say: 5 fives are 25. That leaves 3 ones over.
What do we do with the 3 that are left over?

ask.ifNot: We can keep sharing. 3 ones cannot be shared by 5 as wholes, but each one is 10 tenths. So 3 ones are 30 tenths.

beats.say: 3 ones are 30 tenths. Share 30 tenths by 5, and each share is 6 tenths.
5 ones and 6 tenths. So 28 divided by 5 is 5.6.
Check by multiplying back: 5.6 times 5 is 28.
A neat shortcut: to divide by 5, double the number and then divide by 10. Double 28 is 56, and 56 divided by 10 is 5.6.
11.2 divided by 4. We divide just as with whole numbers, and keep the decimal point in its place.
Start with the whole part. How many fours fit into 11?

ask.ifNot: Two fours are 8, and that fits into 11. Three fours would go past 11.

beats.say: 2 fours are 8. That leaves 3 ones over.
Those 3 ones are 30 tenths. And there are 2 tenths in the number already. Together that is 32 tenths.
Share 32 tenths by 4. How many tenths in each share?

ask.ifNot: From the 4 times table: 4 times 8 is 32.

beats.say: 2 ones and 8 tenths. So 11.2 divided by 4 is 2.8.
Check by multiplying back: 2.8 times 4 is 11.2.
When ones are left over, turn them into tenths and keep on sharing.
Let us add 50 and 42.
50 is a round number, full tens and no ones. So we only need to split the 42, into 40 and 2.
Add the tens first. What is 50 plus 40?

ask.ifNot: 5 tens and 4 tens make 9 tens. And 9 tens is 90.

beats.say: 5 tens and 4 tens make 9 tens. That is 90.
Now bring in the 2 ones. 90 and 2 make 92.
There it is. 50 plus 42 makes 92.
A quick check. 92 take away 42 is 50, right where we started. It fits.
So add the tens first, then drop the ones in.
1.264 divided by 0.04. Dividing by a decimal is awkward, so we change the sum into one where we divide by a whole number.
What should we multiply 0.04 by, to turn it into a whole number?

ask.ifNot: 0.04 has two digits after the point. Times 10 would still leave a decimal. Times 100 moves the digits two places, and gives 4.

beats.say: Whatever we do to one number we must do to the other, so the answer stays the same. 1.264 times 100 is 126.4, and 0.04 times 100 is 4.
Now divide 126.4 by 4. Split it into two easy parts: 120 and 6.4. First, 120 divided by 4 is 30.
And what is 6.4 divided by 4?

ask.ifNot: 6.4 is a bit more than 4, so the answer is a bit more than 1. And 4 times 1.6 is 6.4.

beats.say: 6.4 divided by 4 is 1.6. Add the two parts: 30 and 1.6 make 31.6.
So 1.264 divided by 0.04 is 31.6.
Check by multiplying back: 31.6 times 0.04 is 1.264. The answer is much bigger than 1.264, because lots of tiny pieces of 0.04 fit into it.
3.43 divided by 0.07. We would much rather divide by a whole number, so let's change the sum without changing its answer.
How many digits does 0.07 have after the point?

ask.ifNot: After the point there is a 0 and then a 7. That is two digits.

beats.say: Two digits, so we multiply by 100 to clear them. And we do it to both numbers. 3.43 becomes 343, and 0.07 becomes 7.
Now 343 divided by 7. Take a big bite first: 7 times 40 is 280. That leaves 63.
How many sevens are there in 63?

ask.ifNot: From the 7 times table: 7 times 9 is 63.

beats.say: So 7 goes in 40 times, and then 9 more times. 40 and 9 make 49.
So 3.43 divided by 0.07 is 49.
Check by multiplying back: 49 times 0.07 is 3.43. To divide by a decimal, multiply both numbers by 10 or 100 until you divide by a whole number.
Let us take 8 away from 82.
82 has only 2 ones, and we need to take away 8. So first take away 2, to land on the round number 80.
We have taken 2 so far, out of 8. How many more do we still have to take away?

ask.ifNot: 8 is 2 and 6. We have taken the 2, so 6 more are still to go.

beats.say: 8 is 2 and 6. The 2 is done, and the 6 is still waiting.
Now hop back 6 more from 80. That lands on 74.

spec.note: Then hop the last 6

beats.say: So 82 take away 8 equals 74.
Check by adding back. 74 plus 8 makes 82, the number we started with.
The plan: go back to the round ten first, then take away the rest.
Here is 7.06 in a place-value chart. We divide it by 10.

spec.note: Divide by 10: where does each digit move?

beats.say: Dividing by 10 makes the number ten times smaller. Which way do the digits move?

ask.ifNot: Smaller places are on the right. So to become ten times smaller, each digit moves one place to the right.

beats.say: The 7 ones become 7 tenths. The 0 tenths become 0 hundredths. The 6 hundredths become 6 thousandths.

spec.note: 7 tenths, 0 hundredths and 6 thousandths

beats.say: What happens to the 0 in the middle of 7.06?

ask.ifNot: Every digit moves, and zero is a digit. It keeps the 7 and the 6 apart, in their proper places.

beats.say: And the ones place is empty now, so we write a 0 in front of the point.
So 7.06 divided by 10 is 0.706.
Check: 0.706 times 10 moves every digit back, and we get 7.06. Dividing by 10 moves every digit one place to the right, zeros included.
Let us multiply 97 by 46. Look at the sign first. It is times, so we multiply.
That is a big one, so we break it into two smaller jobs. Split 46 into 40 and 6.

spec.note: Split 46 into 40 and 6

beats.say: Start with the tens piece, 40. First, 97 times 4. 90 times 4 is 360, and 7 times 4 is 28. Together that makes 388.
40 is 4 tens. So what is 97 times 40?

ask.ifNot: 40 is ten times 4. So the answer is ten times 388, which is 388 with a 0 on the end.

beats.say: Ten times 388 is 3880. That is the first piece done.
Now the ones piece. 97 times 6. 90 times 6 is 540, and 7 times 6 is 42. Together that makes 582.
Add the two pieces. 3880 plus 582 is 4462.
So 97 times 46 equals 4462.
A quick check on the last digit. 7 times 6 is 42, which ends in 2. Our answer ends in 2 too.
Break it up, multiply each piece, add the pieces. Big sums are just small sums in a row.
652.7 divided by 100.

spec.note: Divide by 100: where does each digit move?

beats.say: Will the answer be bigger or smaller than 652.7?

ask.ifNot: Dividing shares the number out into 100 equal parts. Each part is much smaller than the whole.

beats.say: 100 has two zeros, so every digit moves two places to the right. Let's go one place at a time. First: 652.7 becomes 65.27.

spec.note: One place: 652.7 becomes 65.27

beats.say: One more place to the right. What does 65.27 become?

ask.ifNot: Each digit moves one more place to the right. The 6 tens become 6 ones, so the number starts with 6 and then the point.

spec.note: One more place: 652.7 ÷ 100 = 6.527

beats.say: So 652.7 divided by 100 is 6.527.
Does it make sense? 652.7 has about six and a half hundreds in it, and 6.527 is about six and a half. Yes.
The digits stay the same, in the same order. Count the zeros in 100, and move the digits that many places to the right.
Here is our sum. 3 times 2. Look at the sign first. It is times, so we multiply.
3 times 2 means 3 groups of 2. Picture 3 rows with 2 in each row.

spec.note: 3 rows of 2 squares

beats.say: Which adding sum shows 3 groups of 2?

ask.ifNot: 3 groups of 2 means the 2 is written 3 times, with plus signs in between.

beats.say: Add them up. 2 plus 2 plus 2 makes 6.
There it is. 3 times 2 makes 6.
We can turn it round as well. 2 groups of 3 also make 6.
So times is a quick way of adding the same number again and again.
3.8 divided by 100.

spec.note: Divide by 100: where does each digit move?

beats.say: 100 has two zeros. What happens to the digits?

ask.ifNot: Dividing makes a number smaller, so the digits move right, into smaller places. Two zeros means two places.

beats.say: One place first. The 3 ones become 3 tenths, and the 8 tenths become 8 hundredths. 3.8 becomes 0.38.

spec.note: One place: 3.8 becomes 0.38

beats.say: Now one more place. The 3 moves to the hundredths and the 8 to the thousandths. What goes in the empty tenths place?

ask.ifNot: An empty place must be held by a zero. Without it, the 3 would slide back into the tenths place.

beats.say: A zero holds the tenths place. So 0.38 becomes 0.038.

spec.note: One more place: a zero fills the gap

beats.say: So 3.8 divided by 100 is 0.038.
Check: 0.038 times 100 is 3.8. When the digits move right and leave a gap after the point, fill the gap with a zero.
Here is our sum. 4 plus 11.
Adding works in any order. So let us start from the bigger number, 11, and add the 4 to it.
11 is 10 and 1. Let us split it into its tens and its ones.
There is room in the ones place, so only the ones will change. What is 1 plus 4?

ask.ifNot: Start at 1 and count on 4 more. You land on 5.

beats.say: 1 one and 4 ones make 5 ones.
The tens have not changed, so put them back. 10 and 5 make 15.
So 4 plus 11 equals 15.
Let us check by going backwards. 15 take away 11 brings us back to 4.
So when you add a small number and there is room in the ones, keep the tens and just add the ones.
We want to write 3 over 4 as a decimal. The bar shows it: 3 parts out of 4 are shaded.

spec.note: 3/4 as a decimal = ?

beats.say: Decimals are tenths and hundredths. So one good way is to change the bottom number into 100.
4 times what makes 100?

ask.ifNot: Think of a rupee. 4 coins of 25 paise make 100 paise.

beats.say: So multiply the top and the bottom by 25. 3 times 25 is 75. So 3 over 4 is 75 over 100.
How do we write 75 hundredths as a decimal?

ask.ifNot: Hundredths take two digits after the point. So 75 hundredths is 0.75. It must be less than 1, because 3 out of 4 is less than a whole.

beats.say: So 3 over 4 is 0.75.
We can also divide 3 by 4. 30 tenths shared by 4 is 7 tenths, with 2 tenths left. Those are 20 hundredths, and 20 shared by 4 is 5. Again 0.75.
Three quarters is 0.75. Think of 75 paise, three quarters of a rupee. It is a fact worth keeping in your head.
We want to write 0.125 as a fraction, as simple as it can be.

board.text: Express 0.125 as a fraction in simplest form

beats.say: 0.125 has three digits after the point. So what goes on the bottom of the fraction?

ask.ifNot: One digit means tenths, two digits mean hundredths, and three digits mean thousandths. So the bottom is 1000.

beats.say: 0.125 is 125 thousandths.
Now we simplify. Both numbers divide by 25. 125 divided by 25 is 5. What is 1000 divided by 25?

ask.ifNot: 4 lots of 25 make 100. So 40 lots of 25 make 1000.

beats.say: So 125 over 1000 becomes 5 over 40.
Are we done? Not yet. 5 and 40 both divide by 5. That gives 1 over 8.
1 and 8 share no factor, so this is the simplest form. 0.125 is one eighth.

spec.note: 0.125 is 1/8, and it cannot be made simpler

beats.say: Check: 8 lots of 0.125 make exactly 1. Write the decimal over 10, 100 or 1000, then keep dividing until nothing more goes into both.
Which of these four decimals is the greatest? They are all made of 5s and zeros, so we must look closely.
First give them all three digits after the point. Zeros at the end do not change a number.
Compare the tenths first. Which number has 0 tenths?

ask.ifNot: The tenths digit is the first digit after the point. In 0.05 that digit is 0.

beats.say: 0.05 has no tenths at all, so it is the smallest. The other three all have 5 tenths, so that is a tie.
To break the tie, look at the hundredths. We have 0.500, 0.550 and 0.505. Which has the biggest hundredths digit?

ask.ifNot: Look at the second digit after the point: 0, then 5, then 0. The 5 belongs to 0.550.

beats.say: 0.550 wins, and 0.550 is 0.55. The trap is 0.505: it looks big because it has the most digits. But as thousandths it is 505 against 550.
So the greatest is 0.55.

spec.note: 0.55 is the greatest

beats.say: To compare decimals: same number of places first, then compare from the left, one place at a time.
Three decimals to add, and all three have different lengths. So first we line them up.
0.004 has three digits after the point, so give the others three as well. Zeros go at the end.
Add the first two. Start from the right. Thousandths: 0 and 0. Hundredths: 6 and 0 make 6.
Tenths: 5 and 8 make 13 tenths. What do we write?

ask.ifNot: 13 tenths is 1 whole and 3 tenths. The 3 stays in the tenths place, and the 1 is carried to the ones.

beats.say: Ones: 4 and 7 and the carried 1 make 12. Write 2, carry 1. Tens: 3 and the carried 1 make 4. So far we have 42.36.
Now add the 0.004. In which place does its 4 land?

ask.ifNot: In 0.004 the 4 is the third digit after the point. The third place is the thousandths.

beats.say: 42.36 is 42.360. The 4 drops into the empty thousandths place. So the total is 42.364.
A rough check: about 35 and about 8 make 43, and our answer is a little under that. Line up the points, and every digit finds its own column.
Here is our sum. 86 times 12. The sign is times, so we want 86 lots of 12, not 86 plus 12.
Too big to do in one go. So split 12 into 10 and 2, and do one piece at a time.

spec.note: Split 12 into 10 and 2

beats.say: First, 86 times 10. That is 860, the same digits with a 0 on the end.
We split 12 into 10 and 2. The 10 is done. What is still left to multiply 86 by?

ask.ifNot: 12 is 10 and 2. We have done the 10, so the 2 is still left.

beats.say: Now the ones piece. 86 times 2. 80 times 2 is 160, and 6 times 2 is 12. Together that makes 172.
Now put the two pieces together. 860 and 172 make 1032.
So 86 times 12 equals 1032.
A quick check on the last digit. 6 times 2 is 12, which ends in 2. Our answer ends in 2 too.
Break it up, multiply each piece, add the pieces. Big sums are just small sums in a row.
50 take away 23.75. 50 is a whole number, so we can write it as 50.00 to match.
Let's take 23.75 away in two bites: first the 23 wholes, and then the 0.75.
First bite. What is 50 take away 23?

ask.ifNot: Check by adding: 23 and 27 make 50. With 37 we would get far too much.

beats.say: 50 take away 23 is 27.
Second bite: take 0.75 from 27. Break one whole open. What is 1 take away 0.75?

ask.ifNot: 0.75 is three quarters. Take three quarters from a whole, and one quarter is left. That is 0.25.

beats.say: So one of the 27 wholes turns into 0.25. That leaves 26 wholes and 0.25, which is 26.25.
So 50 take away 23.75 is 26.25.
Check by adding back: 26.25 plus 23.75 makes 50. The answer had to be below 27, because we took away more than 23.
Here is our sum. 14 take away 4.
14 is 10 and 4. Let us split it into its tens and its ones.
There are enough ones to take 4 from. So only the ones change. What is 4 take away 4?

ask.ifNot: Start at 4 and hop back 4. You land on 0.

beats.say: 4 ones take away 4 ones leaves no ones at all.
The tens have not changed, so put them back. 10 and 0 make 10.
There it is. 14 minus 4 leaves 10.
Let us check by going backwards. 10 plus 4 is 14. It fits.
So when there are enough ones, keep the tens and just take away from the ones.
2.5 times 0.4. Two decimals to multiply.
First forget the points and multiply the digits. 25 times 4 is 100.
Now the point. 2.5 has one digit after the point, and so has 0.4. How many decimal places is that altogether?

ask.ifNot: Count one place for 2.5 and one place for 0.4. One and one make 2.

beats.say: So the answer needs two digits after the point. Count two digits from the right of 100, and put the point there. That gives 1.00.
1.00 is the same as which of these?

ask.ifNot: Zeros at the end, after the point, do not change a number. 1.00 and 1.0 are both just 1.

beats.say: So 2.5 times 0.4 is 1.0, which is simply 1.
Does it make sense? 0.4 is a little less than a half, and half of 2.5 is 1.25. So a little less than 1.25 is just right.
Multiply the digits, count the decimal places in both numbers, and give the answer that many places.
Let us take 48 away from 88. Look at the sign first. It is a minus, so we take away.
Taking away 48 in one go is hard. So split it into 40 and 8.
Take the tens away first. What is 88 take away 40?

ask.ifNot: Only the tens change. 8 tens take away 4 tens leaves 4 tens, and the 8 ones stay. That is 48.

beats.say: Only the tens change, and the ones stay. So we have 48.
Now take away the 8 ones. 48 take away 8 is 40.
So 88 minus 48 is 40.
Check by adding back. 40 plus 48 makes 88, the number we started with.
So the plan is: take away the tens first, then take away the ones.
0.03 times 0.6. Both numbers are small, so the answer will be very small.
Forget the points and the zeros in front, and multiply the digits. 3 times 6 is 18.
Now count the decimal places. 0.03 has two digits after the point, and 0.6 has one. How many altogether?

ask.ifNot: Two places for 0.03 and one place for 0.6. Two and one make 3.

beats.say: So the answer needs three digits after the point. But 18 has only two digits. Hmm.
How do we give 18 three digits after the point?

ask.ifNot: A zero at the end would not move the 1 and the 8 at all. The zero must go in front, just after the point, to push them along.

beats.say: A zero goes in front of the 18. So the answer is 0.018.
Why does it work? 0.03 is 3 hundredths and 0.6 is 6 tenths. A tenth of a hundredth is a thousandth. So we get 18 thousandths.
When the digits are too few for the places you need, fill up with zeros just after the point.
28 times 36. Let us work it out together.
Too big to do in one go. So split 36 into 30 and 6, and do one piece at a time.

spec.note: Split 36 into 30 and 6

beats.say: Start with the tens piece, 30. First, 28 times 3. 20 times 3 is 60, and 8 times 3 is 24. Together that makes 84.
30 is 3 tens. So what is 28 times 30?

ask.ifNot: 30 is ten times 3. So the answer is ten times 84, which is 84 with a 0 on the end.

beats.say: Ten times 84 is 840. That is the first piece done.
Now the ones piece. 28 times 6. 20 times 6 is 120, and 8 times 6 is 48. Together that makes 168.
Now put the two pieces together. 840 and 168 make 1008.
So 28 times 36 equals 1008.
A quick check on the last digit. 8 times 6 is 48, which ends in 8. Our answer ends in 8 too.
So the plan is: split one number into tens and ones, multiply each piece, then add.
A ribbon is 6.9 metres long. How many pieces of 3 centimetres can be cut from it?

board.text: 6.9 m ribbon. Pieces of 3 cm. How many?

beats.say: Can we just divide 6.9 by 3?

choices: no, make the units the same first
ask.ifNot: The ribbon is in metres but the pieces are in centimetres. We must change the ribbon into centimetres first.

beats.say: 1 metre is 100 centimetres. So 6.9 metres is 6.9 times 100, which is 690 centimetres.
Careful: 690, not 69. Times 100 moves the digits 2 places.
Now, how many 3s are in 690? 69 divided by 3 is 23, so 690 divided by 3 is 230.
So 230 pieces can be cut.
Check: 230 pieces of 3 centimetres make 690 centimetres. Same units first, then divide.
81 plus 48. Let us work it out together. Look at the sign first. It is a plus, so we add.
Big numbers are friendlier in pieces. So we split each one into its tens and its ones.
Start with the tens. What is 80 plus 40?

ask.ifNot: 8 tens and 4 tens make 12 tens. And 12 tens is 120.

beats.say: 8 tens and 4 tens make 12 tens. That is 120.
Now the ones. 1 plus 8 is 9.
Last, join the two parts. 120 plus 9 is 129.
So 81 plus 48 equals 129.
Let us check by going backwards. 129 take away 48 brings us back to 81.
So the plan is: split into tens and ones, add the tens, add the ones, then join them.
Here is our sum. 34 take away 32. Look at the sign first. It is a minus, so we take away.
Look how close these two numbers are. So here is a neat way: ask how far it is from 32 up to 34.
Count the hops from 32 up to 34. How many are there?

ask.ifNot: Start at 32 and hop up one at a time until you reach 34. That takes 2 hops.

beats.say: 2 hops. So 32 and 2 more make 34.
There it is. 34 minus 32 leaves 2.
The answer cannot be a big number here, because 34 and 32 are almost the same size.
So when two numbers are close together, count up from the smaller one to the bigger one.
One bottle holds 125 millilitres of oil. How many bottles do we need for 2.5 litres?

board.text: Bottle: 125 ml. Oil: 2.5 litres. How many bottles?

beats.say: First, the same unit. 1 litre is 1000 millilitres, so 2.5 litres is 2500 millilitres.
Think about 1 litre first. 2 bottles hold 250 millilitres. So how many bottles fill 1000?

ask.ifNot: 4 lots of 250 make 1000. Each 250 is 2 bottles, so that is 8 bottles.

beats.say: 8 bottles fill 1 litre.
We have 2 and a half litres. 2 litres need 16 bottles, and the half litre needs 4 more.
16 plus 4 is 20. So 20 bottles are needed.
Check: 20 bottles of 125 millilitres make 2500 millilitres. It fits.
Here is 45.783 in a place-value chart. In which place is the digit 8?

board.text: In 45.783, the digit 8 is in which place?

spec.note: Name the place of each digit

beats.say: First, is the 8 before the decimal point or after it?

ask.ifNot: Find the point. It sits between the 5 and the 7. The 8 comes later, so it is after the point.

beats.say: After the point, the places have their own names. In order they are tenths, hundredths, thousandths.
Which digit after the point is the 8: the 1st, the 2nd or the 3rd?

ask.ifNot: After the point come 7, then 8, then 3. So the 8 is the second one.

beats.say: The 7 is in the tenths place. The 8 is in the hundredths place. The 3 is in the thousandths place.

spec.note: 8 is in the hundredths place

beats.say: So the 8 is in the hundredths place.

board.text: The 8 is in the hundredths place

beats.say: After the point, count along: tenths, hundredths, thousandths. And listen for the t h at the end. Hundreds are on the other side of the point.
What is the value of the 6 in 2.0639? Here is the number, with each digit under the name of its place.

board.text: What is the value of 6 in 2.0639?

beats.say: The 6 is not simply worth 6. What a digit is worth depends on the place it sits in.
Count from the decimal point. Which digit after the point is the 6?

ask.ifNot: After the point come 0, and then 6. The zero counts as a digit too. So the 6 is the second one.

beats.say: Careful with that zero. It is holding the tenths place. So the 6 is one place further along, in the hundredths place.
So the 6 is worth 6 hundredths. How do we write 6 hundredths as a decimal?

ask.ifNot: Hundredths are the second place after the point. So we write a 0 in the tenths place, and then the 6.

beats.say: The value of the 6 is 0.06.
The digit itself is 6. But its value here is only 0.06, because of where it sits. Name the place first, then write the value.
Riya buys 2.5 kilograms of apples at 120 rupees a kilogram, and 1.25 kilograms of oranges at 80 rupees a kilogram. How much does she spend?

board.text: 1.25 kg oranges at ₹80 per kg. Total = ?

beats.say: Two costs to find, and then we add them. Start with the apples. 2.5 kilograms is 2 kilograms and half a kilogram.
2 kilograms of apples cost 240 rupees. What does half a kilogram cost?

ask.ifNot: Half a kilogram costs half the price of a whole kilogram. Half of 120 is 60.

beats.say: Half a kilogram costs 60. So the apples cost 240 and 60, which is 300 rupees.
Now the oranges. 1.25 kilograms is 1 kilogram and a quarter of a kilogram. The 1 kilogram costs 80 rupees.
What does a quarter of a kilogram of oranges cost?

ask.ifNot: A quarter is one of 4 equal parts. 80 shared into 4 parts is 20 each.

beats.say: A quarter costs 20. So the oranges cost 80 and 20, which is 100 rupees.
Add the two costs. 300 and 100 make 400. Riya spends 400 rupees.

spec.note: Riya spent ₹400 in total

beats.say: The decimals were friendly here: point five is a half, and point two five is a quarter. Find each cost on its own, then add.
Look at the signs here. A minus, then a times, then a plus.
Which part do we work out first?

ask.ifNot: Times goes before plus and minus, even when it sits in the middle. So we begin with 3 times 4.

beats.say: Times is the boss here. It goes before plus and minus, so put a box round 3 times 4.
3 times 4 is 12. So 12 goes where the box was. The rest of the sum stays the same.
Just a minus and a plus now. Which one comes first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 13 take away 12.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 13 take away 12 is 1.
And now the plus. 1 plus 1 is 2.
The trap in this sum is the minus at the front. It looks like the place to start, but the times must go first.
The rule: multiply first. Then add and take away in order, from left to right.
809 divided by 10.

spec.note: Divide by 10: where does each digit move?

beats.say: 809 is a whole number. Where is its decimal point?

ask.ifNot: Every whole number has a decimal point hiding at its end. We can write 809 as 809.0.

beats.say: So 809 is the same as 809.0.

spec.note: Write 809 as 809.0

beats.say: Dividing by 10 moves every digit one place to the right. The 8 hundreds become 8 tens. The 0 tens become 0 ones. The 9 ones become 9 tenths.
What happens to the 0 in the middle?

choices: it stays between the 8 and the 9
ask.ifNot: Every digit keeps its order. The zero is holding a place, so it must stay between the 8 and the 9.

beats.say: So 809 divided by 10 is 80.9.

spec.note: The point moves one place to the left. The 0 stays

beats.say: Check: 80.9 times 10 is 809. The digits 8, 0, 9 stay in the same order. Only the point seems to hop one place to the left.
We must put four decimals in ascending order.
What does ascending order mean?

ask.ifNot: Ascending means going up, like climbing stairs. So we start with the smallest and finish with the biggest.

beats.say: The numbers have different lengths, so give each one three digits after the point. Then we can compare them fairly.
They all have 3 wholes. So look after the point: 300, 030, 303 and 330. Which is the smallest?

ask.ifNot: 030 is just 30. The others are all 300 or more.

beats.say: So 3.03 comes first. It has 0 tenths, and the others all have 3 tenths. Next is 300, which is 3.3.
Two are left: 3.303 and 3.33. Which is bigger?

ask.ifNot: 3.33 is the same as 3.330. Now compare 330 with 303. 330 is more.

beats.say: 3.303 has more digits, but 3.33 is bigger. So the order is 3.03, then 3.3, then 3.303, then 3.33.

spec.note: In order, smallest first

beats.say: Same number of places first. Then compare from the left. A longer decimal is not always a bigger one.
Look at the signs here. A minus, then a times, then a plus.
So, which bit goes first?

ask.ifNot: It is tempting to start on the left. But multiplying always goes first, so 3 times 9 is our first job.

beats.say: Times is the boss here. It goes before plus and minus, so put a box round 3 times 9.
3 times 9 is 27. So 27 goes where the box was. The rest of the sum stays the same.
Now only a minus and a plus are left. Which do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 40 take away 27.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 40 take away 27 is 13.
One job left, the plus. 13 and 15 make 28.
Did you spot the trap? Going left to right from the very start would mean taking away before multiplying, and that gives a different number.
So remember: times first, then plus and minus from left to right.
Three decimals to multiply. We take them two at a time.
Start with 0.25 times 0.4. Forget the points: 25 times 4 is 100.
0.25 has two digits after the point and 0.4 has one. So the answer needs three. Where does the point go in 100?

ask.ifNot: Two places and one place make three places. Count three digits from the right of 100, and put the point there.

beats.say: That gives 0.100, and 0.100 is just 0.1. It makes sense: 0.25 is a quarter, and a quarter of 0.4 is 0.1.
Now 0.1 times 0.8. The digits give 1 times 8, which is 8. The two numbers have two decimal places altogether. So what is the answer?

ask.ifNot: We need two digits after the point, but 8 is only one digit. So a zero goes in front of it: 0.08.

beats.say: So the whole product is 0.08.
A good check: all three numbers are less than 1, so the product must be smaller than each of them. 0.08 is. Multiply two at a time, and count the places each time.
Let us add 49 and 4. Look at the sign first. It is a plus, so we add.
49 is very close to 50. It needs just 1 more to get there.

spec.note: Then hop the last 3

beats.say: So we use 1 of the 4 to reach 50. How much of the 4 is still left to add?

ask.ifNot: We used 1 out of the 4 to reach 50. Take 1 from 4 and 3 is left.

beats.say: 4 is 1 and 3. The 1 took us to 50, and the 3 is still waiting.
Now it is easy. 50 plus 3 is 53.
So 49 plus 4 equals 53.
Let us check by going backwards. 53 take away 4 brings us back to 49.
The plan: make the next ten first, then add the rest.
Someone wants to measure the perimeter of a classroom. Which of these units should they use?

board.text: Perimeter of a classroom: which unit?

beats.say: The perimeter is the distance all the way round the walls. Imagine walking round the room with your hand on the wall.

board.text: perimeter = distance all the way round

beats.say: So what kind of thing is a perimeter?

ask.ifNot: A perimeter tells us how far it is around the room. How far is a length.

beats.say: Now check each unit. Litres measure liquids, like milk. Kilograms measure how heavy something is.
Metres measure length. And a classroom is a few metres long, so the metre is just the right size.
What about 'any of these'? Each unit measures one kind of thing only, so that cannot be right. The answer is the metre.
Before you measure anything, ask yourself: is it a length, a weight, or a liquid? Then choose the unit.
One American dollar is worth 40 rupees. How many dollars do we get for 100 rupees?

spec.note: How many 40s fit into 100?

beats.say: Which sum do we need?

ask.ifNot: Each dollar uses up 40 rupees. We want to know how many 40s fit into 100, and that is dividing.

beats.say: Take out the whole dollars first. 2 dollars use 80 rupees. That leaves 20 rupees.

spec.note: Two dollars use 80 rupees, and 20 rupees are left

beats.say: We have 20 rupees left, and a dollar costs 40. How much of a dollar do 20 rupees buy?

ask.ifNot: 20 is half of 40. So 20 rupees buy half a dollar.

beats.say: Half a dollar. As a decimal, a half is 0.5.
2 dollars and half a dollar. So 100 rupees give 2.5 dollars.
Check: 2.5 lots of 40 make 100. And it makes sense: 100 rupees is more than 2 lots of 40, but less than 3 lots.
To change money, divide by what one unit costs. And when something is left over, turn it into a decimal part.
How do we change decametres into decimetres? The two words look alike, so let's go slowly.

board.text: decametre → decimetre: what do we do?

beats.say: Deca means ten. So 1 decametre is 10 metres. Deci means a tenth. So 1 metre is 10 decimetres.
Which one is the smaller unit?

ask.ifNot: A decimetre is only a tenth of a metre, about the length of a crayon. A decametre is 10 whole metres.

beats.say: We are going from a big unit to a small one. So there will be more of them, and that means we multiply.
Two steps down: decametre to metre is times 10, and metre to decimetre is times 10 again. 10 times 10 is 100.
So to change decametres into decimetres, we multiply by 100.
Going to a smaller unit: multiply. Going to a bigger unit: divide. And count the steps between them.
We want a pair of units where one is 1 hundredth of the other.

board.text: Which pair: one unit = 1/100 of the other?

beats.say: Let's test each pair. A kilogram and a tonne: 1000 kilograms make a tonne. That is a thousandth, not a hundredth.
A metre and a kilometre: 1000 metres make a kilometre. A thousandth again.
A gram and a decagram: deca means ten, so 10 grams make a decagram. That is a tenth.
That leaves centilitre and litre. What does centi mean?

ask.ifNot: Think of a century, which is 100 years, or a centimetre: 100 of them make a metre. Centi means a hundredth.

beats.say: 100 centilitres make 1 litre. So a centilitre is 1 hundredth of a litre. That is our pair.
The start of the word tells you: deci is a tenth, centi is a hundredth, milli is a thousandth.
125 millilitres is what part of a litre? The answer will be a fraction.
1000 millilitres make 1 litre. So 125 millilitres is 125 out of 1000.
That fraction is clumsy, so let's make it simpler. 125 doubled is 250. 250 doubled is 500. And 500 doubled is 1000.
We doubled 3 times. So how many 125s make 1000?

ask.ifNot: Doubling 3 times is 2 times 2 times 2. That makes 8.

beats.say: 8 times 125 is 1000. So we can divide the top and the bottom of the fraction by 125.
125 millilitres is 1 eighth of a litre.
So 8 small glasses of 125 millilitres fill 1 litre. Write the part over the whole, then simplify.
37.02 kilograms. Let's write it as kilograms and grams.
Split it at the point. 37 whole kilograms, and 0.02 of a kilogram.
1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So what is 0.02 kilograms in grams?

ask.ifNot: Multiply 0.02 by 1000. The digits slide 3 places to the left, so 0.02 becomes 20.

beats.say: 0.02 times 1000 is 20. So 0.02 kilograms is 20 grams.
Careful: it is not 2 grams. 2 grams would be 0.002 kilograms, with one more 0.
So 37.02 kilograms is 37 kilograms 20 grams.
Split at the point, keep the whole kilograms, and multiply the decimal part by 1000.
How many articles make 0.3 score? An article just means one thing, one item.
First, how many is 1 whole score?

ask.ifNot: A score is 20. A dozen is 12.

beats.say: 1 score is 20. So 0.3 score is 0.3 times 20.
0.3 means 3 tenths. One tenth of 20 is 2.
So 3 tenths of 20 is 3 times 2, which is 6.
So 0.3 score is 6 articles.
0.3 score is less than 1 score, so the answer must be less than 20. Always check the size of your answer.
How many gross make a dozen? That sounds upside down, so let's think carefully.
A gross is 12 dozen. That is 12 times 12, which is 144 things.
Which is bigger: a gross or a dozen?

ask.ifNot: A gross holds 12 dozens inside it. So a gross is much bigger than a dozen.

beats.say: A dozen is smaller than a gross. So a dozen is only a part of a gross. The answer must be a fraction, less than 1.
12 dozens make 1 gross. So 1 dozen is 1 of 12 equal parts of a gross. That is 1 twelfth.
So 1 twelfth of a gross makes a dozen.
Careful with the choices. 12 is how many dozens make a gross, and 144 is how many things. The question asked it the other way round.
We must add 4 kilometres, 40 metres and 400 centimetres, and give the answer in metres.
Three different units. What do we do before adding?

ask.ifNot: We can only add lengths in the same unit. The answer is wanted in metres, so let's change each part into metres.

beats.say: 1 kilometre is 1000 metres. So 4 kilometres is 4000 metres.
The 40 metres are already in metres. They stay as 40.
Now the centimetres. 100 centimetres make 1 metre, so 400 centimetres is 400 divided by 100. Only 4 metres.
Careful there: going to a bigger unit, the number gets smaller. 400 centimetres is not 400 metres.
Now add. 4000 plus 40 plus 4 is 4044.
So the total is 4044 metres.
Let us multiply 81 by 37. Look at the sign first. It is times, so we multiply.
Too big to do in one go. So split 37 into 30 and 7, and do one piece at a time.

spec.note: Split 37 into 30 and 7

beats.say: Start with the tens piece, 30. First, 81 times 3. 80 times 3 is 240, and 1 times 3 is 3. Together that makes 243.
30 is 3 tens. So what is 81 times 30?

ask.ifNot: 30 is ten times 3. So the answer is ten times 243, which is 243 with a 0 on the end.

beats.say: Ten times 243 is 2430. That is the first piece done.
Now the ones piece. 81 times 7. 80 times 7 is 560, and 1 times 7 is 7. Together that makes 567.
Add the two pieces. 2430 plus 567 is 2997.
There it is. 81 times 37 makes 2997.
A quick check on the last digit. 1 times 7 is 7, and our answer ends in 7 too.
So the plan is: split one number into tens and ones, multiply each piece, then add.
Let us take 22 away from 72.
Let us take the 22 away in two easy pieces. Split it into 20 and 2.
Take the tens away first. What is 72 take away 20?

ask.ifNot: Only the tens change. 7 tens take away 2 tens leaves 5 tens, and the 2 ones stay. That is 52.

beats.say: Only the tens change, and the ones stay. So we have 52.
Now take away the 2 ones. 52 take away 2 is 50.
There it is. 72 minus 22 leaves 50.
Check by adding back. 50 plus 22 makes 72, the number we started with.
So the plan is: take away the tens first, then take away the ones.
75 plus 17. Let us work it out together.
Big numbers are friendlier in pieces. So we split each one into its tens and its ones.
Start with the tens. What is 70 plus 10?

ask.ifNot: 7 tens and 1 ten make 8 tens. And 8 tens is 80.

beats.say: 7 tens and 1 ten make 8 tens. That is 80.
Now the ones. 5 plus 7 is 12. That is more than 9, and that is fine. We just add it on.
Last, join the two parts. 80 plus 12 is 92.
So 75 plus 17 equals 92.
A quick check. 92 take away 17 is 75, right where we started. It fits.
Tens with tens, ones with ones, then put them together. That works every time.
We need to change 5 hectometres into decimetres.
Let's go through metres. Hecto means a hundred, so 1 hectometre is 100 metres. 5 hectometres is 500 metres.
Now metres to decimetres. Deci means a tenth. So how many decimetres are in 1 metre?

ask.ifNot: A decimetre is a tenth of a metre. So it takes 10 of them to make 1 whole metre.

beats.say: 1 metre is 10 decimetres. So 500 metres is 500 times 10, which is 5000 decimetres.
So 5 hectometres is 5000 decimetres.
Careful: 500 is in the choices, but that is the metres. We needed one more step down.
Times 100, then times 10. Altogether that is times 1000.
We want to write 800 grams in kilograms.
Is 800 grams more than 1 kilogram, or less?

ask.ifNot: 1 kilogram is a thousand grams. 800 is not quite that many, so it is less than 1 kilogram.

beats.say: 1000 grams make 1 kilogram. 800 is less than 1000, so our answer will start with 0 point something.
To change grams into kilograms we divide by 1000. Each digit slides 3 places to the right.
The 8 lands in the tenths place. 800 divided by 1000 is 0.8.
So 800 grams is 0.8 kilograms.
Check: 0.8 is 8 tenths, and a tenth of a kilogram is 100 grams. 8 of those make 800 grams.
We want to write 80 metres in kilometres.
1000 metres make 1 kilometre. 80 metres is much less than that, so the answer is a small decimal.
To go from metres to kilometres, what do we do?

ask.ifNot: Kilometres are bigger, so we need fewer of them. And 1000 metres make 1 kilometre, so we divide by 1000.

beats.say: 80 divided by 1000. The digits slide 3 places to the right. The 8 lands in the hundredths place.
So 80 metres is 0.08 kilometres.
Careful with the place. 0.8 kilometres would be 800 metres, ten times too far.
Divide by 1000, then check where each digit landed.
We want to write 5 milligrams in grams.
How many milligrams make 1 gram?

ask.ifNot: Milli means a thousandth. So 1000 milligrams make 1 gram.

beats.say: 1000 milligrams make 1 gram. So 1 milligram is 1 thousandth of a gram, and we divide by 1000.
5 divided by 1000. The 5 slides 3 places to the right: past the tenths, past the hundredths, into the thousandths.
We fill the empty places with zeros. 0.005.
So 5 milligrams is 0.005 grams.
Thousandths always need 3 places after the point. 0.5 grams would be 500 milligrams, far too much.
3 metres 7 decimetres. We want it all in centimetres.
Start with the metres. 1 metre is 100 centimetres, so 3 metres is 300 centimetres.
Now the decimetres. How many centimetres are in 1 decimetre?

ask.ifNot: A decimetre is a tenth of a metre. A tenth of 100 centimetres is 10 centimetres.

beats.say: 1 decimetre is 10 centimetres, so 7 decimetres is 70 centimetres.
Careful: 70, not 7. With 7 centimetres we would get 307, and that is in the choices to catch us.
Add the two parts. 300 plus 70 is 370.
So 3 metres 7 decimetres is 370 centimetres.
3 metres 7 centimetres. This time we want decimetres.
A decimetre sits between the metre and the centimetre. 1 metre is 10 decimetres, and 1 decimetre is 10 centimetres.
The metres first. 3 metres is 3 times 10, which is 30 decimetres.
Now 7 centimetres. Is that more than 1 decimetre, or less?

ask.ifNot: It takes 10 centimetres to make 1 decimetre. We only have 7, so it is less than 1.

beats.say: 7 centimetres is 7 tenths of a decimetre. 7 divided by 10 is 0.7.
Add the parts. 30 plus 0.7 is 30.7.
So 3 metres 7 centimetres is 30.7 decimetres.
Bigger unit to smaller: multiply. Smaller unit to bigger: divide. We used both here.
2.5 kilograms. Let's write it as whole kilograms and grams.
Split at the point. 2 whole kilograms, and 0.5 of a kilogram.
0.5 is the same as a half. 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So what is half a kilogram?

ask.ifNot: Half of 1000 is 500. So half a kilogram is 500 grams.

beats.say: 0.5 times 1000 is 500. So 0.5 kilograms is 500 grams.
So 2.5 kilograms is 2 kilograms 500 grams.
Careful: the 5 after the point does not mean 5 grams. It means 5 tenths of a kilogram.
Split at the point, then multiply the decimal part by 1000.
2.05 litres. Let's write it as whole litres and millilitres.
Split at the point. 2 whole litres, and 0.05 of a litre.
1 litre is 1000 millilitres. So we multiply 0.05 by 1000.
Times 1000 slides the digits 3 places to the left. What does 0.05 become?

ask.ifNot: Slide the 5 once, twice, three times. It ends up in the tens place, with a 0 after it. That makes 50.

beats.say: 0.05 times 1000 is 50. So 0.05 litres is 50 millilitres.
So 2.05 litres is 2 litres 50 millilitres.
Watch that 0 after the point. 0.5 litres would be 500 millilitres, but 0.05 is ten times less.
2.05 metres. Let's write it as whole metres and centimetres.
Split at the point. 2 whole metres, and 0.05 of a metre.
Now be careful. How many centimetres make 1 metre?

ask.ifNot: Centi means a hundredth. So 100 centimetres make 1 metre. The 1000 is for millimetres.

beats.say: 1 metre is 100 centimetres. So we multiply 0.05 by 100, and the digits slide 2 places to the left.
So 0.05 metres is 5 centimetres.
And 2.05 metres is 2 metres 5 centimetres.
With metres and centimetres it is times 100, not times 1000. Know your unit before you multiply.
We want to write 30 kilograms in tonnes. A tonne is a very heavy weight, about as heavy as a small car.
How many kilograms make 1 tonne?

ask.ifNot: A tonne is a thousand kilograms.

beats.say: 1000 kilograms make 1 tonne. 30 kilograms is tiny next to that, so the answer is a small decimal.
We divide by 1000. The digits slide 3 places to the right, so the 3 lands in the hundredths place.
So 30 kilograms is 0.03 tonnes.
Check the place. 0.3 tonnes would be 300 kilograms, and 0.003 tonnes would be only 3 kilograms.
Divide by 1000, then check where the digits landed.
We want to write 240 paise in rupees.
How many paise make 1 rupee?

ask.ifNot: One rupee is 100 paise.

beats.say: 100 paise make 1 rupee. So 200 paise make 2 rupees.
Take those 200 paise out of the 240. 40 paise are left over.
So we have 2 rupees and 40 paise. How is that written in rupees?

ask.ifNot: The rupees go before the point, and the paise go after it, in two places. 40 paise is point four zero.

beats.say: 2 rupees and 40 paise is written 2.40.
That is the same as dividing 240 by 100: the digits move two places to the right.
To change paise into rupees, divide by 100. The rupees are much bigger than paise, so the number gets smaller.
We want to write 4.06 rupees in paise.
How many paise are there in 1 rupee?

ask.ifNot: One rupee is 100 paise.

beats.say: So the 4 whole rupees are 4 lots of 100 paise. That is 400 paise.
Now look after the point: zero six. How many paise is that?

ask.ifNot: The two digits after the point show the paise. Zero six means just 6. For 60 paise it would say six zero.

beats.say: That is the part to watch. It is 6 paise, not 60. The zero is holding the tenths place.
400 paise and 6 paise make 406 paise.
That is the same as multiplying 4.06 by 100: the digits move two places to the left.
To change rupees into paise, multiply by 100. Paise are small, so there are many more of them.
A shopkeeper has 5.4 kilograms of rice. He sells 2 kilograms 750 grams. How much rice is left?
One weight is a decimal, and the other is in kilograms and grams. What is the easiest plan?

ask.ifNot: Mixed forms are hard to subtract. If both weights are in grams, it is one simple subtraction.

beats.say: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. So 5.4 kilograms is 5.4 times 1000, which is 5400 grams.
And 2 kilograms 750 grams is 2000 plus 750, which is 2750 grams.
Now subtract. 5400 minus 2000 is 3400. Then take away the 750: 3400 minus 700 is 2700, and 50 less is 2650.
2650 grams is 2 kilograms and 650 grams. That is how much rice is left.
Check: 2650 plus 2750 is 5400. It works.
The trap is to take 400 from 750 because it looks easier. The 750 is being sold, so it is the one we take away.
A box has 3 gross of pencils, and 5 dozen are given away. The answer must be in pencils, so we change everything into pencils first.

board.text: 3 gross of pencils.   5 dozen given away.

beats.say: One gross is 12 dozen. And one dozen is 12. So how many pencils are in one gross?

ask.ifNot: 12 dozen means 12 lots of 12. And 12 times 12 is 144.

beats.say: 12 times 12 is 144. So one gross is 144 pencils.
3 gross is 3 times 144. 3 times 100 is 300, 3 times 40 is 120, and 3 times 4 is 12. Together, 432 pencils.
Now the pencils given away. 5 dozen is 5 times 12, which is 60.
The box had 432 pencils, and 60 are given away. What now?

ask.ifNot: Given away means they leave the box. So take 60 away from 432.

beats.say: 432 take away 60 is 372. So 372 pencils are left.
The trap is mixing units. Gross, dozen and pencils are different sizes, so change everything into pencils before you subtract.
The letter a is standing in for a number. We are told that a is 3. We want the value of a plus 4.
What do we do with the letter a?

ask.ifNot: a is just a name tag for the number 3. So wherever we see a, we take it out and put 3 in its place.

beats.say: Rub out the a and put 3 in its place. Now it says 3 plus 4.
The sign between them is a plus. So what do we do with the 3 and the 4?

ask.ifNot: The plus sign is still there, and it tells us to add. We do not just write the two digits next to each other.

beats.say: 3 plus 4 is 7.
So when a is 3, a plus 4 is 7. Swap the letter for its number, then do what the sign says.
We are told that a is 6 and b is 7. We want to know what 3 a minus b is worth.
Look at 3 a. The 3 and the a are side by side. When a is 6, what does that mean?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 3 a means 3 times a. Here that is 3 times 6.

beats.say: So swap each letter for its number. 3 a becomes 3 times 6, and b becomes 7.
Two jobs here: a times and a take away. Which one goes first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding and taking away. So 3 times 6 comes first.

beats.say: 3 lots of 6 make 18.
The sign before b is a minus, so b comes off. 18 minus 7 leaves 11.
That gives 11. Remember: a number next to a letter means times, and the times is done first.
Here a is 9 and b is 5. Let's find what 3 a minus b comes to.
Before we swap anything: when a is 9, what is 3 a?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 3 a means 3 times a. Here that is 3 times 9.

beats.say: Now put the numbers in. 3 a is 3 times 9. And in place of b we write 5.
Two jobs here: a times and a take away. Which one goes first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding and taking away. So 3 times 9 comes first.

beats.say: 3 times 9 is 27.
The sign before b is a minus, so b comes off. 27 minus 5 leaves 22.
So 3 a minus b is worth 22. The plan: swap the letters for their numbers, do the times first, then the taking away.
Here a is 9 and b is 2. Let's find what a plus 4 b comes to.
Before we swap anything: when b is 2, what is 4 b?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 4 b means 4 times b. Here that is 4 times 2.

beats.say: So swap each letter for its number. a becomes 9, and 4 b becomes 4 times 2.
Careful now. The plus comes first as we read, but that does not mean it is done first. Which job do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding, even when the plus is written first. The 4 belongs to b, so 4 times 2 comes first.

beats.say: 4 times 2 is 8.
Now add a, which is 9. We add it just once. 9 plus 8 is 17.
That gives 17. Remember: a number next to a letter means times, and the times is done before the plus.
Two letters here. a stands for 10 and b stands for 3. Our job is to find the value of 2 a plus b.
First, what does 2 a turn into when a is 10?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 2 a means 2 times a. Here that is 2 times 10.

beats.say: Now put the numbers in. 2 a is 2 times 10. And in place of b we write 3.
Two jobs here: a times and a plus. Which one goes first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding and taking away. So 2 times 10 comes first.

beats.say: 2 times 10 is 20.
We are not done yet: b still has to be added. 20 plus 3 makes 23.
So 2 a plus b is worth 23. The plan: swap the letters for their numbers, do the times first, then the adding.
a is 3. We want the value of 4 a. Look: the 4 and the a are side by side, with no sign between them.
There is a hidden sign between the 4 and the a. Which one is it?

ask.ifNot: In algebra, a number right next to a letter means multiply. So 4 a means 4 times a. It is 4 lots of a.

beats.say: 4 a means 4 times a. I'll write the hidden sign in.
Now swap the a for 3. We get 4 times 3.
4 times 3 is 12.
Watch out for two slips. 4 plus 3 is 7, but nothing here says add. And 4 a is not the digits 4 and 3 written side by side.
A number next to a letter always means times. So 4 a is 4 times 3, which is 12.
We are told that a is 10 and b is 5. We want to know what 3 a minus b is worth.
First, what does 3 a turn into when a is 10?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 3 a means 3 times a. Here that is 3 times 10.

beats.say: So swap each letter for its number. 3 a becomes 3 times 10, and b becomes 5.
Two jobs here: a times and a take away. Which one goes first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding and taking away. So 3 times 10 comes first.

beats.say: 3 times 10 is 30.
Now take away b, which is 5. We take it away just once. 30 minus 5 is 25.
So 3 a minus b is worth 25. The plan: swap the letters for their numbers, do the times first, then the taking away.
Here a is 3 and b is 9. We need a squared. That is the a with a small 2 up above it.
That small 2 has a special job. What does a squared mean?

ask.ifNot: The small 2 is not a number to add or to multiply by. It says: use a two times over, multiplied together. So a squared is a times a.

beats.say: a squared is a times a. It is a short way to write a number times itself.
We were also told that b is 9. Do we need b here?

choices: No, there is no b in a²
ask.ifNot: Look at what we are asked for: a squared. There is no b in it at all. So b is extra, and we leave it alone.

beats.say: Only a matters. Put 3 in place of each a, and we get 3 times 3.
3 times 3 is 9. So a squared is 9.
So squared means the number times itself, never times 2. And we only use the letters that are asked for. The answer is 9.
We are told that a is 10 and b is 8. We want to know what 3 a minus b is worth.
Look at 3 a. The 3 and the a are side by side. When a is 10, what does that mean?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 3 a means 3 times a. Here that is 3 times 10.

beats.say: Now put the numbers in. 3 a is 3 times 10. And in place of b we write 8.
Two jobs here: a times and a take away. Which one goes first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding and taking away. So 3 times 10 comes first.

beats.say: 3 lots of 10 make 30.
Now take away b, which is 8. We take it away just once. 30 minus 8 is 22.
So 3 a minus b is worth 22. The plan: swap the letters for their numbers, do the times first, then the taking away.
a is 3. We want 2 a over 3. The sloping line means divided by. So this is 2 a, divided by 3.
What do we work out first?

ask.ifNot: The whole of 2 a is being divided by 3. So we need to know what 2 a is before we can divide it.

beats.say: 2 a means 2 times a. And a is 3, so 2 a is 2 times 3, which is 6.
Are we finished at 6?

ask.ifNot: 6 is only the top part, 2 a. The expression still says divided by 3. So there is one more step.

beats.say: Now divide by 3. 6 divided by 3 is 2.
So 2 a over 3 is 2. Work out the top first, then divide by the bottom.
Here a is 4 and b is 6. Let's find what 3 a minus b comes to.
Before we swap anything: when a is 4, what is 3 a?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 3 a means 3 times a. Here that is 3 times 4.

beats.say: So swap each letter for its number. 3 a becomes 3 times 4, and b becomes 6.
Two jobs here: a times and a take away. Which one goes first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding and taking away. So 3 times 4 comes first.

beats.say: 3 times 4 is 12.
Now take away b, which is 6. We take it away just once. 12 minus 6 is 6.
That gives 6. Remember: a number next to a letter means times, and the times is done first.
We are told that a is 9 and b is 10. We want to know what 2 a plus b is worth.
Look at 2 a. The 2 and the a are side by side. When a is 9, what does that mean?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 2 a means 2 times a. Here that is 2 times 9.

beats.say: So swap each letter for its number. 2 a becomes 2 times 9, and b becomes 10.
Two jobs here: a times and a plus. Which one goes first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding and taking away. So 2 times 9 comes first.

beats.say: 2 lots of 9 make 18.
We are not done yet: b still has to be added. 18 plus 10 makes 28.
So 2 a plus b is worth 28. The plan: swap the letters for their numbers, do the times first, then the adding.
We are told that a is 5 and b is 4. We want to know what 2 a plus b is worth.
First, what does 2 a turn into when a is 5?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 2 a means 2 times a. Here that is 2 times 5.

beats.say: So swap each letter for its number. 2 a becomes 2 times 5, and b becomes 4.
Two jobs here: a times and a plus. Which one goes first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding and taking away. So 2 times 5 comes first.

beats.say: 2 times 5 is 10.
We are not done yet: b still has to be added. 10 plus 4 makes 14.
That gives 14. Remember: a number next to a letter means times, and the times is done first.
Two letters here. a stands for 9 and b stands for 7. Our job is to find the value of a plus 4 b.
Look at 4 b. The 4 and the b are side by side. When b is 7, what does that mean?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 4 b means 4 times b. Here that is 4 times 7.

beats.say: So swap each letter for its number. a becomes 9, and 4 b becomes 4 times 7.
Careful now. The plus comes first as we read, but that does not mean it is done first. Which job do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding, even when the plus is written first. The 4 belongs to b, so 4 times 7 comes first.

beats.say: 4 times 7 is 28.
Now add a, which is 9. We add it just once. 9 plus 28 is 37.
That gives 37. Remember: a number next to a letter means times, and the times is done before the plus.
a is 3. We want a plus 12, in a bracket, all divided by 3.
What does the bracket tell us to do first?

ask.ifNot: A bracket is a parcel. Whatever is inside gets done first. So we add a and 12 before any dividing.

beats.say: Inside the bracket: a plus 12. a is 3, so that is 3 plus 12, which is 15.
Now the whole 15 is divided by 3. Not just the a, and not just the 12. The whole parcel.
15 divided by 3 is 5.
If we divided only the a by 3, we would get 1, and then 1 plus 12 is 13. That is a different sum, because it ignores the bracket.
Bracket first, then divide the whole result. So the value is 5.
We are told that a is 9 and b is 9. We want the value of a b. Two letters, side by side.
There is no sign between the a and the b. So what does a b mean?

ask.ifNot: When two letters stand side by side, there is a hidden times sign between them. So a b means a times b.

beats.say: So a b is a times b. I'll write the hidden times sign in.
Now swap each letter for its number. a is 9 and b is 9, so we get 9 times 9.
9 times 9 is 81. So a b is worth 81.
Watch out for the classic slip: adding. 9 plus 9 is 18, but that is a plus b, a different thing.
So remember: letters side by side mean times. a b is a times b, and here that is 81.
We are told that a is 8 and b is 7. We want the value of a squared. See the small 2 sitting up high?
That small 2 has a special job. What does a squared mean?

ask.ifNot: The small 2 is not a number to add or to multiply by. It says: use a two times over, multiplied together. So a squared is a times a.

beats.say: So a squared means a times a. The letter is multiplied by itself.
We were also told that b is 7. Do we need b here?

choices: No, there is no b in a²
ask.ifNot: Look at what we are asked for: a squared. There is no b in it at all. So b is extra, and we leave it alone.

beats.say: Only a matters. Put 8 in place of each a, and we get 8 times 8.
8 times 8 is 64. So a squared is 64.
Remember: a squared is a times a. And a number we are given but do not need can be left alone. That gives 64.
We are told that a is 4 and b is 4. We want to know what 2 a plus b is worth.
Look at 2 a. The 2 and the a are side by side. When a is 4, what does that mean?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 2 a means 2 times a. Here that is 2 times 4.

beats.say: Now put the numbers in. 2 a is 2 times 4. And in place of b we write 4.
Two jobs here: a times and a plus. Which one goes first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding and taking away. So 2 times 4 comes first.

beats.say: 2 times 4 is 8.
Now add b, which is 4. 8 plus 4 is 12.
So 2 a plus b is worth 12. The plan: swap the letters for their numbers, do the times first, then the adding.
a is 3. We want a squared. That is the a with a small 2 sitting up high.
What does the small 2 tell us to do?

ask.ifNot: The small 2 is not an ordinary number. It says: use a two times, multiplied together. So a squared is a times a.

beats.say: a squared means a times a.
Swap each a for 3. That gives 3 times 3.
3 times 3 is 9.
Here is the most common slip: doing 3 times 2 and getting 6. Squared never means times 2.
Squared means the number times itself. So a squared is 3 times 3, which is 9.
We are told that a is 3 and b is 2. We want to know what 3 a minus b is worth.
Before we swap anything: when a is 3, what is 3 a?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 3 a means 3 times a. Here that is 3 times 3.

beats.say: Now put the numbers in. 3 a is 3 times 3. And in place of b we write 2.
Two jobs here: a times and a take away. Which one goes first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding and taking away. So 3 times 3 comes first.

beats.say: 3 lots of 3 make 9.
Now take away b, which is 2. We take it away just once. 9 minus 2 is 7.
So 3 a minus b is worth 7. The plan: swap the letters for their numbers, do the times first, then the taking away.
We are told that a is 4 and b is 7. We want the value of a b. Two letters, side by side.
There is no sign between the a and the b. So what does a b mean?

ask.ifNot: When two letters stand side by side, there is a hidden times sign between them. So a b means a times b.

beats.say: So a b is a times b. I'll write the hidden times sign in.
Now swap each letter for its number. a is 4 and b is 7, so we get 4 times 7.
4 times 7 is 28. So a b is worth 28.
Watch out for the classic slip: adding. 4 plus 7 is 11, but that is a plus b, a different thing.
So remember: letters side by side mean times. a b is a times b, and here that is 28.
We are told that a is 3 and b is 2. We want to know what 2 a plus b is worth.
First, what does 2 a turn into when a is 3?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 2 a means 2 times a. Here that is 2 times 3.

beats.say: So swap each letter for its number. 2 a becomes 2 times 3, and b becomes 2.
Two jobs here: a times and a plus. Which one goes first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding and taking away. So 2 times 3 comes first.

beats.say: 2 lots of 3 make 6.
We are not done yet: b still has to be added. 6 plus 2 makes 8.
So 2 a plus b is worth 8. The plan: swap the letters for their numbers, do the times first, then the adding.
a is 3. We want 4 a squared. There is a 4, an a, and a small 2 up high.
Who does the small 2 belong to?

ask.ifNot: The small 2 sits on the a, so it belongs to the a alone. The 4 is not squared.

beats.say: So we square the a first. a squared is a times a. That is 3 times 3, which is 9.
Now, what do we do with the 4?

ask.ifNot: 4 a squared means 4 times a squared. A number next to a letter always means times. So it is 4 times 9.

beats.say: 4 times 9 is 36.
The trap is to do 4 times 3 first, and then square the 12. That gives a much bigger number, because it squares the 4 as well.
Squares come first, then the times. So 4 a squared is 4 times 9, which is 36.
Here a is 2 and b is 2. We need to find a b: the a and the b written right next to each other.
There is no sign between the a and the b. So what does a b mean?

ask.ifNot: When two letters stand side by side, there is a hidden times sign between them. So a b means a times b.

beats.say: So a b is a times b. I'll write the hidden times sign in.
Put the numbers in place of the letters. That makes it 2 times 2.
2 times 2 is 4. So a b is worth 4.
A funny thing: 2 plus 2 is also 4. That is just luck with these numbers. Letters side by side always mean times.
The plan: read a b as a times b, put the numbers in, and multiply. That gives 4.
Two letters here. a stands for 3 and b stands for 3. Our job is to find the value of a plus 4 b.
Before we swap anything: when b is 3, what is 4 b?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 4 b means 4 times b. Here that is 4 times 3.

beats.say: So swap each letter for its number. a becomes 3, and 4 b becomes 4 times 3.
Careful now. The plus comes first as we read, but that does not mean it is done first. Which job do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding, even when the plus is written first. The 4 belongs to b, so 4 times 3 comes first.

beats.say: 4 times 3 is 12.
Now the plus. 3 plus 12 makes 15.
So a plus 4 b is worth 15. The plan: swap the letters for their numbers, do the times first, then add.
a is 3 and b is 5. We want 4 a b. A number and two letters, all side by side.
What does 4 a b mean?

ask.ifNot: When things stand side by side with no sign, they are all multiplied. So 4 a b is 4 times a times b.

beats.say: So 4 a b means 4 times a times b. Nothing is added.
Swap a for 3 and b for 5. We get 4 times 3 times 5.
Multiply two at a time. 4 times 3 is 12. That 12 is only 4 a. We still have to multiply by b.
So now 12 times 5. What is that?

ask.ifNot: Think of 12 as 10 and 2. Multiply each of them by 5, then add the two answers.

beats.say: 10 times 5 is 50, and 2 times 5 is 10. 50 plus 10 is 60.
So 4 a b is 60. Side by side means times, for every number and letter in the row.
Here a is 6 and b is 9. Let's find what a plus 4 b comes to.
Before we swap anything: when b is 9, what is 4 b?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 4 b means 4 times b. Here that is 4 times 9.

beats.say: So swap each letter for its number. a becomes 6, and 4 b becomes 4 times 9.
Careful now. The plus comes first as we read, but that does not mean it is done first. Which job do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding, even when the plus is written first. The 4 belongs to b, so 4 times 9 comes first.

beats.say: 4 times 9 is 36.
Now add a, which is 6. We add it just once. 6 plus 36 is 42.
So a plus 4 b is worth 42. The plan: swap the letters for their numbers, do the times first, then add.
a is 3 and b is 5. We want the value of 4 a plus b.
What does 4 a mean here?

ask.ifNot: 4 a is 4 times a. And a is 3, not 5. Each letter has its own number. So 4 a is 4 times 3.

beats.say: Swap the letters for their numbers. 4 a becomes 4 times 3. And b becomes 5.
Times goes before plus. 4 times 3 is 12.
Is 12 the answer?

ask.ifNot: 12 is only 4 a. The expression says plus b, and b is 5. So we add 5.

beats.say: 12 plus 5 is 17.
So 4 a plus b is 17. Swap the letters, do the times first, and do not forget the part that is added.
Here a is 2 and b is 2. We need a squared. That is the a with a small 2 up above it.
That small 2 has a special job. What does a squared mean?

ask.ifNot: The small 2 is not a number to add or to multiply by. It says: use a two times over, multiplied together. So a squared is a times a.

beats.say: a squared is a times a. It is a short way to write a number times itself.
We were also told that b is 2. Do we need b here?

choices: No, there is no b in a²
ask.ifNot: Look at what we are asked for: a squared. There is no b in it at all. So b is extra, and we leave it alone.

beats.say: So we only swap a for 2. a times a becomes 2 times 2.
2 times 2 is 4. So a squared is 4.
With 2 it looks the same as doubling, but that is just luck. Squared always means the number times itself. The answer is 4.
We are told that a is 2 and b is 6. We want to know what a plus 4 b is worth.
Before we swap anything: when b is 6, what is 4 b?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 4 b means 4 times b. Here that is 4 times 6.

beats.say: So swap each letter for its number. a becomes 2, and 4 b becomes 4 times 6.
Careful now. The plus comes first as we read, but that does not mean it is done first. Which job do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding, even when the plus is written first. The 4 belongs to b, so 4 times 6 comes first.

beats.say: 4 times 6 is 24.
Now add a, which is 2. We add it just once. 2 plus 24 is 26.
So a plus 4 b is worth 26. The plan: swap the letters for their numbers, do the times first, then add.
a is 3 and b is 5. We want 6 b minus 4 a. Notice that b comes first this time.
First part: 6 b. That is 6 times b, and b is 5. 6 times 5 is 30.
Second part: 4 a. Which sum is that?

ask.ifNot: 4 a is 4 times a. And a is 3. Each letter keeps its own number.

beats.say: 4 times 3 is 12.
Now we have 30 and 12. What does the sign between the two parts tell us?

ask.ifNot: The sign between 6 b and 4 a is a minus. So the second part is taken away from the first.

beats.say: 30 minus 12 is 18.
Work out each part with its own letter first, and only then subtract. The trap is to do 6 minus 4 first: that mixes up the two letters.
Here a is 9 and b is 3. Let's find what a plus 4 b comes to.
Before we swap anything: when b is 3, what is 4 b?

ask.ifNot: When a number sits right next to a letter, there is a hidden times sign between them. So 4 b means 4 times b. Here that is 4 times 3.

beats.say: So swap each letter for its number. a becomes 9, and 4 b becomes 4 times 3.
Careful now. The plus comes first as we read, but that does not mean it is done first. Which job do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Multiplying goes before adding, even when the plus is written first. The 4 belongs to b, so 4 times 3 comes first.

beats.say: 4 times 3 is 12.
Now add a, which is 9. We add it just once. 9 plus 12 is 21.
So a plus 4 b is worth 21. The plan: swap the letters for their numbers, do the times first, then add.
a is 3 and b is 5. We want 12, minus 5 a, plus 3 b.
Work out the letter parts first. 5 a is 5 times 3, which is 15. 3 b is 3 times 5, which is 15 too.
Put them back, each with the sign in front of it. 12, minus 15, plus 15.
Look at the signs. Which part is taken away, and which is added?

ask.ifNot: Each part keeps the sign in front of it. There is a minus in front of 5 a, and a plus in front of 3 b.

beats.say: 12 minus 15 looks hard, because 15 is bigger than 12. But look closer. We take 15 away, and then we put 15 straight back.
Taking 15 away and then adding 15. What does that do to the 12?

ask.ifNot: Taking something away and then putting the same amount back leaves you where you started. The two 15s undo each other.

beats.say: The minus 15 and the plus 15 cancel each other. We are left with 12.
So the value is 12. Keep each sign with its own part. And when the same number is taken away and added, the two cancel.
Our angle is 51 degrees, and we want its complementary partner. The two angles fit snugly into one square corner, like this.

ask.ifNot: Look at the drawing. The two angles fit inside a square corner, and a square corner is a quarter turn. That makes 90 degrees. 180 is for a straight line.

beats.say: A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a book or a door. Turning through it is a quarter turn. So how much do our two angles make together?
A right angle is a quarter turn, and a quarter turn is 90 degrees. So 51, plus our missing angle, makes 90.

ask.ifNot: When we know the whole and one part, we take the part away from the whole. So it is 90 take away 51.

beats.say: The whole is 90 and one piece is 51. Which sum finds the missing piece?
Let's take 51 away in two easy hops. First the 50: 90 take away 50 leaves 40.
Now the 1 that is left: 40 take away 1 leaves 39. So 90 minus 51 is 39.
So the complement is 39 degrees. Watch it go into the drawing.
